stories.title: 5 killed after being run over by train in Prayagraj:Were standing below after getting down from coach; hit by 2 trains
stories.summary: In Prayagraj, 5 people died after being hit by a train around 7:30 PM on Wednesday evening. Upon receiving information, police and railway teams reached the spot and took possession of the bodies, sending them for post-mortem. According to the police, efforts are being made to identify the deceased. The accident occurred at Pachdeora Halt in the Karchhana area. Passengers had got down from the train at a halt station Akash (19), son of Giriraj and a resident of Prithvipur village under Khairgarh police station in Firozabad, was travelling to attend a wedding at a relative’s house in Kolkata. Ajay, son of Munna Pasi and a resident of Kolkata, was also with him. Near Pachdevara, a man fell from the same train, after which the emergency chain was pulled and the train stopped. All the passengers got down to relieve themselves. At that moment, the Kalka Mail sounded its horn and people started moving back towards the train. Meanwhile, the Purushottam Express, coming from the Mirzapur side, hit five people, killing all of them. Two of the deceased have been identified as Akash Kumar from Firozabad and Sunil Kumar from Mirzapur. Three bodies remain unidentified. As soon as the information was received, the Karchana police, ACP Sunil Kumar Singh, GRP and railway officials reached the spot. See 3 pictures Passengers had alighted from the train at Halt station A train stopped for a while near Pachdeora Halt. A passenger got down and went to the other track to use the toilet. Just then, the Kalka Mail arrived, and the young man died on the spot after being hit by it. Seeing this incident, passengers on the train raised an alarm. The deceased's family members got down in a panic, and then another train also arrived, and all three were hit by it. They also died on the spot in this accident. After the incident, another person is reported missing. It is suspected that he was also hit by the train, although this has not been officially confirmed yet. Upon receiving the information, police from Karchhana police station, ACP Sunil Kumar Singh, GRP, and railway officials reached the spot.

stories.title: UP to have 120 Lok Sabha seats in next election:Currently 80 seats; change after Delimitation Commission is formed
stories.summary: The special session of Parliament in New Delhi is starting tomorrow (Thursday). The government is going to form a Delimitation Commission and introduce the 131st Constitution Amendment Bill. If both these bills are passed by a two-thirds majority in the House, then the picture of UP regarding the 2029 Lok Sabha elections will also become clear. UP's seats in the Lok Sabha can be increased from 80 to 120. Meanwhile, the Assembly seats can increase from 403 to 550-600. The number of Lok Sabha seats in UP has been increased from time to time based on the recommendations of the Delimitation Commission. What is the 131st Constitution Amendment? The Constitution Amendment Bill proposes to increase the Lok Sabha seats from 543 to 850. Of these, a maximum of 815 seats will be for states and 35 for Union Territories. A Delimitation Commission will be formed to determine the number of seats. The commission will also decide how many seats each state will have. According to sources, the 2011 census will be considered the basis for the new delimitation. The distribution of seats will be determined based on population. In 2011, Uttar Pradesh's population was 16% of the country's total population. In this regard, if the Lok Sabha has 835 seats for states, then based on population, UP's seats could increase from 80 to 120-130. 40 seats will be reserved for women If the Lok Sabha seats in UP reach 120 after the new delimitation, then 33% of those seats will be reserved for women. This means only women MPs will be elected on 40 seats. This will also give an opportunity to women workers of political parties to go to Parliament. Assembly Seats Will Increase to 600 Experts believe that the current number of UP Assembly seats is based on the 1971 census. The population has increased significantly in the last 55 years. In 2026, the estimated population of UP has been assessed at 24.82 crore. In five and a half decades, migration from villages to cities has also been very high. The number of cities has increased. In UP, on average, there are more than 4 lakh voters in one assembly constituency. However, in the recently conducted Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the voter list, the number of voters has decreased. Still, the number of voters in UP's assembly constituencies is higher than in other states. If the formula of increasing seats according to population and reducing the burden of voters in existing assembly constituencies is implemented, the assembly seats here will increase to 550 to 600. Among these, 33% of seats (from 181 to 198) will be reserved for women. Assembly election seats could increase from 2032 In 2027, the assembly elections will be held on 403 seats only, but in the 2032 assembly elections, the number of seats will increase. Experts believe that if One Nation-One Election is implemented, the assembly seats in UP will increase even before 2032. Currently 12% Women MLAs in the Assembly Currently, there are 51 women MLAs in the UP Assembly compared to 403 seats. Among these, there are 30 from BJP, 15 from Samajwadi Party, 4 from Apna Dal (S), one from RLD, and one woman MLA from Congress. Assembly constituencies will be within the ambit of a single Lok Sabha constituency After the new delimitation, a major problem of political parties will be resolved. There are many Lok Sabha constituencies in UP whose assembly constituencies are within the boundaries of more than one district. In the new delimitation, it will be ensured that all assembly constituencies under a Lok Sabha constituency are within the boundaries of a single district. An assembly constituency will also not be divided between two Lok Sabha constituencies.

stories.summary: A massive fire broke out in the Vikasnagar area of Lucknow on Wednesday evening around 5:30 pm, destroying over 50 slum huts and triggering explosions of more than 30 LPG cylinders. The flames were so intense that they were visible from nearly 10 kilometres away. As the fire spread rapidly, around 20 nearby houses were evacuated as a precaution. Fire brought under control after 3 hours Around 20 fire brigade vehicles were deployed to control the blaze, which was finally brought under control after nearly three hours. Electricity supply in the area was cut off during the firefighting operation to prevent further hazards. A local resident claimed that his four children were burnt alive in the fire, though official confirmation is awaited. Several families lost all their belongings as their huts were reduced to ashes. Those affected were seen wailing in distress as they watched their homes burn down. Allegations of deliberate fire Some residents alleged that the fire may have been deliberately set, though authorities have not confirmed this. An investigation into the cause of the fire is underway. CM orders swift action Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath took cognisance of the incident and directed officials to immediately reach the spot and oversee relief efforts. Deputy Chief Minister Brajesh Pathak also visited the site and instructed authorities to expedite rescue and relief operations.

stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:DMs, SSPs in 25 UP districts are women; SC continues hearing in Sabarimala women entry case on Day 4 more
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. Sabarimala women entry case hearing on Day 4: Adv Singhvi says court can’t rule on religious beliefs A hearing is underway in the Supreme Court of India concerning the entry of women into the Sabarimala Temple. 2. Parents plan to sell their newborn fails: Grandmother rescues child; mother had struck a deal with a businessman for 2.5 lakhs In Agra, a mother made a deal to sell her two-day-old newborn baby. The price of the baby was fixed at Rs 2.5 lakh. A businessman even reached the hospital to take the baby, but the grandmother and aunt got wind of it. 3. Woman remains unidentified 5 days after her dead body recovery: Post-mortem report shows 17 injury marks The post-mortem report of the unidentified woman's body found by the roadside in the Kakori area has arrived. The report shows two severe injury marks on the front and back of the woman's head, while about 15 injuries were found on other parts of the body. 4. 'Har ghar bhagwa chhaega, Ram Rajya aaega', says BJP's Suvendu Adhikari Suvendu Adhikari, Leader of the Opposition in West Bengal and BJP candidate from Nandigram and Bhabanipur, said that “the public is ready”. He raised a slogan while campaigning, ‘Har ghar bhagwa chhaega, Ram Rajya aaega’. 5. Women DMs, SSPs in 25 UP districts:33% posting plan before 2027 polls Efforts are underway in Uttar Pradesh to increase women’s participation in governance, with the first impact likely to be seen in district-level administration. 6. 4-year-old girl shows no fear of water: Swims 900 metres across the Yamuna River in 21 minutes In Prayagraj district of Uttar Pradesh, 4-year-old Satya Bharti from the Mahewa West area has achieved a feat that even seasoned swimmers often find challenging. She swam across the Yamuna river in just 21 minutes and 28 seconds. 7. Dalal Street cheers Modi-Trump call over Hormuz Strait trade Following the conversation between US President Donald Trump and his India counterpart PM Modi, the Indian benchmark indices advanced in early deals on Wednesday, 15 April, 2026. Sensex soared 1,300 points at opening. 8. Misleading video sparks FIR on 2 RJD women spokespersons After two days of unrest, factories in Noida reopened on Wednesday, with the situation returning to normal. Heavy security has been deployed, with surveillance through CCTV cameras and drones. 9. 3 years after Atiq’s killing, wife Shaista is still missing:2 other family members are absconding Three years on, the UP Police has failed to trace Atiq Ahmed’s wife, Shaista Parveen. Raids were conducted across nine states, with support from ATS and RAF teams, but she remains untraceable. 10. India's wholesale inflation rises for the 5th month in a row to 3.88% Wholesale prices of goods in India have gone up again in March 2025, increasing by 3.88%, the government data showed. This marks the fifth month in a row that prices have climbed.

stories.title: Woman climbs water tank for boyfriend, threatens to end life:Family conducts garland ceremony in Gorakhpur; wedding was fixed elsewhere on April 21
stories.summary: In Gorakhpur, an 18-year-old girl climbed a 70-foot-high water tank on Tuesday evening, demanding to marry her boyfriend and threatening to end her life. She shouted from the top, asking people to call her boyfriend and warned that she would kill herself if anyone tried to stop her. Soon, a large crowd gathered at the spot and tried to convince her to come down, but she refused. Police also reached the scene after getting information, but their efforts failed to calm her. After nearly two hours, her boyfriend was brought there and both families agreed to the marriage. Only then did the girl come down safely. Later, the couple exchanged garlands and got married on the spot. After the ceremony, the girl was sent to the boy’s house. The incident took place in Mahavir Chhapra village under Belipar police station area. The couple had been in a relationship for four years, but the girl’s family had fixed her marriage elsewhere, scheduled for April 21. Met during college studies The girl said - she was studying intermediate, and during that time, she met a young man (19) from the same village. In 2022, we first became friends, and then gradually fell in love with each other. We have been in a relationship for four years. My family was not ready for the marriage. They fixed my marriage with another boy. The wedding procession was due to arrive on April 21st. I refused the marriage, but my family did not agree. They also stopped me from leaving the house. I tried to convince my parents, but they didn't agree. On April 14, Tuesday, at 3 PM, I reached near the water tank of the Jal Jeevan Mission located in Jotbagahi village. I thought that if my family didn't agree today, I would jump and end my life. People bowed to the girl's stubbornness, pressured the family to agree Villagers said that many attempts were made to get the girl down, but she did not agree. The police also tried to explain. Seeing her stubbornness, we talked to her family. Both families were called. The police spoke to both families and then they agreed to the marriage. After the family agreed, the girl was brought down. The varmala ceremony was arranged right there. And the two were married in front of everyone. After this, the girl was sent with the boy. After the marriage, the young woman was sent with her husband SP South Dinesh Puri said - The young woman was safely brought down. She was handed over to her family. Then, on the spot, both families were talked to and consent for the marriage was obtained. After this, the young woman was married. After the varmala ceremony, the girl was sent with her boy.

stories.title: Big setback for Baahubali Dhananjay, Abhay Singh acquitted:Varanasi court verdict in 24-year-old Taksal case, firing allegation involved
stories.summary: Strongman Dhananjay Singh has suffered a setback in the 24-year-old Taksal Cinema incident of Varanasi. The MP-MLA Court on Wednesday acquitted all 6 accused, including Abhay Singh and Mirzapur MLC Vineet Singh. Dhananjay had alleged that Abhay and Vineet Singh, along with 4-5 associates, had indiscriminately fired upon his convoy. In this, he, his gunner, and driver were injured. On April 13, Special Judge (MP-MLA Court) Yajuvendra Vikram Singh had reserved the verdict. Security was beefed up in and around the court premises in view of the verdict. More than 350 policemen, including 2 IPS officers and 3 ACPs, were deployed. One company of PAC (Provincial Armed Constabulary) was also called. Meanwhile, on Tuesday night, before the judgment, Dhananjay Singh bowed his head at Baba Vishwanath Temple and performed Rudrabhishek. He also offered prayers at the Kalbhairav Temple. He had said - 'We will definitely get justice.' Know the full story 1- Abhay got Dhananjay a hostel by calling him his maternal aunt's son According to Abhay Singh, Dhananjay Singh, who graduated from Karra College in Jaunpur in 1992, was first introduced by Dharmendra Singh, the president of Tilakdhari Singh College. It was the day of Dussehra. It was then that he said Dhananjay was also going to Lucknow to study, and asked to help him. According to Abhay Singh, Dhananjay's admission was arranged by his close friend Piyush Singh. Piyush was also studying at Lucknow University. However, Dhananjay Singh has himself narrated the story of his admission. According to him, admission was then through an entrance exam. He had passed the entrance test in both Prayagraj and Lucknow universities, but he decided to take admission in Lucknow University. At Lucknow University, Abhay Singh was one year senior to Dhananjay Singh in studies. He was already living in room number 51 in the hostel. He lied to the hostel warden that Dhananjay was his aunt's son. After this, Dhananjay Singh was allotted room number 18 on the lower floor of Abhay Singh's hostel. 2- The friendship of the three was famous in the university Arun Upadhyay, also from Jaunpur, was studying at Lucknow University. He was active in student politics. Due to their connection with Jaunpur, Abhay and Dhananjay were friends with him. According to Abhay Singh, his dream was to qualify for UPSC. Meanwhile, Dhananjay Singh says that he had only two dreams from the beginning: first, to join the army, and second, to enter politics after retirement. This trio became famous on the university campus. The three were seen together in protests against the Mandal agitation. At that time, Lucknow University had dominance across the entire state. Arun Upadhyay was preparing for the General Secretary election. Their friendship lasted until 2002. After this, their relationship started to sour. In 2002, Dhananjay Singh was subjected to a deadly attack in Banaras. Dhananjay Singh filed an FIR, naming his close friend Abhay Singh as the accused. 3- How Both Got the Title of Strongman Former Jaunpur MP Dhananjay Singh of Jaunpur and Abhay Singh, MLA from Goshainganj, Ayodhya, are known as strongman leaders in politics. Dhananjay Singh claimed in an interview with Dainik Bhaskar that after meeting Abhay Singh, he also became an accused in every one of Abhay Singh's cases. Later, when he became active in politics, cases kept piling up due to political reasons. On the other hand, Abhay Singh claims that before Arun Upadhyay's student elections, only one assault case was registered against him. After this, all other cases were registered. Many cases were registered even without any crime. In many, he was also made an accused in Dhananjay Singh's crimes. 4- In 1996, Abhay went to jail, and Dhananjay absconded In 1996, Hemant Singh was murdered. At that time, the then SSP Surya Kumar Shukla in Lucknow made both Abhay and Dhananjay accused. However, Abhay Singh claims that both of them were falsely implicated in this case. On January 11, 1996, Abhay Singh went to jail in a case registered for attempted murder and remained there for 4 and a half years. Dhananjay Singh remained absconding till February 1999. 5- Dispute in jail, both went their separate ways After Dhananjay surrendered in February 1999, he met Abhay in jail. There, a dispute arose between the two over old incidents, tender money, and the murders of Santosh and Abhishek. From there, both went their separate ways. In 2000, Abhay was released on bail. He met Naseemuddin Siddiqui in jail. Through him, Abhay Singh got his first MLA ticket from BSP in 2002. But he lost. Meanwhile, Dhananjay Singh contested the Rari assembly election as an independent in 2002 and won. On October 4, 2002, Dhananjay Singh's convoy was attacked. Dhananjay filed a case against Abhay, and since then, their paths diverged. Whenever they get a chance, they keep showering accusations on each other. When Dhananjay's close associates Alok Singh and Manish Singh Tata were caught in the codeine cough syrup case, Abhay had then taunted him by calling him 'Codeine Bhaiya'.

stories.title: 4-year-old girl shows no fear of water:Swims 900 metres across Yamuna river in 21 minutes; stuns onlookers
stories.summary: In Prayagraj district of Uttar Pradesh, 4-year-old Satya Bharti from the Mahewa West area has achieved a feat that even seasoned swimmers often find challenging. She swam across the Yamuna river in just 21 minutes and 28 seconds. The historic swim began at exactly 7am on Saturday. Displaying remarkable confidence and courage, Satya battled the strong currents of the Yamuna river and swam from one bank to the other, leaving everyone astonished. A video of her achievement is rapidly going viral on social media, with people widely praising her determination and bravery. Her parents and coach are extremely proud of her accomplishment. Training under coach Tribhuvan Nishad Satya is the daughter of Devendra Kumar and has been training regularly under her coach, Tribhuvan Nishad. According to him, she has shown discipline, eagerness to learn and strong confidence from a very young age. At an age when most children are just getting familiar with basic play, Satya has crossed a major river like the Yamuna, proving that with determination and proper guidance, age is no barrier to success. She has now become an inspiration not just for Prayagraj, but for the entire state. A promising future ahead Her coach believes that with advanced training, Satya has the potential to win medals for the state and the country. Meanwhile, her video continues to gain traction online, with people encouraging her and urging support to help her reach greater heights.

stories.title: Misleading video sparks FIR on 2 RJD women spokespersons:Unrest-hit Noida factories reopen after 2 days with heavy security
stories.summary: After two days of unrest, factories in Noida reopened on Wednesday, with the situation returning to normal. Heavy security has been deployed, with surveillance through CCTV cameras and drones. Around 16 companies of Rapid Action Force (RAF) and Pradeshik Armed Constabulary (PAC) have been stationed, while police conducted flag marches in Sectors 63, 80, 84, 85 and Phase 2. Notices on salary hikes have been put up outside several companies. However, some units remained shut for the day, informing employees through notices that operations would resume later, with further updates to be shared in advance. Meanwhile, an FIR has been registered at Noida’s Cyber Crime Police Station against two RJD women spokespersons, Kanchana Yadav and Priyanka Bharti. They have been accused of sharing misleading videos on social media to incite unrest and damage the image of law enforcement. District Magistrate (DM) Medha Rupam said- If any outsourcing agency or its employee causes disturbance or mischief, the agency will also be held responsible. In such a situation, the agency can be blacklisted. Its license can also be revoked. Actually, factory workers created a ruckus on Monday-Tuesday over salary increases. Stone-pelting occurred at more than 80 places. Vandalism occurred in 350 companies. Minister Anil Rajbhar said, “There is a strong whiff of a big conspiracy in this entire incident. Some anti-national forces might be involved in this.” Meanwhile, the company owners say that outsiders instigated the atmosphere. Workers can never resort to violent protests. They cannot harm the place from where they earn their livelihood. Currently, the police have arrested 396 people, including 4 women. See pictures- DM said, ‘Contractors should follow guidelines’ Union leader says, ‘No connection with agitation’ Amar Singh, District President of All India Centre Council Trade Union, says that the union has no connection with the violence and agitation. The agitation was carried out by the workers. Surendra Nahata, President of MSME Industrial Association Noida, informed that industries from Sector-1 to 6 are opening. The remaining factories will also open. Situation completely normal, no law and order problem Regarding the workers' protest in Noida, Uttar Pradesh Director General of Police (DGP) Rajiv Krishna said that the situation in the district is completely normal. There is no law and order problem anywhere. All senior officers are present on the spot. The situation is being continuously monitored.

stories.title: 3 years after Atiq’s killing, wife Shaista still missing:2 other family members absconding; search continues for co-conspirators in Umesh Pal murder case
stories.summary: Three years on, the UP Police has failed to trace Atiq Ahmed’s wife Shaista Parveen. Raids were conducted across nine states, with support from ATS and RAF teams, but she remains untraceable. A reward of ₹50,000 has been announced for information on Shaista, who has been underground since the Umesh Pal murder case. She continues to feature on the UP Police’s most-wanted list of women criminals, yet her whereabouts remain unknown. Apart from Shaista, Atiq’s sister Ayesha Noori and brother Ashraf’s wife Zainab are also absconding. All three have been accused of conspiring in the Umesh Pal murder and aiding the attackers. The police have announced rewards of ₹25,000 each on Ayesha and Zainab. While there were initial suspicions that they may have fled to Dubai, officials later ruled out that possibility. Notably, Atiq Ahmed was killed on April 15, 2023. Even after three years, the police have not been able to arrest the three key accused women linked to the conspiracy. What happened over these three years, and why have they remained beyond the police’s reach? Read the full report. On February 24, 2023, lawyer Umesh Pal and his two police gunners were killed in a brutal shooting and bombing in Prayagraj’s Dhumanganj area, setting off one of Uttar Pradesh’s biggest crime probes. CCTV clues and widening conspiracy CCTV footage showed Atiq Ahmed’s son Asad firing, while Guddu Muslim hurled bombs. Others, including Ghulam, Shabir and Usman, were also seen shooting. At the time, Atiq was lodged in Sabarmati Jail, and investigators alleged he orchestrated the attack from there. He, along with brother Ashraf, son Asad and nine others, was named in the case. Within days, Atiq’s wife Shaista Parveen, sister Ayesha Noori and Ashraf’s wife Zainab were also accused of conspiracy and aiding the attackers. Notably, all three were still in the Dhumanganj area even two days after the murder. Shaista later wrote to Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and the Allahabad High Court Chief Justice, calling the case a political conspiracy aimed at keeping Atiq’s family out of local elections. Manhunt without breakthrough After CCTV footage was released on February 26, showing Asad firing, Shaista, Zainab and Ayesha went underground. Police launched an extensive crackdown—encounters followed, properties were demolished, and rewards were announced for information. Multiple teams carried out raids across Uttar Pradesh before expanding the search to nine states. Within weeks, more than 500 locations were searched. Several accused were caught, but the three women remained untraceable. No trace even after key killings On April 13, 2023, Asad was killed in a police encounter in Jhansi. Two days later, Atiq Ahmed and Ashraf were shot dead in Prayagraj during a medical visit. Despite these developments, none of the three women surfaced—not even for the last rites, despite heavy police surveillance. Repeated inputs placed Shaista in parts of Kaushambi, where police conducted searches using drones and combing operations, but found no trace. Assets seized, leads go cold As the search continued, authorities seized properties worth nearly ₹3,000 crore linked to Atiq’s network, many allegedly held in benami names. Investigators believe the total value could be significantly higher. CCTV clues from Meerut suggested Guddu Muslim had taken shelter at a relative’s house linked to Ayesha Noori, leading to one arrest, but Ayesha herself remained absconding. Later inputs from Odisha and Delhi also failed to yield results, though police ruled out any foreign escape. Meanwhile, the trial in the Atiq-Ashraf murder case continues, largely through video conferencing due to security concerns.

stories.title: DMs, SSPs in 25 UP districts are females:Govt plans 33% women reservation in postings before 2027 polls
stories.summary: Efforts are underway in Uttar Pradesh to increase women’s participation in governance, with the first impact likely to be seen in district-level administration. The state government is preparing to assign more women IAS and IPS officers to key positions such as Divisional Commissioner, District Magistrate (DM), and Senior Superintendent of Police (SSP). At present, women account for around 16% of DMs and about 12% of SSPs across the state’s 75 districts. Even before the implementation of the ‘Nari Shakti Vandan Adhiniyam’, the government is planning to increase women’s representation in bureaucracy to 33%. The move is aimed at sending a strong political message on women’s empowerment. Officials believe this step could help strengthen trust among women voters ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections. The move is being seen as part of a broader strategy: Message of empowerment: Extending ‘Nari Shakti’ beyond Parliament and Assemblies to decision-making roles like DM and SSP Targeting women voters: Of UP’s 13.39 crore voters, nearly 6.5 crore are women From beneficiaries to decision-makers: After schemes like free ration, Ujjwala and Mission Shakti, focus now shifts to representation Governance branding: Women officers are often associated with stricter law enforcement and greater sensitivity in social issues Countering opposition narrative: Aimed at addressing criticism on jobs, governance and social balance Currently, 12 out of 75 districts (16%) have women District Magistrates. This number could increase to 20–25 districts in the coming reshuffle. In policing, women IPS officers are posted in only 8 districts, indicating significant scope for expansion. Who could get key postings? Several women officers are being considered for district leadership roles, including: Annapurna Garg (IAS, 2016 batch) Kavita Meena, Vice Chairman, Muzaffarnagar Development Authority Saranjit Kaur Broca, Director, Women and Child Welfare Isha Priya, Special Secretary, Tourism Transfers likely before elections Transfers were restricted during the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) period from October 27, 2025 to April 10, 2026, with changes requiring Election Commission approval. With the 2027 Assembly elections expected in February–March, a major reshuffle of Commissioners, DMs and police chiefs is likely before the Model Code of Conduct comes into force, possibly by late January or early February. Election rules may trigger reshuffle As per Election Commission norms, officers posted in the same district for over three years ahead of elections are typically transferred. Apart from election-related changes, DMs of several districts—including Ambedkar Nagar, Chandauli, Hapur, Chitrakoot, Shravasti, Bhadohi, Mahoba, Sultanpur, Hathras, Barabanki and Lalitpur—may also be shifted for administrative reasons. Some may be moved to other districts, while others could be assigned roles such as Director or Special Secretary in government departments.

stories.title: Woman remains unidentified 5 days after her dead body recovery:Post-mortem report shows 17 injury marks, rape suspected
stories.summary: The post-mortem report of the unidentified woman's body found by the roadside in the Kakori area has arrived. The report shows two severe injury marks on the front and back of the woman's head, while about 15 injuries were found on other parts of the body. Doctors have stated the cause of death as severe head injury. Given the suspicion of rape, doctors have prepared slides and sent them for examination. Only after the report comes will it be known whether rape occurred or not. However, the woman has not yet been identified. Body was covered in blood On the morning of 9 April, outside Madarpur village in Kakori, the blood-soaked body of an unknown woman, approximately 35 years old, was found in a field by the roadside. Looking at the condition of the body, murder after rape was suspected. According to Inspector Satish Rathore, the woman's head had been struck with a stick or a heavy object. Injury marks were also found at several places on the body, which point towards a violent incident. So far, the woman has not been identified. For identification, photos have been pasted in public places in the city and surrounding districts. CCTV camera footage from toll plazas on Agra Expressway and other major highways is being scrutinized. No concrete clue has been found from the crime scene or the woman's clothes that could help identify her. The investigation into the case is ongoing. Unidentified body was cremated Due to lack of identification, the police cremated the woman's body on April 13. DNA samples have been preserved for future identification. A case of murder has been registered against unknown persons in the matter. ACP Kakori Shakeel Ahmed said that so far, footage from more than 500 CCTV cameras has been scanned for the identification of the woman. Pictures of the body have been circulated on social media platforms. Missing person cases registered in nearby districts are also being investigated.

stories.title: Parents plan to sell their newborn fails:Grandmother rescues child; mother had struck a deal with businessman for 2.5 lakhs
stories.summary: In Agra, a mother made a deal to sell her two-day-old newborn baby. The price of the baby was fixed at Rs 2.5 lakh. A businessman even reached the hospital to take the baby, but the grandmother and aunt got wind of it. Both of them filed a complaint on the Child Helpline. As soon as the information was received, the team reached the spot. Immediate action was taken with the help of police. The newborn and family members were taken into custody. Everyone was presented before the magistrate of the Child Welfare Committee (CWC). On Monday, the magistrate had the couple fill an affidavit. After this, the newborn was handed over to them. Now know the complete case A call came to Childline's helpline number 1098 on Friday night. The woman who called, identified herself as Rajkumari. Rajkumari said that her son Manoj lives in Shastripuram, Sikandra. Manoj works as a laborer in a factory. His wife Kumkum has a son from before. “Kumkum gave birth to a second son at the hospital on Wednesday. The child is being sold right after birth. A deal has already been made with a trader from Kamla Nagar. A deal has been fixed for two and a half lakh rupees to hand over the newborn. The trader was supposed to reach the hospital on Friday night to take the child,” she said. Childline team reached the hospital, couple denied the allegations As soon as the complaint was received, the Childline team reached the hospital with the police. The team spoke with the woman who gave birth to the newborn and her husband. The couple flatly denied the allegations of selling the child. They claimed that some relatives were making false allegations as part of a conspiracy. After this, with the help of police, the child and family members were presented before the Child Welfare Committee (CWC). Here, an affidavit was filled by the couple. After completing the procedure, the newborn was handed back to the couple. Grandmother said - They were selling the newborn for two and a half lakh Grandmother Rajkumari said - On Friday, my daughter-in-law gave birth to a son at Lady Lion Hospital. Just a short while later, some people arrived at the hospital to see the child. Those people were talking about buying the child. I wanted to bring my grandson home. The son, daughter-in-law, and father-in-law were going to give away the child for two and a half lakh rupees. I opposed this, but no one listened to me. Angered by this, I returned home. After some time, my daughter called, so I told her the whole matter. Child reunited with family after two days of surveillance Rajkumari said that my daughter immediately complained to Agra Child Helpline number 1098 from Meerut. After this, the team reached the spot and action was initiated. Due to Saturday and Sunday being holidays, further proceedings could not take place. The Childline team deployed police personnel outside the hospital. The police kept surveillance for two days so that no one could take the child away. On Monday, we were presented before the magistrate of the Child Welfare Committee (CWC). After filling out an affidavit there, further action was taken. Now the child is at our home and we are happy. Child will have to be presented again after 15 days Childline coordinator Brajesh Kumar Gautam said- On Monday, the couple was presented before the Child Welfare Committee (CWC). Here, a written affidavit was taken from the couple. It was clarified in the affidavit that they will not give the newborn to any other person for adoption. After completing the procedure, the child has been handed over to the couple. They have been instructed that the child will have to be presented before the committee again within 15 days.

stories.title: Shankaracharya Avimukteshwaranand receives death threat:Audio clip warns of fate similar to Atiq Ahmed
stories.summary: A case of death threats against Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand has come to light, with the seer being warned of a fate similar to that of mafia don Atiq Ahmed. According to reports, threatening messages were sent to the official number of the Jyotish Peeth. Initially, objectionable text messages were received. After the number was blocked, the sender continued to issue threats through voice messages. In the audio clips, the caller allegedly used abusive language and threatened to kill the Shankaracharya, stating that he would be targeted during his upcoming tour. Threat linked to upcoming ‘Gavishti Yatra’ Swami Avimukteshwaranand has been leading a nationwide campaign advocating “Gomata as Rashtramata”. As part of this initiative, his “Gavishti Yatra” is scheduled to begin from May 3, covering every assembly constituency in Uttar Pradesh. During the yatra, he plans to raise awareness about cow protection and the establishment of cow shelters. Earlier threats also reported This is not the first time the seer has received threats. His supporters claim that certain groups are unhappy with his cow protection campaign and have been targeting him. Security concerns rise ahead of Yatra With the Gavishti Yatra approaching, the latest threat has raised serious concerns regarding security arrangements. Questions are being raised about ensuring adequate protection for the Shankaracharya during the tour, as authorities are expected to review and strengthen security measures in light of the threat.

stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:Kanpur kidney racket-agent claims of facilitating 50 transplants; Trump threatens with 50% tariffs on countries supplying weapons to Iran more
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. Trump threatens 50% tariffs on countries supplying weapons to Iran US President Donald Trump on Wednesday said the US and Iran are moving towards a longer-term peace deal, while warning that countries supplying weapons to Iran will face 50% US tariffs. 2. School bus carrying 35 children overturns, 10 injured A school bus carrying 35 school children overturned in Meerut on Wednesday morning at 7:30 AM. More than 10 children were injured in the accident. Chaos ensued at the scene after the incident. People present nearby rushed to help. 3. Kanpur kidney racket - Agent claims of facilitating 50 transplants, Delhi's renowned hospital name surfaces In Kanpur's kidney scandal, police interrogated agent Shivam Agarwal alias Kada on Tuesday. During this, Shivam confessed to facilitating 50 kidney transplants. He revealed that he received ₹50K for each operation. In the interrogation that lasted about 2 hours, he was asked 15 questions. He gave evasive answers to most questions. DCP West SM Kasim Abidi said, Shivam is not cooperating in the interrogation. He will soon be taken into police custody, and then a detailed interrogation will be conducted. 4. RBI's repo rate unchanged at 5.25% The Reserve Bank of India (RBI), Governor, Sanjay Malhotra, said on Wednesday, 8 April, 2026, that the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) has decided to keep the repo rate unchanged at 5.25%. 5. Cops join prostitution racket kingpin’s birthday party Two constables in Kanpur have been suspended after a video surfaced showing them attending a birthday party of an alleged prostitution racket kingpin. The action comes after police recently busted a sex racket on April 3 and arrested its alleged mastermind, Rohit Verma. 6. 13-year-old raped in Lucknow with hands and legs tied, 5 arrested A rape case of a 13-year-old girl has come to light in Lucknow. The girl was found unconscious in an under-construction house on Tuesday, 7 April, night. Her hands and feet were tied. According to victim's brother, his sister, who was returning after work, had stopped in the under-construction house to take shelter from the storm and rain. 7. Sabarimala case; govt says courts can’t label religious practices as superstition Supreme Court on Wednesday continued, for the second day, hearing the case on alleged discrimination against women in religious places. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta argued that no secular court can label a religious practice as mere superstition. 8. 'Will my prepaid meter automatically become postpaid?':Prepaid smart metre mandate removed on new connections The mandatory requirement for prepaid smart meters when getting a new electricity connection in UP has been removed. This means when getting a new electricity connection, you will have to specify whether you want a prepaid smart meter or a postpaid smart meter. 9. CM Yogi questions scientists on changing weather, inaugurates Agricultural Science Congress-2026 Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath inaugurated the Uttar Pradesh Agricultural Science Congress-2026 in Lucknow, where he shared an anecdote from his interaction with agricultural meteorologists. He said he recently asked scientists why weather conditions were deteriorating suddenly during crucial farming periods. 10. BJP alleges mistreatment of Kolkata rape-murder victim's mother Ratna Debnath, BJP candidate from West Bengal’s Panihati constituency and mother of the Kolkata rape-murder victim, alleged on Wednesday that TMC workers tried to attack her during campaigning, injuring several BJP workers.

stories.title: CM Yogi questions scientists on changing weather:Western disturbances cited as the reason behind changes
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath inaugurated the Uttar Pradesh Agricultural Science Congress-2026 in Lucknow, where he shared an anecdote from his interaction with agricultural meteorologists. He said he recently asked scientists why weather conditions were deteriorating suddenly during crucial farming periods. Western disturbance cited as key reason According to the Chief Minister, scientists attributed the changes to a western disturbance. He said atmospheric disturbances originating in Iran and Pakistan were affecting weather patterns in India. “They explained that clouds are forming at lower levels, which is causing hailstorms and unseasonal rainfall,” Yogi said, adding that such climatic disruptions are likely to continue. Remarks on nature and human tendencies Yogi remarked that such challenges arise repeatedly, drawing a parallel between human tendencies and nature. He said that just as some people disrupt peace, nature too can behave unpredictably, adversely impacting farmers. He stressed the need to adopt and promote indigenous agricultural practices, as repeatedly advocated by the Prime Minister. Read 5 major points from CM's address 1. Agriculture and Entrepreneurship were targeted historically The Chief Minister said that when India accounted for 44–45% of the global economy, agriculture was its backbone, supported by farmers and artisans. He added that historically, invaders not only targeted agriculture but also India’s entrepreneurial ecosystem. Referring to the song Vande Mataram from the novel Anandamath, he highlighted the hardships during Bengal’s famine and colonial exploitation, where farmers were pushed into debt. 2. Sugar industry has revived in UP Yogi said that earlier, sugar mills in Uttar Pradesh were shutting down or being sold, and farmers often did not receive payments for years. “Today, these mills have transformed into sugar complexes. Uttar Pradesh produces 55% of the country’s sugarcane, and ethanol production has increased significantly,” he said. He added that over ₹2.9 lakh crore has been transferred to sugarcane farmers through Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT), and most mills now make payments within a week. 3. Trust deficit before 2017 The Chief Minister noted that before 2017, there was a lack of trust among farmers toward the government. He said farmers faced distress, including suicides, migration, and exploitation, as they felt disconnected from policymaking. 4. Farmers were merely an electoral issue Yogi stated that earlier governments lacked a clear policy for farmers, treating them mainly as an electoral issue. He said farmers were divided along caste lines, faced high input costs, low output, and exploitation by middlemen. 5. Middlemen dominated procurement system He added that government procurement centers were ineffective, allowing middlemen to dominate. “As a result, farmers were burdened with debt and often driven to extreme distress,” he said, adding that policies implemented after 2017 have addressed these issues. Farmers hit by unseasonal rainfall For the past 15 days, unseasonal rainfall and hailstorms have severely impacted farmers in Uttar Pradesh. Thousands of acres of crops, including wheat, mustard, and pulses, have been damaged. The Chief Minister has directed officials to conduct surveys promptly and ensure compensation for affected farmers. Scientists honoured at the event During the event, CM Yogi Adityanath honoured 15 scientists under the “Uttar Pradesh Agricultural Scientist Award Scheme 2025–26.” Additionally, 30 scientists from the Uttar Pradesh Academy of Agricultural Sciences were felicitated for their outstanding work in 2025. Discussions on modern agricultural technologies and innovations were also held, and the Chief Minister released several publications during the event.

stories.title: Kanpur police nab 20 cyber fraudsters in a dramatic operation:70 ops team in 17 vehicles conduct raid, chase suspects from fields
stories.summary: In a major crackdown, Kanpur Police busted another 'mini Jamtara' in Uttar Pradesh, arresting 20 cyber fraudsters in a dramatic, film-style operation. Around 70 police personnel arrived in 17 vehicles, surrounded the area from all sides, and used drones for surveillance before launching the raid. The operation was carried out on Tuesday evening in the Reuna area of Ghatampur. Fraudsters operating from makeshift huts The accused were operating from huts built in fields, from where they ran their cyber fraud network. According to police, the gang targeted people across the country by posing as police officers or offering fake housing schemes and bank loans. All those arrested are reportedly educated up to Class 5, 8, or 11. See 2 pictures- Area emerging as cyber crime hotspot ADCP Sumit Sudhakar Ramteke, who led the operation, said the Reuna region was emerging as a hotspot for cyber fraud. Villages such as Rathigaon, Lakshmanpur, Samaj Nagar, Badela, and Adigaon had been flagged on the police’s Pratibimb portal as cybercrime hotspots. Surveillance conducted before raid Police officials had earlier visited the village in civil dress to assess the situation. They observed that groups of young men gathered in huts located in fields and orchards every morning and carried out fraudulent calls from there. Laptops, phones, SIM cards seized Following intelligence inputs, the police conducted the raid and arrested 20 suspects. Several items were seized from the huts, including laptops, mobile phones, hundreds of active SIM cards, and other electronic devices. The sudden operation created panic in the village. Each fraudster made several calls on daily basis According to ADCP Ramteke, each fraudster made around 50 to 60 calls daily, successfully trapping at least 5 to 6 victims. The gang was reportedly earning a large sum of money every day. Police also recovered details of 20–50 mule bank accounts linked to the operation. Search on for absconding accused ACP Ghatampur stated that around 15 suspects managed to flee during the raid. Several villagers also escaped after getting wind of the police action. Search operations are underway to track down the absconding accused and dismantle the entire network. These accused were arrested

stories.title: Cops join prostitution racket kingpin’s birthday party:Constable face suspension after clip surfaces
stories.summary: Two constables in Kanpur have been suspended after a video surfaced showing them attending a birthday party of an alleged prostitution racket kingpin. The action comes after police recently busted a sex racket on April 3 and arrested its alleged mastermind, Rohit Verma. According to police, the racket involved sending women to nearly 20 hotels across the city. Videos show assault and abuse of minor Following the bust, multiple disturbing videos of the accused Rohit Verma and his associate Sahil have surfaced. In one video, the duo is seen brutally beating a minor with sticks and shoes. In another, Rohit is seen urinating on the minor. The videos also show the accused invoking the name of a police officer to intimidate the victim. Police response and ongoing investigation DCP South Deependra Nath Chaudhary confirmed that two constables—Deepak Chaudhary and Dharmendra Singh—have been suspended after their presence at the party came to light. He added that Rohit Verma has already been arrested, while three police teams have been deployed to arrest absconding accused Sahil. See 2 pictures- Birthday party video raises questions In the viral video, Rohit Verma is seen celebrating his birthday, cutting a cake and partying with several individuals, including the two suspended constables. However, DCP Chaudhary clarified that the video is old and was recorded when both constables were posted at Barra Police Station. An investigation has been initiated. How the prostitution racket was busted The case came to light on April 3 when a young woman from West Bengal approached Police Commissioner Raghubir Lal in Kanpur. She alleged that a person known as “Kolkata’s Dada,” along with Rohit Verma, lured her with a job offer and brought her to Kanpur, where she was held captive and forced into prostitution. The victim said she was sent to clients under strict surveillance and was not allowed to step out alone. She managed to escape on April 3 and reported the matter to the police. Arrest and raids conducted Following the complaint, multiple police teams were formed under the leadership of ADCP Crime Sumit Sudhakar Ramteke, ADCP Line Shiva Singh, and trainee IPS officer Sumedh M. Jadhav. Police conducted raids in the Indiranagar area and arrested Rohit Verma. A separate team has been sent to West Bengal to trace and arrest the other accused, known as “Kolkata’s Dada.” Racket linked to 20 hotels Police said around 20 hotel names were found in Rohit Verma’s mobile phone, where women were allegedly supplied. Booking registers and other documents have been seized from these hotels. However, no victims were found during the raids. Police are continuing efforts to identify other victims and those involved in the network. Who are Rohit Verma and Sahil Rohit Verma is a Kanpur-based YouTuber who, along with his associate Sahil, created videos for social media. Police also recovered a press card from him. Rohit has six cases registered against him, including charges of molestation, offences under the POCSO Act, running a sex racket, theft, and dealing in stolen property. Sahil, a resident of Barra-2, is educated up to Class 12 and remains absconding. Multiple videos surface after arrest After Rohit’s arrest, four videos have surfaced, though their exact time and location remain unverified: Probe underway Police officials stated that investigations are ongoing to uncover the full extent of the racket and identify all those involved, while disciplinary and legal action continues against the accused and implicated personnel.

stories.title: Crackdown on unauthorized schools and coaching centers in UP:Special drive to continue till April 18 on HC orders; action to be taken against violators
stories.summary: There will now be major action against the arbitrariness of unauthorized schools and private coaching institutions in Uttar Pradesh. On the orders of the High Court, the Board of Secondary Education, Uttar Pradesh, has been directed to run a special inspection campaign in all districts from 6 to 18 April. Schools and coaching centers running without recognition will be cracked down upon. Action on HC orders The matter is related to Public Interest Litigation number 542/2024 of the Allahabad High Court. The High Court has ordered strict action against those running schools and coaching centers without legal recognition. The Secretary of the Board issued a letter on 5 April directing all District School Inspectors, District Basic Education Officers, and Block Education Officers to conduct this campaign strictly and take action against schools and coaching centers without recognition. What needs to be done? Running schools without recognition is a violation of RTE The Council Secretary has written in the letter that running schools without recognition is a violation of the Right to Education Act 2009. In the state, coaching can only be operated in recognized schools. The responsibility of admitting students studying in unauthorized institutions to other schools will also lie with the concerned officials. Report sought on 5 points, district-wise Appeal to parents The Secretary has appealed to parents to enroll their children only in recognized schools and coaching centers listed on upmsp.edu.in. Admission to unauthorized institutions can put students' future at risk. This campaign will run simultaneously across the entire state. The Education Department believes that this will improve the quality of education and stop the exploitation of students.

stories.title: PMO, NITI Aayog commend Gorakhpur’s UFMC:Over 65% improvement in monsoon waterlogging clearance
stories.summary: The country's first AI-based Urban Flood Management Cell (UFMC), established in Gorakhpur, is receiving appreciation from the Prime Minister's Office (PMO) and NITI Aayog. NITI Aayog found in its assessment that the Gorakhpur model can strengthen the disaster response capacity of urban bodies across the country through data-based forecasting. This has been considered a major shift in the direction from reactive to proactive urban management. This UFMC was inaugurated by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on July 23, 2025. It is an advanced Urban Flood Early Warning and Decision Support System. According to Municipal Commissioner Gaurav Singh Sogarwal, after establishing UFMC, the forecast of rainfall and waterlogging has become more than 80 percent accurate 24 hours in advance. In the trial phase, 70 percent of the 250 complaints were resolved within a few hours. An improvement of more than 65 percent was observed in overall system efficiency. This system integrates AI-based rainfall forecasting, sensor-based water level monitoring, and stormwater modeling. As soon as the water level rises, sensors send alerts and the automated pumping system gets activated immediately, ensuring real-time solutions in waterlogged areas. Work done on two major aspects The Municipal Commissioner states that work has been done on two major aspects under the Urban Flood Risk Management Program. First, the Urban Flood Early Warning System, which provides warnings and real-time information to provide immediate relief to citizens. Second, the Decision Support System, which assists in long-term planning and policy making for the city, so that flood management capabilities can be made more robust and effective in the future. Complete automation of all pumping stations This comprehensive approach of the Gorakhpur Model not only enables the city to effectively deal with current disasters, but also reduces the risk of loss of life and property in the future. Under this project, all important drains of the city, all equipment, and all responsible officers and teams have been mapped along with their contact details. A total of 28 waterlogging hotspots and 85 points of interest have been identified in the city, which are more sensitive from a waterlogging perspective. Complete automation of all pumping stations in the city has been done. A 24x7 emergency control room has been established, which performs continuous monitoring and coordination work. A grievance portal has been prepared for citizens, through which notification of any problem and its quick resolution can be ensured. Rain-related information is received every 15 mins The Municipal Commissioner informed that the Municipal Corporation has also installed two automatic rain gauges in the city, which provide rain-related information every 15 minutes. A total of 110 automatic water level recorders have been installed on primary and secondary drains. These sensors send information related to water levels every 2 to 15 minutes. When the water level in the drains exceeds 80 percent, automated alerts start reaching the concerned officials. When the water level in sump wells exceeds 60 percent, pumps automatically start through the automatic system. Warnings related to fuel shortage and pump maintenance also reach officials in time. Strategy adopted by UFMC "Forecast, prepare, and ensure safety. Before the rain, through Urban Flood Modeling, it is predicted which areas of the city are likely to experience waterlogging the next day. A detailed report based on this forecast is sent to the concerned authorities so that they can prepare in time. Mobile pumps and suction machines are arranged in advance. A day before, warnings regarding the amount and timing of rainfall are sent to all officers and field teams through walkie-talkies. It is also ensured that all pumps are functioning properly and there are no blockages anywhere in the drains. As soon as rainfall begins, UFMC's 24x7 emergency control room becomes active. Announcements are made from the control room about which drains are overflowing, which points of interest are at high risk or have been submerged, at which hotspots mobile pumps should be immediately activated, and in which areas suction machines should be deployed. This keeps field teams fully alert and makes it clear to them where and what action needs to be taken. Response time to waterlogging complaints is now significantly reduced Pumping stations in the city where the water level in sump wells exceeds 60 percent are automatically activated from the control room. This system has been operational for the past 4 months, and the results have been very good. For instance, the response time to waterlogging complaints has reduced considerably. Earlier, it took 10-12 hours; now, this time has reduced to less than 1-2 hours, especially in places where waterlogging occurred repeatedly. 60 percent reduction in pump shutdown cases Similarly, pump shutdown incidents have reduced by more than 60 percent, because now pumps operate automatically and their maintenance is done on time. More than 250 people registered complaints, of which more than 70 percent of complaints were resolved immediately and correctly. Due to real-time alerts and early warnings, many old waterlogging-prone areas did not experience flooding this time. Technology has increased capacity and efficiency, enabling teams to work faster and collaboratively. Pumping stations have now become automatic, reducing manual work and making results more reliable. Through this innovative initiative, Gorakhpur Municipal Corporation has not only reduced the problem of waterlogging but has also made remarkable improvements in accountability, quick response, and citizen satisfaction.

stories.title: Pradeep Jaiswal's relatives linked to codeine cough syrup case:5 family members of SP Trade Council State President arrested
stories.summary: New layers are beginning to unfold in the nationally discussed Varanasi codeine cough syrup case after the arrest of Vaibhav Jaiswal, nephew of Samajwadi Party Trade Council State President Pradeep Jaiswal. Following Vaibhav's arrest in the case, police have also found five women, including his wife and mother, involved in money laundering. Liquor shops were opened in the names of these women using earnings from the codeine cough syrup business. Kotwali police had apprehended five women, including Vaibhav Jaiswal's mother and wife. Police presented them before the judicial magistrate for remand late at night. It should be noted that earlier, a photo of Pradeep Jaiswal with cough syrup mafia Shubham Jaiswal had also surfaced; since then, his entire family and relatives have been on the police radar. Meanwhile, several relatives of the SP leader also appear to be caught in the net. The arrest of women for the first time in the case has raised many questions. Hawala trader Vaibhav's mother and wife arrested ACP Kotwali Vijay Pratap Singh informed that the proprietor of Shaili Traders and Bhola Jaiswal, lodged in Sonbhadra jail, had arranged liquor contracts under the lottery system for Vaibhav Jaiswal's mother Radhika, wife Shivani, both residents of Navapura, Usha Devi of Rajghat Bharadwaji Tola, Rekha Devi of Kayasth Tola, and Babita Singh. Through these contracts, he used to convert his black money into white. Secret revealed after arrest of Vaibhav Jaiswal The ACP informed recently that police had arrested Amla businessman Vaibhav Jaiswal, a resident of Navapura. Based on the interrogation conducted after the arrest, information about the syndicate converting black money to white was revealed. In this, Bhola and Shubham Jaiswal had also invested their black money in the liquor business and converted it to white. Upon receiving this information, these licensees were arrested after conducting raids. Court released them, police could not provide evidence Police presented everyone before the judicial magistrate in the late evening and demanded 14 days of judicial remand. After hearing all aspects and examining the evidence, the court released all the women from the court itself. It should be noted that the mastermind of the cough syrup case, Shubham Jaiswal, is still absconding.

stories.title: 13-year-old raped in Lucknow with hands and feet tied:Victim took shelter in an under-construction house, 5 arrested
stories.summary: A rape case of a 13-year-old girl has come to light in Lucknow. The girl was found unconscious in an under-construction house on Tuesday, 7 April, night. Her hands and feet were tied. According to victim's brother, his sister, who was returning after work, had stopped in the under-construction house to take shelter from the storm and rain. During this, a 17-year-old minor accused, along with his four friends, held his sister captive. They beat and raped her. According to the brother, when his sister did not reach home, we reached the spot while searching. Seeing us, the accused started fleeing. Two accused jumped from the roof, due to which they got injured. Hearing the noise, people from the surrounding area gathered. All five accused were caught after chasing and handed over to the police. The police have admitted the girl to Lokbandhu Hospital for treatment. According to police, the girl accepted during interrogation, that the accused is her acquaintance. He is the one who raped her. His friends supported him. A case has been registered based on the statement, and the matter is being investigated. The case is from the Ashiana police station area. The teenager had gone to work in place of her mother The minor girl is originally a resident of Kannauj. She lives with her family in a rented house in the Ashiana area. Her father is a mason. Her mother works in households. According to her brother, their mother was not feeling well. Due to this, on Tuesday evening, the sister went to work in households in place of their mother. She was returning home after finishing work at 8:30 PM when she took shelter in an under-construction house to escape the storm and rain. During this time, the accused arrived there with his friends and committed the crime. When the sister did not reach home late at night, the family members started searching for her. A sound was heard from a house under construction on the way. Family members reached the spot. There, the girl was found in a distressed condition. Her hands and feet were tied. Seeing the family members, the accused started fleeing. People from the surrounding area also reached the spot. They surrounded and caught the accused. The matter was reported to the police control room. Police immediately reached the spot. All the accused were taken into custody. Forensic team collected evidence Police took the accused into custody and brought them to the Ashiana police station. DCP Central Vikrant Veer reached the spot. He gathered information about the incident from family members and people around. The forensic team collected evidence from the crime scene. The DCP said- On Tuesday night, Ashiana police station received information via Dial 112 about the rape of a minor girl. Police immediately reached the spot and the main accused is being interrogated.

stories.title: Sanitation worker robs ex-railway man posing cop:Gorakhpur police arrests in 4 hrs, recovers full amount
stories.summary: Police have apprehended the accused who allegedly posed as a police inspector and snatched a bag full of money from a retired railway employee near the GM Office in the Cantt area of Gorakhpur. The accused is a sanitation worker in the municipal corporation. Police have recovered the bag and Rs 20,000 kept in it from the accused. Accused has served jail term earlier After being caught, the accused started apologizing to the police. During police interrogation, it was revealed that he is also a sanitation worker in the municipal corporation. He has been to jail in a case before as well. The accused has been identified as Vikky Bansfor, a resident of Humayunpur in Gorakhnath police station area. Railway employee was going home after withdrawing pension money According to information, Ramsati, a resident of Jungle Sikri in Khorabar police station area, filed a case. He told the police that he was a letter carrier for the Railway General Manager. He retired in the year 2010. On the morning of April 6 at 10:45 AM, he had withdrawn 20 thousand rupees of pension from SBI located opposite the Railway GM office. He was walking on foot after putting the money in a bag. When he reached near the Railway office gate, a person came from behind and said that you smuggle ganja. Claiming to be a police inspector, he took the bag in the name of checking and fled with the money. Accused caught within four hours The victim had informed the police about the incident. Cantt police registered a case and started investigation with the help of CCTV cameras installed nearby. After identifying the accused in the investigation, the team of Railway Chowki In-charge Amit Chaube arrested him. The police recovered 20 thousand rupees from the accused. Railway outpost in-charge Amit Chaube said that information about the incident was received on Monday. After this, the accused was immediately identified through CCTV camera. Within four hours, the accused was searched and caught. After interrogation, 20 thousand rupees along with the bag were recovered from him on Tuesday.

stories.title: Storms, rain lash UP, 20-foot road stretch collapses in Muzaffarnagar:Tree falls on moving bus in Barabanki; rain strikes over 20 districts, including Lucknow
stories.summary: Unseasonal rain and storms continue to batter Uttar Pradesh, with no immediate relief in sight. On Wednesday morning, strong winds accompanied rainfall in five districts, including Lucknow. Late at night in the capital, a tree collapsed onto a car. The driver, who was inside the vehicle, narrowly escaped unhurt, though the car was completely damaged. The Meteorological Department has issued a rain alert for 48 districts and a hailstorm warning for nine districts. Wind speeds during this period may reach up to 60 km per hour. According to the department, sudden weather changes are being caused by an active western disturbance. On Tuesday, storms and rain were reported in 15 districts, including Agra and Mathura. In Badaun, daytime turned unusually dark due to dense cloud cover. In Agra, strong winds caused the gate of a marriage hall to collapse, burying an auto beneath it. In Hathras, more than 10 trees were uprooted. Jalaun recorded the highest temperature in the state at 37.4°C. Atul Singh, meteorological scientist of Lucknow, said- "The effect of the western disturbance will end from tomorrow. But a new disturbance has become active from April 11. After this, the weather is likely to deteriorate again. There will be rain with strong winds and the temperature will drop by 3 to 5 degrees." Temperature dropped 4-5 °C due to rain The average temperature of the state has dropped by 4-5 °C due to rain and strong winds. Speaking of the last 4 days, it rained in 43 districts, including Varanasi-Kanpur. Hailstorms occurred in 10 cities, including Mathura, Sambhal, and Jalaun. 15 people have died due to storms and lightning strikes. What will the weather be like for the next 3 days?

stories.title: 'Will my prepaid meter automatically become postpaid?':Prepaid smart metre mandate removed on new connections
stories.summary: The mandatory requirement for prepaid smart meters when getting a new electricity connection in UP has been removed. This means when getting a new electricity connection, you will have to specify whether you want a prepaid smart meter or a postpaid smart meter. The Central Electricity Authority (CEA) has issued this order. Electricity companies will not be able to install prepaid meters at their discretion, nor will they be able to pressure you to do so. CEA amended its 4-year-old order on 1 April. This order will be applicable across the country. This has provided relief to 70 lakh consumers in UP. But what exactly are smart prepaid and postpaid meters? Why did CEA have to change the order? What problems were common to people with prepaid meters? Which is more beneficial between smart prepaid and postpaid meters? Read in the explainer... Question 1. What is the difference between prepaid and postpaid smart meters? Answer. This is exactly like the prepaid and postpaid versions of your mobile SIM. Just as you have to recharge first to use a prepaid SIM. Only after that can you make calls or send messages. All services stop when the balance runs out. Similarly, in a prepaid smart meter, you have to recharge first. As soon as the recharge runs out, the electricity gets cut off. You can see real-time electricity consumption, balance, etc., through the smart meter app. No security money needs to be deposited for this meter either. On the other hand, in a postpaid smart meter, the bill comes at the end of the month. You can see daily electricity consumption on the smart meter app. However, payment has to be made only when the bill is issued. For such connections, ₹2K has to be deposited as security. Question 2. What order did the authority issue 4 years ago? Answer. The authority had stated in its 2022 order that prepaid smart meters must be installed compulsorily at the homes of those taking new connections. However, Section 47(5) of the Electricity Act-2003 gives consumers the option to choose prepaid or postpaid smart meters according to their convenience. According to Avdhesh Verma, President of UP Consumer Council, the authority's notification was a direct violation of the Act. This is why there was opposition to it across the country. Now the authority has amended this order and given people the right to choose prepaid or postpaid smart meters. Question 3. What benefit will 70 lakh consumers get? Answer. UP Power Corporation has installed 75 lakh smart meters in the state so far. Of these, 70 lakh were postpaid, and 5 lakh were prepaid meters. After the 2022 order, electricity companies converted old postpaid meters to prepaid meters without the consent of consumers. The security deposit of 2 thousand rupees that was paid while installing postpaid meters was converted into a recharge balance. Consumers were informed about this through messages. When the balance ran out, people's household electricity was automatically cut off. The problem increased further when electricity did not resume even after recharging. This happened with more than 5 lakh consumers. After the change in the authority's order, companies will now have to convert the connections of all 70 lakh consumers back to postpaid. Question 4. What needs to be done to convert prepaid meter to postpaid? Answer. According to UP Consumer Council President Avdhesh Verma, to convert your prepaid smart meter to postpaid, you will have to submit an application to the XEN (Executive Engineer) of your area. Along with this, you will also have to attach a reference to the Central Electricity Authority's notification or its photocopy. A security deposit of 2 thousand rupees will also have to be paid in lieu of the postpaid smart meter. Question 5. What to do if the electricity company does not convert to postpaid? Answer. Under Section 47(5) of the Electricity Act 2003, you can file a complaint with the Consumer Forum, UP Electricity Regulatory Commission. According to UP Consumer Council Chairman Avdhesh Verma, they are y to provide full assistance to such consumers. Question 6. What should one do if the department pressures to install a prepaid meter on a new connection? Answer. If an electricity department employee pressures you to install a prepaid meter when getting a new electricity connection, you can file a complaint against them at your police station. Section 47(5) of the Electricity Act gives consumers the option to choose between prepaid or postpaid smart meters according to their convenience. Violating this will be considered an infringement of individual freedom. Question 7. What exactly is the problem with smart prepaid meters? Answer. Consumer Council President Avdhesh Verma explains - Just as you cannot talk on a mobile when the balance runs out, smart meters function the same way. When you recharge your mobile, conversation starts immediately, but this doesn't happen with prepaid meters. People recharged after their balance finished, but their electricity didn't resume. It took anywhere from 2-4 hours to 2-4 days for the electricity to be restored. This happened to approximately 5 lakh consumers. People were forced to make rounds of offices to get their electricity restored. The electricity helpline number was flooded with such complaints. The reason behind this came to light when it was discovered that the Meter Management System (MDM), Head End System (HES), and Revenue Management System (RMS) of the Power Corporation that operates the smart meters were not able to connect with each other. Question 8. How do MDM, HES and RMS control the smart meter? Answer. Meter Management System (MDM) is the software for smart meters. Data from smart meters, such as how much electricity was consumed, when it was consumed, and load, etc., is stored in it. Based on this data, MDM prepares the bill. Then it gives a report to the company. Common people can see electricity consumption data, balance alerts, recharge history, etc. through this. Head End System (HES) is the bridge between smart meters and MDM. It takes data from smart meters through the network. It sends commands to the meter for recharge updates, disconnection, or connection. When consumers recharge through the app, HES updates the balance in the meter. Revenue Management System (RMS) is operated by the Power Corporation. Billing, payment, recharge, disconnection-reconnection - everything is handled by RMS. If, for some reason, the HES-MDM communication breaks down, then the recharge does not get updated. In such a case, the meter remains off. The problem faced by 5 lakh consumers in the state happened due to this reason. Question 9. What is being done to fix this prepaid meter glitch? Answer. Power Corporation companies have updated the RMS system software to fix this technical glitch. For this, the RMS system was kept shut down for 16 hours. Meanwhile, the update of HES and MDM lies with the private companies installing smart meters. They are also working on their software and hardware. According to experts, this happened due to Chinese hardware and software installed in smart meters, whereas there was a ban on installing such smart meters. Power Corporation Chairman Dr. Ashish Goyal has given instructions to remove these shortcomings.

stories.title: School bus carrying 35 children overturns, 10 injured:Family members surround principal's office and raise slogans
stories.summary: A school bus carrying 35 school children overturned in Meerut on Wednesday morning at 7:30 AM. More than 10 children were injured in the accident. Chaos ensued at the scene after the incident. People present nearby rushed to help. They broke the windows to pull the children out. Several children were trapped between the seats. The injured children were admitted to SDS Global Hospital by bike and ambulance. According to doctors, most children sustained minor injuries. The bus belonged to St. Mary Academy. The accident occurred on the road near the Kali River. School bags and books were seen scattered at the scene. The children panicked after the accident. Many children started crying loudly together. People from the surrounding area somehow calmed the children and informed their families. As soon as they received the information, several parents reached the hospital and school. Family members surrounded the principal's office and raised slogans. Police say the causes of the accident are being investigated. The driver fled from the spot; he will soon be arrested.
