stories.title: Mastermind linked to 400 crimes hides underwater for 5 hours:Uses lotus stem to breathe; escaped after purse snatch in AC coach
stories.summary: A dramatic, film-like sequence unfolded in Jabalpur on Tuesday evening when police chased a cunning interstate thief who tried to evade arrest by jumping into a deep, moss-covered pond near Khitoula railway station. Taking advantage of darkness and thick algae, he disappeared from sight and remained hidden underwater for nearly five hours. In a shocking twist, the accused managed to breathe by using a hollow lotus stem as a makeshift pipe. When Khitoula police and divers began the rescue operation, they found no trace of him on the surface. He had completely submerged himself underwater, using the lotus stalk for oxygen. After nearly five hours of continuous search, divers finally located and caught him from beneath the algae. Completely submerged, survived using Lotus Stalk The incident began on the Rewa–Itwari Express train, where the accused attempted to snatch a woman’s purse in an AC coach. He was spotted by RPF personnel. As the train slowed near Sihora Road railway station, he pulled the chain, jumped off, and fled. RPF personnel chased him, but he ran towards a nearby pond and jumped in to hide. Old photograph reveals true identity After his arrest, Harvinder Singh tried to mislead police by giving his name as Bablu and claiming he was from Chandigarh. However, RPF Station Incharge Rajiv Kharb grew suspicious and recalled a photo of a wanted thief saved on his phone in 2018. As soon as he addressed the accused by his old alias “Sunny,” Singh was stunned and revealed his real identity. Past crimes and political background Investigations revealed that 32-year-old Harvinder Singh, a resident of Bijnor in Uttar Pradesh, has carried out more than 400 thefts across the country, shocking police officials. He had also served as an independent ward councillor from Haldaur Nagar Nikay in Bijnor in 2017. In 2018, Vijayawada police arrested him and recovered diamonds and jewellery worth ₹70 lakh. He had also stolen a licensed pistol and cash from a passenger on the Avantika Express. He typically targeted AC coaches, travelled without tickets, and hid in train bathrooms to avoid ticket examiners. Nationwide manhunt Cases against Harvinder Singh are registered in multiple states, including Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh and Mumbai. He frequently changed SIM cards after each crime and never carried identification documents. Following his arrest, police from several states have started arriving for questioning, while Jabalpur police and RPF continue to interrogate him about other offences and his wider network.

stories.title: Kanpur kidney racket - Agent claims of facilitating 50 transplants:Receives ₹50,000 per case; Delhi's renowned hospital name surfaces
stories.summary: In Kanpur's kidney scandal, police interrogated agent Shivam Agarwal alias Kada on Tuesday. During this, Shivam confessed to facilitating 50 kidney transplants. He revealed that he received ₹50K for each operation. In the interrogation that lasted about 2 hours, he was asked 15 questions. He gave evasive answers to most questions. DCP West SM Kasim Abidi said, Shivam is not cooperating in the interrogation. He will soon be taken into police custody, and then a detailed interrogation will be conducted. Police have found a call recording from Shivam's mobile. In this, Shivam can be heard talking to Delhi NCR agent Naveen Pandey. The recording is from after the death of a patient during a kidney transplant. In the 1 minute 36 second recording, Shivam is telling Naveen that Rohit sir (absconding accused doctor) has asked to remain silent. Police claim that the name of Max Hospital in Delhi has also surfaced in the audio. Police will send a notice and seek a response from the hospital. Additionally, police have arrested Dr. Afzal's driver, Parvez Saifi. A total of 10 arrests have been made in the case so far. First, read the conversation between Shivam and Naveen Shivam: Did you talk to Rohit, sir? Naveen: He picked up the phone, then disconnected it. When I called on WhatsApp, he didn't answer. Shivam: In the morning, he was also telling us to hurry up a bit, Shivam. Saying the message, then said look into it a bit. Stay a bit silent, so we said okay. Naveen: So, what should I do? Should I become silent? Shivam: No, he was telling us. Was saying that keep watching... Whatever it is, we'll see. Going Naveen bhai would be better because, suppose if there's any matter, it will be settled. Naveen: The patient is talking very lovingly. He had just called. He's saying that my patient, who has been admitted to Max, should get him discharged. That's it; otherwise, we will also get trapped, and you will also get trapped. Shivam: So he got admitted to Max? Naveen: Yes, he got admitted. I have talked to the doctor. Shivam: What is the doctor saying? Naveen: Talked to the doctor, he's saying that we are getting him discharged without papers. What's the problem with this? Shivam: Okay, so when he was admitted to MAX, what did they show? Naveen: As soon as they reached, he expired. Shivam: Did he expire in the emergency or after being admitted to the ICU? Naveen: First, he expired, but they took him to the emergency. Shivam: Yes... Naveen: There's some matter, they said to get the discharge done, take him, I'll get it done. Shivam: Did you talk to Rohit, sir? Naveen: I'm not able to reach Rohit, sir. If you can talk to him, tell him to speak with us for a minute. Shivam: We also have the same number. We don't have his other number. Naveen: Okay, if we can talk, we'll see. For now, we're not going. Shivam: Alright. Now know what Shivam told in the interrogation Dr. Rohit used to come to Kanpur for every operation In a police interrogation, agent Shivam Agarwal said that Dr. Rohit had sent the African woman Arabica. He had called and said that an African woman was coming to Kanpur for a kidney transplant. Arrange a hotel and a hospital for her. Arrangements were made at Ahuja Hospital for the transplant. Shivam revealed that Rohit met Arabica in Delhi itself. Dr. Rohit used to come to Kanpur for every operation. He had also come during Arabica's transplant. Around 50 transplants have been conducted in Kanpur with him. Dr. Rohit and Dr. Afzal had also come to Kanpur for Parul Tomar's transplant and stayed for about 8-10 days. Used to get ₹50 thousand per operation Shivam also revealed that Rohit used to talk from different numbers. I didn't know them properly. My responsibility was to provide them with the hospital. I used to get ₹50 thousand for every operation. Shivam told about the woman's death at Medi Life Hospital, that she had also come through Rohit. Suddenly, her health deteriorated. On Rohit's advice, she was referred to Max Hospital. She died before reaching there. About agent Naveen Pandey, Shivam said that he is an agent from Delhi NCR and is close to Dr. Rohit. Police found several folders in Shivam's mobile which were password-protected. When asked about the password, he said that the folder has a pattern lock. Only he can open it. Each team had a different task DCP West said, the investigation so far has revealed that Dr. Rohit's job was to divide teams for kidney transplants. The job of Dr. Afzal and Dr. Ali from Meerut was to arrange donors and receivers. Parvez Saifi and Firoz's job was to arrange vehicles, while Shivam and Naveen's job was to manage the hospital. 10th accused Parvez Saifi also arrested Police arrested Dr. Afzal's driver, Parvez Saifi, on Tuesday night. ₹10 lakh has also been recovered from him. He will be presented in court on Wednesday. During interrogation, Saifi revealed that this is the same money that was received after the operation of Parul Tomar from Muzaffarnagar. Dr. Afzal had received ₹22 lakh, out of which he had given ₹10 lakh to Parvez Saifi. Parvez said that after the police raided Ahuja Hospital, Dr. Afzal's mobile was switched off. Saifi had ₹10 lakh, so he was meeting with lawyers to save himself. One lawyer had also assured him of getting anticipatory bail. After this, he took the money and came from Meerut to Kanpur. According to DCP SM Kasim Abidi, when Saifi switched on his mobile to talk to the lawyer, the police got his location. Within 15 minutes of getting the location, Rawatpur police station nabbed him. Came into discussion after video went viral A 19-second video related to the kidney scam had gone viral on April 5. In it, Dr. Afzal was present with Saifi at a hotel in Kalyanpur. The video showed that several bundles of ₹500 notes were spread on the bed, and Afzal was picking up one bundle and fanning his face with it. Parvez Saifi, present in the room, was making a video with his mobile. After some time, Saifi also appears in the video. The video is from after Parul Tomar's transplant. Since the video surfaced, the police had been after Saifi. Parvez Saifi has been to jail for robbery and dacoity According to the DCP, Parvez Saifi is a driver by profession, but is also a criminal. He works for a travel agency. 7-8 criminal cases are registered against him in Meerut and Ghaziabad. He has also spent about two and a half years in jail in a robbery case in Ghaziabad. Parvez Saifi used to bring and take doctors and OT technicians associated with the kidney racket to Kanpur. During interrogation, Saifi revealed that he had brought Dr. Afzal to Kanpur for 7 operations conducted at Ahuja Hospital. During this time, they stayed at a hotel in Kalyanpur for 8-10 days. It was there that the video with the money was made. Clinic-home locked, Dr. Afzal absconding According to the DCP, Meerut's Dr. Afzal has absconded after locking his clinic and home. Along with him, Mudassar Ali Siddiqui, alias Dr. Ali, Dr. Amit, who runs a multi-speciality hospital in Meerut, and dentist Dr. Vaibhav Mudgal are also absconding. Teams are conducting raids to search for them. Police unsuccessful in tracing donors and recipients The police have not yet been able to trace the donors and recipients caught in the kidney racket. The police tried to trace them through samples sent to labs for testing and reports from hospitals linked to the kidney racket, but nothing substantial was found. DCP West SM Kasim Abidi stated that data has been obtained from several labs, but due to the lack of information on sample slips beyond the patient's name and age, there is difficulty in tracing the donors and recipients.

stories.title: SP MP Akshay Yadav defends ‘dynasty politics’:Outlines party's strategy for 2028 MP polls
stories.summary: The Samajwadi Party (SP) has intensified its preparations for the next assembly elections in Madhya Pradesh. Party chief Akhilesh Yadav has appointed three in-charges to strengthen the organisation in the state. These include Firozabad MP Akshay Yadav, Etah MP Devesh Shakya, and former state president and ex-MP Gauri Singh Yadav. All three leaders arrived in Bhopal for the first time as part of this initiative. Akhilesh Yadav’s cousin, Akshay Yadav, along with Devesh Shakya, spoke to Dainik Bhaskar about the party’s strategy and plans. Read conversation with MP Akshay Yadav In Uttar Pradesh, SP contested elections in alliance and achieved success. Will you ally Madhya Pradesh as well? There is still considerable time before the elections. We have come to Madhya Pradesh to explore how the Samajwadi Party can contest independently and form a government here. Our focus will be on strengthening the organisation, including the executive and office bearers. How much time will Akhilesh Yadav devote to Madhya Pradesh? Assembly elections are scheduled in Uttar Pradesh next year, so he will remain occupied there for now. After those elections, he will dedicate time to Madhya Pradesh. Meanwhile, as his representatives, I, along with Devesh ji and Gauri ji, will work to strengthen the organisation. A robbery case involving ₹35,000 was registered against Meera Yadav, a former SP MLA from Niwari. What is your response? Wherever the BJP is in power, it attempts to defame opponents by filing false cases. When the matter reaches court, the truth will emerge. Will there be greater focus on border areas where SP has influence? At present, our priority is organisational strengthening. We will contest the elections in Madhya Pradesh with full strength. Workers in border areas connected to Uttar Pradesh will support efforts here, and similarly, workers from Madhya Pradesh will assist in Uttar Pradesh elections. What will be SP’s role in next year’s urban local body elections in MP? Our immediate focus remains on strengthening the party. Once that is achieved, the party will decide whether to contest local body elections, and if it does, it will participate with full force. 'The BJP works to divide people, while we aim to unite them. We want children to receive quality education and employment opportunities. No one should face injustice, we will fight for this.” BJP leaders often accuse SP of dynastic politics. How do you respond? When we look at legislative assemblies, we see individuals from political families across all parties. If a doctor’s child becomes a doctor or an engineer’s child becomes an engineer, why should it be questioned when someone from a political family enters politics? Ultimately, it is the public who elects them, so such allegations are misplaced. BJP replaced Shivraj Singh with Mohan Yadav as Chief Minister in MP. How do you assess his performance? The expected level of governance is not being delivered. For instance, there have been delays in finalising crop procurement dates. This indicates shortcomings in leadership. What are your expectations for elections in five states, including Assam and West Bengal? I believe these elections are about change, and the BJP will face defeat everywhere. Read the conversation with Etah MP Devesh Shakya What preparations are being made to strengthen the organisation in Madhya Pradesh? Under the guidance of our national president Akhilesh Yadav, we have come to further strengthen the organisation in the state. We aim to connect with grassroots workers so that the party can benefit in the upcoming elections. Akhilesh Yadav has given the slogan of PDA. Do you think these sections will support you? PDA is not limited to a category. It includes backward classes, Dalits, minorities, and all those who feel oppressed or marginalised. The Samajwadi Party stands with them. At one point, SP had eight MLAs in MP, but now it has none. What is your strategy to improve this? We will focus on strengthening the organisation to rebuild our base. Through a strong organisational structure, we aim to win as many seats as possible. SP influences regions like Vindhya, Bundelkhand and Chambal. Why do candidates from Uttar Pradesh contest here? This time, our effort will be to field candidates who are preferred by the local public and who have the capacity to win. With elections due in Uttar Pradesh next year, how much time will you dedicate to Madhya Pradesh? As an in-charge, my priority will be to assign responsibilities within the organisation and regularly review their implementation. This will ensure that by the time elections arrive, our organisational structure is strong at the grassroots level.

stories.title: OP Rajbhar to consolidate 110 seats through Raja Suheldev's fair:Plan to unite three castes; Gazi Miyan fair was earlier held in Bahraich
stories.summary: "The time has come to give Bahraich its true identity. Until now, we have been reading false history. For the vote bank of a particular community, a foreign invader was glorified, and a fair was organized at his shrine." This is the statement of UP Cabinet Minister and Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party (SBSP) chief Om Prakash Rajbhar. Actually, this year, a fair is to be organized in Bahraich from 10 June in memory of Maharaja Suheldev. Until now, a fair has taking place at the shrine of Syed Salar Masud, the commander of Mahmud of Ghazni. However, last year the administration did not allow it. According to historians, Salar Masud was killed on 10 June 1034 in a battle with Maharaja Suheldev. There are preparations to invite CM Yogi Adityanath to the fair. But this matter is not so straightforward either. Through one fair, the BJP and its ally party, SBSP, want to bring three castes into their fold. The question is, how can three castes be won over by organizing a fair? Will the fair be held at the shrine this time or not? What are the preparations for the 10 June fair? Read the special report First, understand the politics of the fair Can impact 110 assembly seats The Rajbhar community has only a 3-4 percent vote bank in the state. However, they are considered to play a decisive role in 40 to 60 assembly seats. The Rajbhar community considers Maharaja Suheldev as their hero. In this context, by organizing a fair in his memory, Om Prakash Rajbhar is trying to strengthen this very vote bank. Similarly, in the Dalit category, the Pasi community's share is considered to be around 15 percent. They influence around 50 seats. Both BJP and the SP have a hold on this community. BJP is working on a strategy to woo the Pasi community through the fair. Meanwhile, the Rajput community is already considered to be in support of the BJP. In this context, this fair is being seen as an attempt to connect with three major castes. Maharaja Suheldev; Hero of Pasis, Rajbhars, and Kshatriyas Different claims have been made in history regarding Maharaja Suheldev. The Kshatriya community considers him to be from the Suryavanshi lineage. Due to this, people from the Kshatriya community have been participating in large numbers in his victory celebrations. The Pasi community also considers the Maharaja as their own. Om Prakash Rajbhar calls him 'Rajbhar Maharaj Suheldev'. Rajbhar claims that he was the most valiant among the 165 Rajbhar kings of that time. There have been differences of opinion about this in history as well. It is believed that they were the sons of King Haridev (or Mangaldhwaj) of Shravasti. Their elder brother, Malladev, was martyred while protecting a temple. After this, Suheldev defeated Salar Masud by taking along local Hindu kings, Rajbhar, Pasi, and Rajput commanders. This is why many caste groups worship Maharaja Suheldev as a hero of their community. Senior journalist Suresh Bahadur Singh says, ‘There is deep reverence for Maharaja Suheldev in the Rajbhar, Pasi, and Rajput communities’. Syed Salar Ghazi is considered a foreign invader. In such a situation, this fair is being considered politically favorable for BJP and Suhelpa. There is a possibility of direct benefit to NDA from this. Administration stopped the fair at Ghazi Miyan's dargah last year The grave of Syed Salar Masud (Ghazi Miyan) is located in the Bankutha area of Bahraich city. He was a commander of the 11th-century invader Mahmud Ghaznavi. He was killed in battle with Raja Suheldev. About 500 years ago, the annual Jeth fair started by portraying Masud as a Sufi saint. This fair used to start from the first Sunday of the month of Jyeshtha according to the Hindu calendar and continue for about a month. Apart from the country, a large number of Muslim and Hindu devotees from Nepal used to participate in the fair. Besides this, people keep visiting here throughout the year. The dargah complex has a mosque, library, and shops. Last year, the government did not give permission to hold the fair due to security reasons. 10-day fair to be held at Maharaja Suheldev Memorial About 8 km away from the dargah, near Chittaura village on Gonda Road, there is a memorial of Maharaja Suheldev spread over 84 bighas. Near Chittaura Lake, the Maharaja defeated the invader Syed Salar Masud and his army on 10 June, 1034. This is why people of the area celebrate Vijayotsav on 10 June. In February 2021, Prime Minister Narendra Modi laid the foundation stone of this memorial. On 10 June, 2025, CM Yogi unveiled a 40-foot-tall bronze statue of Maharaja Suheldev mounted on a horse. This year, a fair will be held here from 10 to 19 June. Now read what OP Rajbhar said Salar Masud was killed after a 17-day war Subhaspa chief Omprakash Rajbhar explains that Salar Masud was a foreign invader who came from Afghanistan. At the time of his invasion, there were 585 kings in the country. There were 165 Rajbhar kings in Bahraich and the surrounding areas. Among them, King Suheldev was the most valiant. He gathered the kings from the surrounding areas. He fought against Salar Masud near the Nanpara field of Bahraich. After 17 days of war, on 10 June, 1034, Salar Masud was defeated on the banks of the Kotla River (Chittora Lake). Historians forgot the brave warrior Maharaja Suheldev. They glorified an invader. During British rule, a dargah was built on his grave, portraying him as a Sufi saint. A fair began to be held for a month every year. Suheldev's bravery is mentioned in Ain-e-Akbari Rajbhar explains that the story of Maharaja Suheldev's bravery is in the book Mirat-e-Masudi by 17th-century Persian historian Abdur Rahman Chishti. It contains a detailed mention of Raja Suheldev, along with the biography of Syed Salar Masud. Maharaja Suheldev's bravery is also mentioned in Ain-e-Akbari. Similarly, this incident is also mentioned in British-era district gazetteers and local folklore. Unfortunately, after independence, we began worshipping a foreign invader. Along with Muslims, a large number of Hindus also began offering chadars at his grave. The valor of the Maharaja had been forgotten in history. Now the government is correcting this. Until now, the Vijayotsav program used to be held for 3 days Yashuvendra Vikram Singh, President of Maharaja Suheldev Memorial Committee, explains that earlier, the Vijayotsav program used to be held for 3 days. Bhagavat Katha or other religious events would be organized in the ancient temple near the memorial. At the conclusion, a guest from the state government would be invited to discuss Maharaja Suheldev's valor. Yashuvendra explains that in 1950-51, his grandfather Raja Virendra Vikram Singh established the trust. 84 bighas of land were donated for the memorial. There are about 500 bighas of land in the name of the trust. This also includes Chittoura Lake. Now, apart from the statue at the memorial site, a new temple has been built. There is also a 200-bed dormitory, a multipurpose hall with a capacity of 250 people, and an open stage. CM says, ‘There should be no fair in the name of Masood’ Yashuvendra Vikram Singh says that CM Yogi had called Salar Masood "the mafia of that time" in Gorakhpur on April 5. The CM had said that the thinking and working style of today's mafia is just like his. There should be no fair in the name of Salar Masood. National heroes should be honored. He says that Maharaja Suheldev defeated Salar Masud and freed the people from slavery. During the war, Suheldev adopted guerrilla tactics to defeat Masud's large army. The Maharaja gave Salar Masud the worst death in Islam. He was tied to a hot iron griddle and burned. This punishment, according to Islam, guarantees sending him to Jahannum (hell). Question 1. Will the Ghazi Miyan fair be held this time? Answer. NOCs from the administration, fire department, and police are necessary to hold the fair. The Dargah Sharif Management Committee has not yet sought permission from the administration for this. Committee President Bakaullah refuses to comment on this. A committee member, speaking on condition of anonymity, said that the fair usually begins around May 21. There is still time for that. Currently, the situation regarding the fair at the dargah is not clear. Contracts are also awarded for arrangements at the fair. However, this time the contract for the fair has not been given. This indicates that organizing the fair this time may also be difficult. Every year in January, a 5-day fair is also held at the dargah. However, this time the administration had given permission for only 2 days, but there was no permission for outside shops. This makes it clear that getting permission for the fair this time also seems difficult. Question 2. Will the HC's order also apply to the Suheldev Memorial? Answer. Last year, when permission for the fair was not granted, the Dargah Sharif Management Committee approached the High Court. At that time, the Lucknow bench of the High Court also did not grant permission for the fair. However, there was no ban on worship. People can go to worship in a normal manner without forming processions. This High Court order is still in effect, and no stay has been obtained on it. The administration is also citing this. Now the question is, when the High Court did not permit the dargah fair, how will permission be granted for the fair at Suheldev Memorial? On this, Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party chief Om Prakash Rajbhar says that there is no restriction on the Suheldev Memorial. The administration has to give permission. The memorial is 8 km away from city, so people coming to the fair will not affect city's traffic.

stories.title: ATS raids Varanasi doctor’s house in terror funding probe:Team questions son, Pakistan links traced
stories.summary: A joint team of the Uttar Pradesh ATS and the Intelligence Bureau raided the house of a doctor in Varanasi on Tuesday afternoon over suspected terror funding. The team stayed at the house for nearly seven hours. Officials seized a mobile phone, laptop and printer from the premises and questioned the doctor’s family members, including his son. Police forces were deployed outside the house during the operation to maintain security. Digital evidence and financial trail under scrutiny Preliminary investigation has revealed transactions worth several lakhs of rupees in the doctor’s bank account. Agencies are examining possible links to individuals in Pakistan and organisations based in Kashmir. Investigators said several suspicious contacts were found saved in the doctor’s phone. Call records, chats and other digital data are being analysed for further leads. See 2 pictures... Son questioned over alleged online contacts The doctor, identified as Dr Arif Ansari, is a paediatrician who runs a local hospital. His 20-year-old son, Abu Bakr, who is preparing for NEET, is also being questioned. Sources said Abu Bakr was allegedly in touch with a Kashmir-based handle through WhatsApp and had communicated with some suspicious individuals, including contacts linked to Pakistan. His electronic devices have also been seized for examination. Heavy police deployment, officials remain tight-lipped As news of the raid spread, a crowd gathered outside the house. Police restricted entry into the lane, allowing only local residents. Senior officers, including ACP Kotwali Vijay Pratap Singh and Adampur Inspector Vimal Kumar Mishra, have not issued any official statement. An ATS officer present at the spot declined to share details, citing the ongoing investigation. Locals express shock, vouch for family Residents in the area described Dr Ansari as a respected and well-behaved person. A local resident said the family has a good reputation and the son is known to be focused on his studies. Many expressed surprise over the development, saying they found it difficult to believe the allegations. Link to Lucknow arrests under investigation The raid is linked to inputs obtained after four suspects were arrested by the ATS near Charbagh railway station in Lucknow on April 10. During interrogation, agencies found possible links between the suspects and Pakistan’s intelligence agency ISI, along with other terror outfits. Investigators believe a wider network involving terror funding may be active across cities such as Mumbai, Lucknow and Varanasi. Based on these inputs, multiple locations are being probed. Agencies are now examining bank transactions, call records and digital evidence to establish the full extent of the network.

stories.title: Ambedkar statue vandalism sparks violence in Lakhimpur:Stone-pelting at police, vehicles smashed; cops allege illegal installation
stories.summary: Tension gripped Uttar Pradesh’s Lakhimpur Kheri on Tuesday evening after a statue of B. R. Ambedkar was allegedly damaged, triggering clashes between villagers and the police in the Bankeganj area. According to officials, an angry crowd gathered in Motipur village under the Gola Gokarnnath police station limits and began pelting stones at police personnel. Several police vehicles were vandalised, and at least one vehicle was overturned during the unrest. Police teams, along with additional forces, were rushed to the spot to bring the situation under control. Authorities said a tense calm prevails in the area, with senior officers deployed and monitoring the situation. See 2 pictures... Dispute over statue installation Villagers alleged that a community feast was underway and a statue of Ambedkar was being installed on land near a Buddhist vihara that had remained vacant for years. After the installation, most men reportedly left for a rally, leaving women at the site. Residents claimed that police, accompanied by a local woman, arrived and removed the statue, during which it was damaged. Some women also alleged that they were subjected to a baton charge when they tried to intervene. Violence escalates, woman assaulted The incident sparked outrage among villagers, who accused local police officials and the woman of triggering the confrontation. In the ensuing chaos, the woman was allegedly assaulted by the crowd before police personnel intervened and escorted her to safety. Officials confirmed that multiple government vehicles, including those used by the Circle Officer (CO) and the tehsildar, were damaged in the violence. Police response Police officials said the statue had been installed without prior permission at a disputed site, and action was taken to remove it. They added that discussions are ongoing between the village head, residents, and officials from the police and revenue departments to defuse tensions. Security remains tight in the area as authorities continue efforts to restore normalcy.

stories.title: Judge who made ‘kathmulla’ remark to retire before impeachment:Case pending in Rajya Sabha for 1.5 years; farewell at Allahabad HC tomorrow
stories.summary: Justice faced criticism over remarks at VHP event; SC had sought clarification Justice Shekhar Kumar Yadav of the Allahabad High Court will retire on Wednesday, April 15, while an impeachment motion against him remains pending in the Rajya Sabha for nearly a year. The motion, however, is expected to lapse automatically after his retirement. Controversy over remarks at VHP event Justice Yadav had attended an event organised by the Vishwa Hindu Parishad’s legal cell in Prayagraj on December 8, 2024. During his speech, he said that India runs according to the wishes of the majority and made remarks referring to “hardline fundamentalists,” which drew sharp criticism. The Supreme Court of India sought clarification from him and reportedly asked him to express regret. Justice Yadav, however, refused, stating that he had said nothing wrong. Impeachment motion: What happens next The impeachment motion was moved in the Rajya Sabha on December 13, 2024, with signatures of 55 opposition MPs, exceeding the required threshold. No action has been taken on it so far. With Justice Yadav retiring before proceedings could begin, the motion will become null and void. Full court reference scheduled A full court reference will be held at the Allahabad High Court on Wednesday at 3:45 PM in the Chief Justice’s courtroom to mark his retirement. Judges, bar association members, and registry officials will attend the ceremony. Justice Yadav was appointed as an additional judge on December 12, 2019, and became a permanent judge on March 26, 2021. Former CJI’s remark on judicial conduct Former Chief Justice of India D Y Chandrachud had emphasised that judges must be cautious in their public statements, noting that remarks should not create an impression of bias in the judiciary. stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. Samrat Chaudhary to be Bihar’s new CM, oath ceremony tomorrow Samrat Chaudhary will be the new Chief Minister of Bihar. He has been chosen as the leader of the BJP legislative party. A formal announcement will be made after the NDA meeting. The swearing-in ceremony will take place tomorrow, 15 April, at Lok Bhavan. 2. Noida unrest flares again, stone-pelting at police; heavy force deployed Fresh protests erupted in Noida as factory workers demanding higher wages clashed with police, pelting stones at multiple locations. Over 300 arrests were made, heavy forces deployed, and surveillance intensified. Rahul Gandhi called the unrest workers’ “last cry” amid escalating tensions. 3. Dalit vote in focus on Ambedkar Jayanti, parties step up outreach On Ambedkar Jayanti, all major parties in Uttar Pradesh reached out to Dalit voters. Mayawati held a show of strength in Lucknow, while BJP, SP and Congress announced schemes and campaigns to win support. 4. Centre plans Lok Sabha expansion to 850 seats The central government on Tuesday, April 14, proposed increasing the number of Lok Sabha seats after the delimitation of constituencies. As per the news agency ANI, the total number of seats will be increased to 850. Out of these, 815 seats will be allocated to the states. 35 seats will be reserved for Union Territories (UTs). 5. UP ATS to probe 26 arson cases over terror link, NIA steps in Uttar Pradesh ATS will re-investigate 26 fire incidents after terror links emerged from arrests in Lucknow. Suspects allegedly filmed arson acts and sent videos to Pakistan-based handlers. National Investigation Agency has issued lookout notices against three accused as the probe widens. 6. Kidney racket busted: Kingpin charged ₹30 lakh, ‘Commando Surgery’ code used in Kanpur hub Police have exposed a kidney racket operating across multiple cities, with the kingpin charging up to ₹30 lakh per transplant. The network used the codeword “Commando Surgery” to avoid detection. Illegal transplants were carried out in Kanpur. Several accused have been arrested. 7. Petrol may become expensive by ₹18 Diesel ₹35 Due to rising crude oil prices, petrol could become expensive by ₹18 and diesel by ₹35 per liter. A report by foreign brokerage firm Macquarie states that despite expensive crude oil, petrol-diesel prices in the country remain stable. 8. Noida film city to benefit Saharanpur populace, says Yogi; ‘those who divide can’t deliver development’ Yogi Adityanath said Saharanpur youth will get opportunities closer to home with the upcoming Noida film city. Addressing an expressway event, he also attacked those “dividing society”, while highlighting improved connectivity and economic boost from the Delhi–Dehradun corridor. 9. Kanpur constable booked for rape, blackmail of MSc student A Kanpur constable has been booked for allegedly raping an MSc student after luring her with job and marriage promises. He filmed obscene videos and threatened to make them viral. FIR registered at Kotwali; police say the accused will be arrested soon. 10. ‘Dhurandhar' becomes first franchise to earn ₹3,000 crore worldwide Ranveer Singh-starrer films Dhurandhar and Dhurandhar 2 have together earned over ₹3,000 crore worldwide, making it the first Indian film franchise to cross the ₹3,000 crore mark.

stories.title: ‘Worship Modi–Yogi, not stones’:BJP MLA criticises idol worship, attacks Dalit leadership at Ambedkar Jayanti event in Hardoi
stories.summary: BJP MLA Shyam Prakash stirred controversy after making remarks on idol worship and Dalit leadership at an Ambedkar Jayanti event in Hardoi. Addressing the gathering, Prakash said, Worshipping stones will get you nothing. If you must worship, then worship Yogi and Modi. From them, you will get something. Criticism of dalit leadership The Gopamau MLA said leaders who speak in the name of Dalits often work for their own interests. “No Dalit leader can ensure your welfare. Big leaders mislead people to secure power,” he said. Read what else the BJP MLA said ‘I have been in all parties’ Prakash added that his views were shaped by political experience. “I have drunk water from every ghat. I have been in all parties and seen everything. You have to establish yourself on your own,” he said. Praise for yogi, modi Praising Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath and Prime Minister Narendra Modi, he said he considers “living people as God” and suggested they have the capacity to help people. Mla calls it personal opinion Responding to questions later, Prakash said the remarks reflected his personal views. He clarified that he was referring to stones kept unnecessarily in homes as family deities.

stories.title: Kanpur constable booked for rape, blackmail of MSc student:Lured victim with job and promise of marriage; filmed obscene videos of her
stories.summary: A constable in Kanpur has been booked for allegedly raping an MSc student after luring her with promises of a job and marriage, police said. The accused also filmed obscene photos and videos and later threatened to make them viral. FIR registered after complaint at Kotwali The student approached Kotwali police station late Monday night. Based on her complaint, an FIR has been registered against constable Yogendra Singh, who is posted at the Reserve Police Lines. Met on train, built trust with false assurances According to the victim, she met Yogendra on January 19, 2026, while travelling from Kanpur Central to Agra for an exam. During the journey, he claimed to be undergoing constable training and offered to help her get a job. The two exchanged numbers and stayed in touch. She alleged that Yogendra later proposed marriage and even spoke to her mother, assuring both a job and marriage. Assault, repeated threats over two months The student alleged that on February 22, the constable called her near the Reserve Police Lines and raped her. During the assault, he recorded obscene photos and videos. She said he continued to sexually assault her for nearly two months by threatening to leak the videos. On April 8, he allegedly raped her again and refused to marry or help her with a job, while repeating threats to make the videos viral. Police action underway Kotwali station in-charge Jagdish Prasad Pandey said an FIR has been registered and efforts are underway to arrest the accused. “He will be arrested and sent to jail soon,” he said.

stories.title: Kidney racket kingpin charged ₹30 lakh per transplant:‘Commando Surgery’ codeword used, Kanpur hub of illegal network
stories.summary: The alleged mastermind of the Kanpur kidney racket, Rohit Tiwari, has revealed key details during police interrogation, exposing how an organised network carried out illegal kidney transplants across multiple cities. ₹25–30 lakh per transplant, agents handled deals Police said Rohit charged between ₹25 lakh and ₹30 lakh for each transplant. He told investigators that agents arranged donors and recipients, while he managed hospitals and medical teams. The gang used the codeword “Commando Surgery” to refer to kidney transplants in conversations. Agents active across major cities The network included agents operating in Delhi, Mumbai, Kanpur, Prayagraj and Meerut. These agents brought cases to Rohit, who then decided the hospital, timing, and medical team for each operation. From factory worker to racket operator Rohit, a Class 12 pass from Hardoi, initially worked as a labourer in Ghaziabad. He later became a receptionist at a clinic in Meerut, where he came in contact with doctors linked to illegal transplant work. He then worked as a ward boy and gradually became involved in managing transplants. Kanpur hub identified for illegal surgeries After a dispute between two doctors, Rohit was given responsibility to arrange transplants in Kanpur. He identified Kalyanpur as a location where such operations could be conducted with ease. Over 30 transplants, multiple hospitals involved Police said several transplants were carried out at different hospitals, with more than 10 at one facility alone. Rohit claimed he had conducted over 30 transplants in Kanpur and nearby districts. Dedicated team handled surgeries Interrogation revealed that a team of five to six people carried out the procedures. Some handled anaesthesia, while others performed the transplant. The team would arrive, complete the surgery, and leave immediately. Donors found through Telegram, no direct contact Rohit said he avoided direct interaction with patients. Agents handled negotiations, while he used platforms like Telegram to find donors. He also managed logistics, including operation theatre preparation and scheduling. Large payments and spending trail In one case, a transplant deal was fixed at ₹60 lakh, out of which Rohit received ₹30 lakh. He used the money to pay team members and cover expenses. Police said he spent significant amounts on travel after such operations. Deaths and foreign patient under probe Investigators are also examining cases involving a foreign national and a patient who died after complications following surgery. Arrests made, search on for others Police tracked Rohit through his girlfriend after he went into hiding and destroyed his phones. Several accused, including doctors and associates, have been arrested. Raids are ongoing to trace other suspects. Rohit will be taken on remand for further questioning.

stories.title: Yogi unveils Noida film city plan:UP CM says Saharanpur youth won’t need to migrate; slams ‘divisive politics’
stories.summary: Travel between Delhi and Dehradun will now be completed in just two-and-a-half hours, significantly reducing travel time and boosting connectivity in western Uttar Pradesh, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath said on Tuesday. He was addressing a gathering in Saharanpur on the occasion of the inauguration of the Delhi–Dehradun Expressway. A 135-kilometre stretch of the corridor passes through Uttar Pradesh. Prime Minister Narendra Modi travelled to Dehradun to formally inaugurate the project. Before that, the Prime Minister held a roadshow in Saharanpur, offered prayers at Maa Daat Kali temple, and inspected the wildlife corridor via helicopter. Governor Anandiben Patel, CM Yogi Adityanath, and Deputy Chief Ministers Keshav Prasad Maurya and Brajesh Pathak were also present. After the events in Saharanpur, the Prime Minister left for Dehradun, while CM Yogi and other leaders stayed back and watched the inauguration programme live from the venue. UP emerging as a hub of employment and security Addressing the gathering, Yogi said Uttar Pradesh has emerged as a new centre of employment, security, and investment under the “double-engine government”. He also noted that the day marked the 135th birth anniversary of Dr B R Ambedkar, who ensured equal rights for citizens through the Constitution. The Chief Minister announced that statues of social reformers such as Babasaheb Ambedkar, Ravidas Maharaj, and Maharishi Valmiki would be provided with protective canopies by the state government. Boost to western UP economy Yogi said the corridor would prove beneficial for districts such as Shamli, Muzaffarnagar, Meerut, and Baghpat, helping local products gain wider recognition. He added that the improved connectivity would enable farmers and producers to access not only the national capital but also international markets. Political remarks without naming opposition Without naming any party, Yogi criticised those who “divide society on the basis of caste and family”, saying such forces cannot deliver development. He added that those who encouraged mafias and unrest in the past cannot be expected to provide employment or progress. Key features of the expressway The 213-kilometre Delhi–Dehradun Economic Corridor has been built at a cost of around ₹12,000 crore. Once operational, it will reduce travel time between the two cities from over six hours to about 2.5 hours. The project includes: Advanced traffic management systems A 12-kilometre elevated wildlife corridor — among the longest in Asia — has also been constructed to ensure safe animal movement and reduce human-wildlife conflict. Additionally, the expressway features multiple animal passes, elephant underpasses, and a 370-metre tunnel near the Daat Kali temple. Security and arrangements Ahead of the Prime Minister’s visit, elaborate security arrangements were made, with over 3,000 personnel deployed. The temple premises were decorated with flowers brought from Vrindavan and West Bengal, and special पूजा arrangements were made. The project is designed with a strong focus on environmental sustainability, incorporating measures to minimise ecological disruption while improving infrastructure.

stories.summary: UP Politics: डॉ. भीमराव आंबेडकर की 135वीं जयंती (14 अप्रैल 2026) पर उत्तर प्रदेश की सियासत गरम हो गई है। बहुजन समाज पार्टी ने लखनऊ में भव्य शक्ति प्रदर्शन की तैयारी की है। समाजवादी पार्टी और भाजपा भी बड़े कार्यक्रम आयोजित कर रही हैं। 2027 के विधानसभा चुनाव से ठीक पहले बाबा साहेब की जयंती क्यों अचानक इतनी अहम हो गई? इसका जवाब है, 21 फीसदी दलित वोट बैंक। यह वोट बैंक सीएम कुर्सी का गेमचेंजर साबित होता है। उत्तर प्रदेश में कुल 403 विधानसभा सीटें हैं। इनमें 84 सीटें अनुसूचित जाति के लिए आरक्षित हैं। दलित आबादी राज्य की कुल जनसंख्या का करीब 21 फीसदी है, यानी लगभग 3.20 करोड़ वोटर। ये वोट सिर्फ आरक्षित सीटों पर ही नहीं, बल्कि 150 से ज्यादा सामान्य सीटों पर भी निर्णायक हैं। पूर्वांचल और बुंदेलखंड में कई सीटों पर दलित वोटर 30 फीसदी से ज्यादा हैं। अगर दलित वोट एक तरफ हो जाए, तो 80-100 सीटें सीधे प्रभावित होती हैं।

stories.title: Sara Ali Khan explores snow-covered hills in Uttarakhand’s Tehri:Walks 18 km, camps overnight in remote area
stories.summary: Bollywood actress Sara Ali Khan trekked in the snowy hills of Uttarakhand. She walked 18 kilometers in Tehri. She witnessed snowfall and beautiful valleys in Panwali Kantha Bugyal. She spent the night in a tent amidst heavy snowfall. She enjoyed local mountain food, spending time with the locals. Trekker Kuldeep Rawat informed that Sara Ali Khan arrived in Ghuttu, Tehri on April 11. She stayed here for 3 days and left on Monday, April 13. Sara started an approximately 18-kilometer long trek from Gwana village. This trek passes through natural beauty, dense forests, and high mountains. He mentioned that during the trek, Sara spent the night at a place called Dophan. There are no hotel or restaurant facilities in this area. Because of this, Sara spent the night staying in a tent. Sara spent time with the local people. She got to know the mountain culture up close. While returning, she said - "It is always beautiful to come to Uttarakhand. It is very beautiful. Coming here is very exciting and peaceful. I will come here again." See Pictures- Sara enjoyed trekking through dense forests and high mountains. She relished the natural beauty. Sara ate red rice, Mandua roti, and Lingdi vegetable Sara visited Rudranath Dham in October Sara Ali Khan visited Rudranath Dham, the fourth Kedar located in Chamoli, in October before its gates closed. During this time, Sara walked 20 kilometers to reach the temple. Sara started her journey from Gangol village in Gopeshwar, Chamoli. After that, a day later, she reached Lwinti Bugyal, where after an overnight stay, she resumed trekking and then reached Rudranath Baba's temple. Throughout this entire journey, Sara passed through many rocky and narrow paths, and in between, she met many local villagers who were very happy to see Sara. Sara Ali Khan stopped at hut-like dhabas during trekking, drank tea, and conversed with local people. She learned about the religious beliefs, folk life, and traditional cuisines of the place. The actress was greatly impressed by the natural beauty of the mountains and the rural culture, calling it a memorable experience. Sara Ali Khan has visited Kedarnath many times Sara Ali Khan has a special connection with Kedarnath Dham. After the making of the film 'Kedarnath', she has visited the shrine many times for darshan and has been performing puja without any hindrance so far. However, after the proposed new system is implemented, she may also have to follow the prescribed procedure like other devotees. Sara's first spiritual and professional connection with Kedarnath happened in 2017 during the shooting of her debut film 'Kedarnath'. Since then, she has been continuously visiting here. In October 2024, just before Diwali, she performed puja at Kedarnath temple and shared photos. In 2023, she visited the shrine twice, performing darshan at Kedarnath and Tungnath on May 6, 2023, while about six months later, in October 2023, she again reached Kedarnath. Additionally, in November 2021, Sara Ali Khan also visited Kedarnath for darshan with her friend and actress Janhvi Kapoor.

stories.title: Caste politics takes centre stage on Ambedkar Jayanti:Mayawati shows strength in Lucknow, BJP unveils statue scheme
stories.summary: Caste equations play a decisive role in Uttar Pradesh politics, no party can secure power without the support of the Scheduled Castes. On 14 April, the birth anniversary of B. R. Ambedkar, all major parties, including BJP, SP, BSP and Congress, are organising events to engage with Dalit voters. In the lead-up to this, Congress held programmes on the birth anniversary of Jagjivan Ram, the country’s only Dalit Deputy Prime Minister, as well as on social reformer Jyotiba Phule. The Uttar Pradesh government has announced the Dr Ambedkar Statue Development Scheme, while the Samajwadi Party (SP) plans to conduct door-to-door campaigns centred on the Constitution. These initiatives are clearly aimed at consolidating the Dalit vote bank. Why the Dalit vote matters ? Dalits constitute approximately 20–21% of Uttar Pradesh’s population. Of the total Assembly seats, 84 are reserved for Scheduled Castes, but their influence extends beyond these constituencies, affecting outcomes in over 124 seats. Senior journalist Ratan Mani Lal notes that since the political weakening of Mayawati after 2012, there has been no single dominant Dalit leader capable of unifying the community. As a result, all parties are competing to attract Dalit voters. Senior journalist Akhilesh Bajpai adds that Dalit communities revere Ambedkar almost as a deity. Parties that consistently honour his legacy tend to find greater acceptance among Dalit voters. BJP’s strategy: Schemes and Symbolism The BJP-led Uttar Pradesh government has announced the Dr B.R. Ambedkar Statue Development Scheme. Under this, ₹1 crore will be allocated in each Assembly constituency for the conservation and beautification of 10 memorials dedicated to Ambedkar and other social reformers. Across the state, garlanding ceremonies and seminars will be organised at Ambedkar memorials. In Lucknow, for the first time, 11,000 lamps will be lit at Ambedkar’s memorial at Hazratganj, an initiative led by BJP state president Pankaj Chaudhary. A seminar is also scheduled for 15 April at Ambedkar’s urn site, to be addressed by Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath. Last year’s approach: In 2025, BJP organised cleaning and garlanding drives at Ambedkar memorials and ran the ‘Dr Bhimrao Ambedkar Samman Abhiyan’ from 13 to 25 April. BSP: Demonstrating core strength The Bahujan Samaj Party (BSP) plans to showcase its core voter base on Ambedkar Jayanti. Its main programme will be held at the Dr Bhimrao Ambedkar Social Transformation Site in Gomtinagar, Lucknow. Party workers and officials from 18 divisions across Uttar Pradesh have been invited along with their families. Leaders, including state president Vishwanath Pal, zonal coordinators, district presidents and Assembly in-charges, will attend. The gathering is expected to draw between 150,000 and 200,000 participants. Interestingly, BSP chief Mayawati and her nephew Akash Anand will not attend the main event. Instead, Mayawati will pay floral tribute to Ambedkar at her Mall Avenue residence at 8 AM and issue a message to party workers. Akash Anand will be in Chhattisgarh. Last year’s approach: BSP organised events in Noida and Lucknow, drawing workers from 6 and 12 divisions respectively. This year, all divisions are converging in Lucknow. SP: Constitution-centric outreach The Samajwadi Party is focusing on Ambedkar’s constitutional legacy. It plans to organise seminars in every village, discussing his life and ideas while targeting the BJP through 'Constitution dialogues'. SP leaders will tell voters that the BJP intends to alter the Constitution and weaken reservation policies. Party chief Akhilesh Yadav is expected to hold a press conference as part of the campaign. Last year’s approach: Akhilesh Yadav garlanded Ambedkar’s statue in Lucknow and emphasised that unity among PDA (Pichda, Dalit, Alpasankhyak—Backward, Dalit and Minority groups) is essential to safeguard the Constitution and reservation. Changing Dalit voting patterns 2017 Assembly Elections- The BJP fielded candidates in 85 of 86 reserved seats and won 75, indicating a major shift of Dalit voters away from BSP. 2022 Assembly Elections- The BJP contested all 86 seats but won 63, suggesting that some Dalit votes had shifted towards SP. 2024 Lok Sabha Elections- Out of 17 SC-reserved seats in Uttar Pradesh, SP won 7. Chandrashekhar Azad won from Nagina, while Congress candidates secured victories in Barabanki and Sitapur. This reflected a relative decline in the BJP’s performance among Dalit voters. SP’s PDA formula and BJP’s concerns SP is continuing with its PDA strategy, uniting Backward Classes, Dalits and minorities, which proved effective in recent elections. The party is emphasising slogans such as 'Save the Constitution' and 'Protect Reservation' to attract Dalit voters. Meanwhile, dissatisfaction among Dalits regarding their representation in government, party organisations, the Legislative Council and the Rajya Sabha has added to the BJP’s concerns. Expert views: Symbolism and Strategy Akhilesh Bajpai highlights that symbols play a crucial role in politics. Ambedkar represents not only Dalits but also broader marginalised communities. Political parties understand that invoking his legacy resonates deeply with these groups. Ratan Mani Lal observes that Mayawati has become active again after a period of relative silence. There are signs of renewed Dalit inclination towards her leadership. This sends a strong message to both BJP and SP: if Dalit votes consolidate behind BSP or split into multiple directions, it could significantly alter electoral outcomes.

stories.title: How Noida factory workers' protest turned violent without leadership?:Communication gap fuelled unrest, rumours of rejected demands triggered escalation
stories.summary: Factory workers in Noida, Uttar Pradesh, had been protesting for three days, demanding a wage increase. On Monday, the agitation escalated into violence, with hundreds of workers taking to the streets carrying sticks and batons. Protesters pelted stones and vandalised more than 350 factories across multiple areas. Over 150 vehicles were damaged, more than 50 were set on fire, and several police vehicles were overturned. Police personnel were also targeted, with around 30 people reported injured. Authorities have registered cases against 60 individuals so far. The violent escalation has significantly disrupted industrial activity, with factory owners estimating losses of nearly ₹3,000 crore due to halted operations and damage. Allegations of instigation and administrative gaps Factory owners have alleged that workers were provoked into violence. Meanwhile, a lack of effective communication between the administration and labourers is being seen as a critical factor behind the unrest. Notably, workers were reportedly not informed about a key meeting held on Sunday, where their demands had allegedly been addressed. This communication failure has raised concerns over administrative handling of the situation. The primary trigger for the protest was a decision by the Haryana government. On 9 April, it approved a 35% increase in minimum wages, with notification issued on 10 April. Following this, workers in Noida’s industrial belt began demanding similar wage hikes. Wage comparison- Haryana- Unskilled: ₹11,275 → ₹15,220 Semi-skilled: ₹12,430 → ₹16,780 Skilled: ₹13,704 → ₹18,500 Highly skilled: ₹14,389 → ₹19,425 Uttar Pradesh (Noida)- Unskilled workers earn around ₹11,313 Daily wages- Haryana: ₹580–₹750 Noida: ₹435–₹535 How did events unfolded ? 10–11 April Around 1,000 workers began protesting at Hosiery Complex and Surajpur–Dadri Road. Tensions escalated following a police lathi-charge. The matter reached Lucknow, and Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath directed officials to resolve it within 24 hours. 12 April Noida District Magistrate Medha Roopam and labour officials met industry representatives. Companies were instructed to comply with labour laws and ensure timely wage payments. A control room was established. 13 April (Monday) Workers remained dissatisfied, as no concrete decision was taken on wage increases. By morning, thousands gathered, and the protest turned violent. Why did the protest turn violent? At around 9 AM, approximately 300–400 workers gathered outside the Motherson company in Sector-81, Phase-2. The protest had no formal leadership, with workers organising themselves. During sloganeering, frustration grew over the lack of response to their demands. A rumour then spread that their demands would not be accepted, triggering anger. Stone-pelting and arson soon followed. Workers entered several factories, halted operations, and forced employees to leave. Female workers reportedly hid under benches in fear and later returned home after the situation calmed. Social media further fuelled tensions, with false reports of deaths and injuries circulating widely. Administrative lapse and communication gap A crucial meeting was held on Sunday at the Noida Authority, attended by officials from the administration, police, and industry. The meeting was chaired by CEO Krishna Karunesh, with Police Commissioner Laxmi Singh and DM Medha Roopam present. Senior officials, including Principal Secretary (Labour) MKS Sundaram and Labour Commissioner Markandey Shahi, joined virtually. Key decisions included strict enforcement of minimum wages, timely payments, equal pay for equal work, overtime compensation, EPF-ESI benefits, gratuity, and workplace safety under new labour codes. However, workers were not informed of these decisions until Monday morning. This information gap significantly contributed to the escalation of unrest. Hour-by-hour escalation of violence 9:00 AM – Motherson Gate (Phase-2) The protest began with 300–400 workers. The situation quickly turned violent, with four police vehicles vandalised and set ablaze. Around 10 other vehicles were also torched. Police used tear gas, and PAC and RAF forces were deployed. 10:00 AM – Streets Blocked Within an hour, hundreds of workers from Sectors 1–6 took to the streets, blocking DSC Road and halting traffic towards Delhi for nearly an hour before police cleared the route. 1:00 PM – Sector-57 Rampage Around 600 individuals armed with sticks and stones targeted industries in B-Block, Sector-57. More than 50 factories were vandalised within 30–35 minutes. Police presence proved insufficient, necessitating RAF deployment. 3:00 PM – Arson in Sector-63 Vehicles outside Vipul Motors were set on fire. Reports of vandalism continued from Labour Chowk to Sectors 62, 63, and 65. Fire services eventually brought the blaze under control. Most rioters were aged between 18 and 25 and carried sticks, stones, petrol-filled bottles, and even firecrackers to create smoke. Business Impact: ₹3,000 crore loss According to Sudhir Srivastava of the Noida Entrepreneurs Association, about 80% of industries were operational in the morning. However, by afternoon, most units shut down as mobs entered factories, halted production, and forced workers out. Business losses are estimated at around ₹3,000 crore in a single day. Industry representatives claim that workers have been influenced or incited. Police action and digital investigation Uttar Pradesh DGP Rajiv Krishna stated that over 50 bot handles had been identified, created within 24 hours to spread misinformation and provoke unrest. The Special Task Force (STF) will investigate the digital trail, with initial findings suggesting an organised attempt to create panic. Police Commissioner Laxmi Singh said- Around 42,000 workers protested at 83 locations. Violence occurred at only two sites, while 78 locations were peacefully resolved through negotiations. She added that individuals from outside districts attempted to incite violence, and arrests have been made. Others are being identified through CCTV footage Additional CP (Law and Order) Rajiv Narayan Mishra confirmed that cases have been registered against 60 individuals, with around 200 detained.

stories.title: Fresh protest erupts in Noida, stone-pelting at police:Paramilitary forces deployed; Rahul Gandhi calls it workers’ 'last cry'
stories.summary: Factory workers in Noida (Gautam Buddh Nagar) again took to the streets on Tuesday, demanding higher wages. Clashes broke out when police attempted to stop them. In two to three locations, the crowd pelted stones at police vehicles. The situation was brought under control shortly, and protesters were dispersed. Police and paramilitary forces have been conducting flag marches in industrial areas since 5 AM. Monitoring is being carried out through CCTV cameras and drones. Additionally, 15 companies of PAC and RAF, along with 26 officers (8 Additional SPs and 18 DSPs), have been deployed in Noida. Most companies remain shut. The Uttar Pradesh government increased minimum wages by up to ₹3,000 late Monday night, effective from 1 April, following a high-level committee meeting with workers. Strict warning from police DGP Rajiv Krishna is monitoring the situation from the Lucknow control room. He said strict action will be taken against those involved in violence and arson, and losses will be recovered from those responsible. Police Commissioner Laxmi Singh said over 300 arrests have been made. Several groups spreading rumours have been identified, with some individuals found active at multiple locations. Around 50 X accounts were used to incite violence. Rahul Gandhi said the unrest reflected workers’ ‘last cry’ after being ignored. On Monday, 42,000 workers vandalised over 350 factories, set more than 50 vehicles ablaze, damaged 150, and pelted stones at police. See photos from today's protest- Recap of Monday’s violence On Monday, factory workers staged violent protests across various parts of Noida. Around 42,000 workers, who had been agitating since 9 April over wage demands, came out onto the streets. They vandalised more than 350 factories, set over 50 vehicles on fire, and damaged around 150 others. Police personnel were also targeted with stone-pelting during the unrest. stories.title: ATS to probe 26 arson cases over terror link:NIA issues lookout notices against three suspected terrorists
stories.summary: The Anti-Terrorist Squad (ATS) in Uttar Pradesh will investigate around 26 incidents of arson across the state from a terror perspective. This decision follows inputs obtained from four suspected terrorists recently arrested in Lucknow. Many of these cases, involving vehicles catching fire in different districts, were previously treated as accidents. They will now be re-examined in detail. The National Investigation Agency (NIA) will also be involved in the probe. Arrest of 4 suspects in Lucknow The Uttar Pradesh ATS arrested four individuals in Lucknow on 2 April, before they could execute a major planned attack. During interrogation, it emerged that they had been carrying out small-scale arson incidents, recording videos, and sending them to handlers in Pakistan. The suspects were identified as Saqib alias Devil (the alleged gang leader), Vikas Gehlawat alias Raunak, Lokesh alias Babu alias Papla Pandit, and Arbab. Investigators recovered several key pieces of evidence from their mobile phones, which are now central to the ongoing inquiry. Arson as ‘proof of work’ for handlers According to investigators, the accused used these minor arson incidents as “trial runs” to demonstrate their capabilities. They would film the incidents and send the footage to a Pakistani handler identified as Abu Bakar. In return, they allegedly received payments via QR code-based transactions. Authorities believe their objective was to create fear and communal tension through repeated small-scale incidents. Reinvestigation of past incidents ADG Law and Order Amitabh Yash stated that fire incidents are often reported as accidental. However, after discovering a possible link between arson and financial transactions, authorities have begun reviewing cases from the past six months. A total of 26 incidents across districts, including Aligarh, Ghaziabad, Bulandshahr, Kanpur, Bareilly, and Prayagraj, have been identified for re-examination. In one confirmed instance, the accused allegedly set fire to a pickup truck in the Kiratpur area on 4 March and recorded the act. Investigators are now analysing seven mobile phones recovered from the suspects to trace the location, timing, and details of similar incidents. Forensic challenges in old cases The probe is expected to be complex, as many of the incidents are several months old. Authorities may face difficulties in retrieving forensic evidence or CCTV footage. Records of arson incidents involving vehicles, shops, and small establishments in districts such as Bulandshahr, Bijnor, Meerut, Baghpat, and Hapur are being reviewed. In the absence of strong physical evidence, statements from residents are likely to play a critical role. Financial trail under scrutiny Investigators have uncovered suspicious transactions in the bank accounts of the accused. These are now being matched with the dates of arson incidents to establish a direct link between payments and criminal acts. This financial trail is expected to provide crucial evidence regarding the operational structure and external support for the network. Links to wider network and foreign handlers During the investigation, ATS identified several suspicious phone numbers linked to other states. This information has been shared with the NIA. Some of these contacts are reportedly based in Maharashtra. Additionally, videos recovered from the suspects’ phones show other individuals carrying weapons. These individuals have been identified as Aakib, Mahjul, Azad, and Ubaid Malik. A case has been registered against them in Bijnor through a central agency. Lookout notices have been issued for Mahjul, believed to be in South Africa, and Aakib and Azad, reportedly based in Saudi Arabia. Use of encrypted communication tools The accused allegedly used multiple methods to communicate with their Pakistani handler- Planned attack on Lucknow Railway Station According to ATS officials, the group had planned a major attack targeting infrastructure near Lucknow Railway Station. Their objective was to damage the signal system and cause a large-scale explosion on 2 April, potentially leading to significant casualties. However, the ATS acted on prior intelligence and arrested the suspects before the plan could be executed. Online radicalisation and bomb-making searches Analysis of the suspects’ mobile phones revealed concerning online activity. Their YouTube search history included queries such as 'How to make a time bomb?', ‘How to make a chemical bomb?’, and 'What are the techniques for accurate targeting?'. Investigators also found that their handler, Abu Bakar, had shared links and instructional videos. The extent of their technical preparedness will become clearer after the completion of their five-day police remand.

stories.title: PM Modi inaugurates Delhi–Dehradun Expressway:Says, 'women’s rights priority for 2029 polls; calls infrastructure ‘Modi’s guarantee’
stories.summary: Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Tuesday inaugurated the Delhi–Dehradun Expressway corridor. On the occasion, he said that there was a time when villagers in Uttarakhand had to wait generations for roads, but under the double-engine government’s efforts, connectivity is now reaching even remote villages. He added that areas which were once deserted are now becoming inhabited again. The Prime Minister said that if seen in terms of national development, roads, highways, airways, railways and waterways are the “lifelines of the nation”. He described these as not just present-day facilities but a “guarantee of Modi” for future generations. He also reiterated the government’s commitment to ensuring women’s rights, stating that steps are being taken in Parliament to secure their due representation by 2029. See pictures- Longstanding association with Uttarakhand Since assuming office in 2014, Modi has maintained a strong connection with Uttarakhand. His first visit to the state as Prime Minister was on 11 September 2015, when he met Swami Dayanand Giri in Rishikesh. Over the years, he has frequently visited prominent religious sites, including Kedarnath, Badrinath, Mukhba, and Adi Kailash, reflecting both administrative and spiritual engagement with the region. Expressway designed for seamless travel The Delhi–Dehradun Expressway has been developed with a focus on uninterrupted and efficient travel. A total of 14 wayside facilities have been established along the route, offering amenities such as parking, food courts, toilets, and essential services. These facilities are intended to minimize the need for frequent stops during long journeys. Additionally, the corridor includes seven interchanges, enabling smooth connectivity to various cities and highways, thereby improving accessibility across the region. Advanced engineering and infrastructure A key feature of the expressway is its 18.6-kilometre elevated corridor, designed to allow traffic to bypass congested and environmentally sensitive areas. The project also includes 19 major underpasses, 57 minor underpasses, and four significant bridges, ensuring both smooth vehicular movement and preservation of local connectivity. To support local communities, service roads have been constructed alongside the expressway. Safety measures such as secure U-turns, crash barriers, and an Advanced Traffic Management System (ATMS) have been implemented to enhance monitoring, traffic control, and emergency response capabilities. Travel time reduced to 2.5 hours The expressway is set to dramatically reduce travel time between Delhi and Dehradun. Currently, the journey via the traditional route, covering approximately 235 kilometres through Delhi, Meerut, Muzaffarnagar, Roorkee, and onward, typically takes around six hours due to congestion and mixed traffic conditions. With the new expressway, the distance will decrease to approximately 212 kilometres, saving around 23 kilometres. More importantly, travel time is expected to be reduced to just 2.5 hours, offering a faster and more predictable journey. Regions set to benefit The expressway will significantly improve connectivity across Delhi-NCR, Western Uttar Pradesh, and Uttarakhand. Areas in East Delhi, such as Akshardham and Sonia Vihar, will gain high-speed access, potentially boosting employment opportunities and real estate development. Districts including Baghpat, Shamli, Muzaffarnagar, and Saharanpur in Western Uttar Pradesh will be directly linked, benefiting sectors such as sugarcane farming, agro-industries, and logistics. In Uttarakhand, Dehradun will receive a direct six-lane connection, while Haridwar, Roorkee, and Rishikesh will be connected via spur routes, supporting tourism and religious travel. Asia’s longest wildlife corridor One of the most notable aspects of the project is the wildlife corridor passing through Rajaji National Park and the Shivalik forest range. This includes an approximately 12-kilometre elevated stretch, allowing animals to move freely beneath the roadway. Special measures have been implemented to protect wildlife, including noise barriers and light control systems to minimise disturbance during night-time. These provisions aim to preserve the natural habitat while maintaining infrastructure efficiency. Key features of the wildlife corridor Boost to tourism and business The expressway is expected to significantly enhance tourism by reducing travel time from Delhi-NCR to popular destinations such as Mussoorie, Rishikesh, Haridwar, Dhanaulti, and Chakrata. Improved access via the Haridwar–Rishikesh spur will also facilitate travel to major religious events and sites, including the Kumbh, Char Dham pilgrimage, and Ganga bathing ghats. From a commercial perspective, the expressway will connect industrial hubs in Delhi-NCR with those in Western Uttar Pradesh and Uttarakhand, including Roorkee, Haridwar, Saharanpur, and Muzaffarnagar. This is expected to streamline freight movement, reduce logistics costs, and create new investment opportunities in sectors such as FMCG, pharmaceuticals, automotive components, and agriculture. Toll structure and charges Toll rates for the Delhi–Dehradun Expressway have been set at approximately ₹3 per kilometre for cars. For a full journey from Delhi to Dehradun, motorists will pay around ₹675 for a one-way trip. If the return journey is completed within 24 hours, the return toll is reduced to ₹335. For light commercial vehicles such as minibuses, the one-way toll is approximately ₹1,100. Larger buses and trucks will be charged around ₹2,275, while heavier vehicles may incur tolls of up to ₹4,000. Standard toll exemptions applicable to other expressways will also apply here. Transformational project for North India Overall, the Delhi–Dehradun Expressway is poised to be a transformative infrastructure project for North India. By significantly reducing travel time and improving connectivity, it is expected to drive growth in tourism, commerce, and regional development, while also incorporating environmentally sensitive design features.

stories.title: ‘Multiple WhatsApp groups created overnight to incite Noida violence’:Commissioner says crowds gathered from nearby villages, over 150 detained
stories.summary: Authorities in Uttar Pradesh’s Gautam Buddh Nagar district (Noida/Greater Noida) have suggested that a ‘deep conspiracy’ may have fuelled the violent protests that erupted on Monday. According to Noida Police, those involved in arson and vandalism were not factory workers but miscreants posing as employees. Police Commissioner Laxmi Singh, speaking to Dainik Bhaskar, said there was ‘a strong indication of a large and organised conspiracy’. She noted that the situation had earlier calmed down, but violence suddenly reignited when unidentified groups, allegedly not labourers, emerged from nearby villages and began rioting. Sudden escalation raises questions The abrupt shift from a peaceful protest to widespread violence has raised several questions: how did the situation spiral so quickly, who orchestrated it, and whether intelligence agencies had prior inputs. There is also uncertainty about the actual target of the protest, whether it was company management, contractors, the administration, or the government. WhatsApp groups used to incite violence Commissioner Singh revealed that thousands of WhatsApp groups were allegedly created overnight to mobilise and radicalise workers. Employees were reportedly added via QR codes and incited to turn the protest aggressive. She added that the police had remained vigilant following similar unrest in Haryana and had deployed forces at sensitive locations. However, there was no prior indication of external elements being involved, which allowed the situation to deteriorate briefly before it was brought under control. Over 150 detained, probe underway More than 150 individuals have been taken into custody in connection with the violence. Police are interrogating them to determine how many are actual employees and how many are outsiders. Investigators are also examining the motives of those involved and whether any organised groups were behind the unrest. Leaderless protest added to chaos Sources indicate that the protest, which had been ongoing for four days since 9 April, had no identifiable leadership. Workers from various companies would gather at a common location, gradually swelling the crowd. When officials attempted dialogue on the first day, several participants refused to engage, stating they were not leaders. This absence of leadership appears to have complicated negotiations and crowd management. Government claims prior agreement The Uttar Pradesh government maintains that discussions had already taken place with workers and agreements were reached on several demands. However, some protesters argue that the agreement reflected only employees’ views and lacked the consent of industry owners. Workers insist that unless employers agree to key demands, such as minimum wages, an eight-hour workday, overtime pay, and night duty allowances, any agreement remains incomplete. They also claim these issues had been raised with the Deputy Labour Commissioner three to four months earlier, who had assured action, but no progress was made. No clear organisational or political link So far, no major organisation has publicly claimed responsibility for leading the protest. However, there are inputs suggesting that some office bearers of the Centre of Indian Trade Unions may have supported the agitation from behind the scenes. Officials state that no direct political connection has been established. Nonetheless, the protest spread beyond Noida to Greater Noida, Faridabad, and Ghaziabad, indicating a broader mobilisation. Workers cite low wages and exploitation Workers allege they are paid as little as ₹10,000–₹12,000 per month, which they say is insufficient amid rising inflation. They claim they are made to work up to 12 hours a day without overtime pay and face additional forms of exploitation. Despite the reported agreement on Sunday, dissatisfaction persisted among sections of workers, some of whom either rejected the terms or continued protesting in what authorities describe as a planned manner. Government response and measures The Noida Police have launched a detailed investigation into the violence. A high-level committee has been formed to examine workers’ demands and has already reached Noida. CM Yogi Adityanath has directed that workers must receive fair wages and adequate safety measures. He emphasised maintaining round-the-clock communication in industrial areas and called for strict action against those attempting to disrupt law and order. Appeal for calm and workplace reforms The administration has urged workers to ignore rumours and maintain peace. Noida District Magistrate Medha Rupam stated that key decisions have been taken following meetings with companies. These include the formation of workplace committees to prevent sexual harassment, chaired by women, installation of complaint boxes, ensuring respectful treatment of employees, mandatory salary payments by the 10th of each month, and provision of salary slips. Authorities continue efforts to stabilise the situation while addressing both the alleged conspiracy and the workers’ grievances.
