stories.title: Girl dragged, forced onto bike in Fatehpur:Harassment on busy road caught on video, accused claims she is his girlfriend
stories.summary: In Fatehpur, on Tuesday evening, a 20-year-old boy molested an 18-year-old student in the middle of the road. He forcibly stopped the student, snatched her bag, and insisted on making her sit on his bike. The girl continuously asked him to let her go, but he refused. Seeing the commotion, people gathered around. Some started making videos. Seeing this, the accused got agitated. He threatened people and asked them not to make videos. He said, "She is my girlfriend. This is our personal matter. Stay away." People complained to the Chief Minister on social media. After this, the police arrested the accused boy. The incident took place 300 meters away from the Abunagar police outpost. First, see 2 pictures Now read the full case in detail The incident is from the Abunagar area, under Kotwali police station. On Tuesday evening, a boy arrived there on a Splendor bike. Soon after, he started molesting the girl. He dragged the girl to the bike and insisted on making her sit on it. The girl continuously refused, but he did not listen. During this, he grabbed the girl's bag and started pulling it. The girl kept trying to free her bag. She pleaded to be let go, but the boy kept dragging the bag. This commotion continued at the intersection for a long time. Fled on threat of calling police A crowd of people gathered around. When people protested, the boy started threatening them. When people in the crowd mentioned calling the police on Dial 100, he fled from the spot. After this, the girl's family took her home with them. The girl is a third-year BA student. Her house is about 3 kilometers away from the incident site. The accused has been identified as Aman Syed alias Jordan. He is a resident of Uttar Kheldar. His father has passed away. His family includes his mother and a sister. Police registered the case themselves After the incident, the girl's family was unwilling to say anything and did not file any complaint. However, the matter reached social media. People tagged the CM on X and demanded action. After this, the police sprang into action. Chowki Incharge Gulab Maurya took cognizance of the video and registered the case himself. Police took action as soon as the video went viral SP Abhimanyu Manglik said that on Tuesday evening around 5 PM in the Abunagar area, Aman Sayyed alias Jordan publicly stopped a girl. He was molesting her and trying to forcibly pull her onto his bike while making obscene gestures. When the girl resisted, the accused abused her and also threatened to kill her. After the video of the incident went viral, the police registered a case against the accused under sections 126(2), 75, 352, and 351(2) of the BNS. He was arrested from his home during a raid around 2 AM on Wednesday night. The accused has been sent to jail.

stories.title: UP orders salary hike for Shiksha Mitras, instructors:Effective from 1 April; 1.67 lakh workers to benefit
stories.summary: The Uttar Pradesh government has issued an order increasing the honorarium of Shiksha Mitras and instructors, benefiting around 1.67 lakh personnel across the state. The order was released on Thursday evening. Under the revised structure, Shiksha Mitras will now receive ₹18,000 per month, up from ₹10,000, while instructors’ honorarium has been raised from ₹9,000 to ₹17,000 per month. The hike is effective from 1 April and the increased payments will start reflecting in bank accounts from 1 May. Currently, there are 1,42,229 Shiksha Mitras and 24,717 instructors in the state. This marks the first salary hike for Shiksha Mitras in nine years. Additional benefits and policy announcements Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath had recently announced that Shiksha Mitras would also be eligible for transfers. Additionally, they and their families will receive cashless medical treatment coverage of up to ₹5 lakh. The proposal to increase the honorarium was approved in a cabinet meeting earlier this week. Subsequently, Additional Chief Secretary Parth Sarathi Sen Sharma issued the official order to the Director General of School Education. Read the government's order Political row ahead of elections The salary hike has sparked political debate ahead of the Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav criticized the move, claiming that during his tenure, Shiksha Mitras effectively earned up to ₹40,000. He alleged that the current hike was driven by electoral fears and termed it insufficient after years of “harassment.” In a letter addressed to Shiksha Mitras, Yadav urged them to mobilize against the ruling BJP in the upcoming elections. He also demanded that the government clear pending dues from previous years. Legal and Policy background on instructors’ pay In 2017, instructors’ honorarium was proposed to be increased from around ₹9,000 to ₹17,000, but the decision was not implemented after a change in government. Following a legal battle, the Lucknow bench of the Allahabad High Court initially ordered payment of ₹17,000 with 9% interest. The state government challenged the order, and a division bench limited the payment to one year. The matter eventually reached the Supreme Court. On February 5, the Supreme Court dismissed the state government’s appeal and directed that instructors should continue in service even after the contractual period, noting that their positions effectively became permanent after long-term service. It also ordered implementation of the ₹17,000 honorarium from 2017. Shiksha Mitras’ journey: From appointment to legal setbacks The appointment of Shiksha Mitras in Uttar Pradesh began in 2001. During the Samajwadi Party government (2013–14), many were adjusted as assistant teachers. However, in 2015, the Allahabad High Court cancelled these appointments. The matter went to the Supreme Court, which, on July 25, 2017, upheld the cancellation. As a result, around 1.78 lakh assistant teachers were reverted to Shiksha Mitra positions, with their salaries dropping sharply from about ₹50,000 to ₹3,500 per month. This triggered widespread protests, including a major agitation in Lucknow. Following this, the government increased their honorarium to ₹10,000 per month and announced teacher recruitment drives. Subsequent recruitment drives in 2018 (68,500 posts) and 2019 (69,000 posts) offered age relaxation and bonus marks to Shiksha Mitras, enabling over 13,000 of them to become assistant teachers.

stories.title: FIR filed against officer hiding ₹17 crore in mattress, bathroom:Kanpur sees action after 9 years; spent 12 times his earnings
stories.summary: A case has been registered against Keshav Lal, a retired Additional Commissioner of the Sales Tax Department in Kanpur, for possessing assets disproportionate to his income. The FIR was filed 9 years later on April 8 by the Kanpur Vigilance team. 9 years ago, in 2017, Keshav was posted in Kanpur. During that time, the Income Tax Department raided his homes in Noida and Kanpur. Bundles of notes were found hidden in mattresses, bathroom flushes, and cardboard boxes. A total of 10 crore cash and 3 crore worth of jewelry were found in Noida, while 4 crore cash was found in Kanpur. In addition, immovable properties worth crores were also discovered. Following this, the Vigilance Department was investigating Keshav. Now, after the completion of the investigation, an FIR has been registered. Now know the full story Keshav Lal lived in a rented house in Kanpur Keshav Lal, originally from Bamhaniyao village in Chandauli district, currently lives in Sector-34, Noida. In 2017, he was posted in Kanpur. According to vigilance, Keshav Lal lived in a rented house in the Lakhanpur area of Kanpur. The rent for the house he lived in was around 10 thousand rupees. It had 2 rooms, 2 bathrooms, a kitchen, and a dining space. However, Keshav Lal mostly lived alone here. His family lived in Noida. Keshav has two children - a son and a daughter. He got his daughter married in December 2016 in Noida. Income Tax Department raided on April 19, 2017 The Income Tax Department raided his homes in Noida and Kanpur on April 19, 2017. Approximately 4 crore rupees were found in the rented house in Kanpur. Meanwhile, approximately 10 crore rupees in cash and 3 crore rupees worth of jewellery were recovered from the Noida house. In Noida, bundles of notes were found from the mattresses, puja room, wardrobe, and unused flush of the bathroom. Additionally, 3 cartons full of notes were found in the bedroom. Subsequently, Keshav Lal was given compulsory retirement in May 2017. Along with this, the investigation of the case was handed over to Vigilance. Since then, an investigation into his properties has been ongoing. On January 6, 2026, Vigilance submitted its investigation report From September 19, 2023, the Vigilance Department rapidly initiated an investigation against the then Additional Commissioner (Grade-2) Commercial Tax, Keshav Lal. During the investigation, documents of several valuable properties were found in Keshav Lal's home district, Chandauli, as well as in Kanpur, Prayagraj, Ghaziabad, and Noida. He owns 2 properties in Lucknow, and one each in Kanpur, Prayagraj, Ghaziabad, and Noida, all valued at crores. After the completion of the investigation, Vigilance officers submitted their report on January 6, 2026. Following this, approval was given to register a report against Keshav Lal. Subsequently, a case was registered in Kanpur on April 8, 2026. According to the Vigilance FIR, Keshav Lal earned a total income of approximately 1 crore 34 lakh from legitimate sources throughout his government career. However, the investigation revealed that he spent approximately 18 crore 27 lakh rupees. Thus, assets and expenses were approximately 17 crore 26 lakh rupees more than his income were found.

stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. Green Asha, carrying 15,400 tonnes of LPG, docks at Mumbai Jawaharlal Nehru Port Authority (JNPA) on Thursday received the India-flagged LPG vessel Green Asha, carrying 15,400 tonnes of liquefied petroleum gas. The ship successfully crossed the Strait of Hormuz. It has now docked at JNPA’s liquid berth operated by BPCL-IOCL. 2. Mafia Ashraf’s aide killed in broad daylight: Shot at a tea shop in Prayagraj The incident occurred around 6:30 PM near Bismillah Chowk. Irfan was sitting at a tea shop close to his house when four attackers arrived on two motorcycles. All had covered their faces with gamchas. 3. An Amity student drowned in a water-filled pit in Noida: Went for a picnic after exams A 23-year-old student of Amity University in Noida, Harshit Bhatt, died after drowning in a water-filled pit on Wednesday evening. Harshit had gone for a picnic with three friends after finishing his exams. During the outing, he entered the pit, went into the deeper section and began to drown. 4. Robot in traditional saree welcomes voters; Puducherry tops voter turnout at 89.81% Polling has concluded in a single phase today for Assembly elections in the states of Assam and Kerala, and the Union Territory of Puducherry. Voter turnout stands at 85.38% in Assam, 78.01% in Kerala, 89.81% in Puducherry. 5.15 accused, multi-city kidney racket: The doctor brought a surgical team from Meerut A large-scale illegal kidney transplant racket, originating from Ahuja Hospital in Kanpur, has exposed a well-organised network spanning nine hospitals across four cities in Uttar Pradesh. 6. AAP to lose by sidelining Raghav Chadha, says Avimukteshwaranand: Calls him ‘An asset to the country’ Swami Avimukteshwaranand has entered the ongoing row between the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and its Rajya Sabha MP Raghav Chadha, calling Chadha “an asset to the nation” and saying the party may be harming itself. 7. PM Modi gives 6 guarantees to Bengal, including the 7th Pay Commission Prime Minister outlined six major assurances for the people of West Bengal, focusing on justice, accountability, and effective governance under a BJP government, which includes implementing the 7th pay commission in the state, curbing infiltrators and protecting women. 8. 'Now I have to support my national-level player daughter ': Mother alleges son-in-law tried to hang daughter in Kashi “Ask a mother. The daughter who once supported me, I have been supporting her for the last 10 months. She used to bring home medals. Today, I am asking for justice for her, which we have not received so far. Her husband left her to die and is now threatening us, too. 9. UP farmer breaks down as hailstorm destroys crop: Hail blankets Hardoi, alert in 44 districts A farmer in Hardoi broke down in tears after seeing his crop destroyed by rain and hail. Unseasonal storms, rain and hail continue to batter Uttar Pradesh. The weather department has issued a rain alert for 44 districts on Thursday, warning of strong winds reaching speeds of up to 60 kmph. 10. Centre criticises Sabarimala verdict in the Supreme Court Supreme Court ruled that the 2018 Sabarimala verdict was based on the notion that men are superior and women inferior. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta supported restrictions on women’s entry to religious sites.

stories.title: 47 police officers transferred in UP:ASP Ayush Vikram Singh moved from Gonda to Bahraich; Twinkle Jain posted to Prayagraj Commissionerate
stories.summary: IPS officers have been transferred in the state. Sagar Jain of IPS-RR-2019 batch has been made Deputy Commissioner of Police, Police Commissionerate Prayagraj, from Additional Superintendent of Police (Rural) Saharanpur. Manoj Kumar Rawat of IPS-RR-2020 batch has been sent from Additional Superintendent of Police (East) Gonda to Additional Superintendent of Police (South) Sambhal, while Ayush Vikram Singh has been posted from Additional Superintendent of Police (City) Meerut to Additional Superintendent of Police (City) Bahraich. Vinayak Gopal Bhosle of IPS-RR-2022 batch has been made Additional Superintendent of Police (City) Meerut from Assistant Superintendent of Police Sitapur, Antariksh Jain from Assistant Superintendent of Police Meerut to Additional Superintendent of Police (Rural) Bulandshahr, Twinkle Jain from Assistant Commissioner of Police Gautam Buddh Nagar to Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police Lucknow, and Lipi Nagayach has been made Additional Deputy Commissioner of Police Varanasi from Assistant Commissioner of Police Ghaziabad. In this sequence, Rajkumar Meena has been appointed from Assistant Commissioner of Police Prayagraj to Additional Superintendent of Police (Naxal) Mirzapur, Rishabh Runwal from Assistant Commissioner of Police Lucknow to Additional Superintendent of Police (Naxal) Sonbhadra, Alok Kumar from Assistant Superintendent of Police Sambhal to Additional Superintendent of Police (City East) Pratapgarh, Dr. Ishan Soni from Assistant Commissioner of Police Varanasi to Additional Superintendent of Police Jalaun, and Mayank Pathak from Assistant Superintendent of Police Aligarh to Additional Superintendent of Police (Rural) Saharanpur. stories.title: Major husband in depression after wife dances post-divorce:Posted in Jalandhar; in-laws say, 'Daughter-in-law broke court agreement, defamed us'
stories.summary: In Meerut, Uttar Pradesh, the husband of Pranita Sharma, the woman who danced to the beat of drums after divorce, is a Major in the Army and is posted in Jalandhar. His parents, residing at Jalandhar Cantt, have stated that their son Major Gaurav Agnihotri has been in depression since the divorce. They said that daughter-in-law Pranita is lying. She has snatched his child from our son and our grandson from us. With a choked voice, the Major's father said - she has taken away my right to be a grandfather. When the daughter-in-law had an operation and her leg was broken, the mother-in-law massaged and served her, and this is the reward we got. By breaking the court agreement, we are being defamed across the entire country. Major's parents decline harassment charges The Major's parents said that their son is in the Army, which has a discipline. Women cannot be harassed here. Within a minute of a complaint, the army takes action against its soldier. The father said that the daughter-in-law is lying on the strength of her advocate brothers and judge father. She has already filed a case in 2019 as well. On December 14, 2018, UP's Shahjahanpur Army Major Gaurav Agnihotri married Pranita Sharma from Meerut. Pranita demanded divorce alleging harassment at her in-laws' place and on April 4, 2026, the court granted the divorce. As soon as she got the divorce, Pranita danced to the beat of drums. The video of this went viral rapidly on the internet. The Major's father said these things about the case The Major's mother stated 3 important points Know what the maternal family told about the whole matter... Retired judge Gyanendra Sharma in Meerut said - My daughter Pranita Sharma's in-laws' behavior has not been good since after marriage. In 7 years, she endured many hardships. Her husband and in-laws started harassing her. During this time, she also had a son, but even after the child's birth, the situation did not change. The in-laws troubled her mentally and physically. Finally, Pranita decided to take a divorce. She filed a petition in Meerut Family Court. On April 4, the court granted the divorce. After this, the family has brought daughter Pranita Sharma back home with full respect. Father said - She is my daughter, not some commodity Father Gyanendra Sharma said - If my daughter was unhappy in her marriage, it was my responsibility to give her happiness. My daughter left for her wedding with pomp and show. Today I have brought her back with the same respect. I did not take any alimony or belongings from those people. He said that forcing a daughter to stay at her in-laws' house at any cost is wrong. A daughter is not a commodity, she is part of the family. Women's empowerment should not remain limited to papers only. It is necessary to implement it on the ground. Pranita Sharma said - First make yourself strong, study and educate yourself Pranita Sharma is the Finance Director at Pranav Vashishth Judicial Academy located in Shastri Nagar, Meerut. She has done post-graduation in Psychology. She is the only daughter of her parents. Her brother died in an accident in 2022. Pranita shared that she had become mentally very weak, but her family stood by her at all times. With this support, she managed to pull herself together. She said - If any woman is facing any kind of harassment, don't stay silent. Fight for yourself. First make yourself strong. Study, educate yourself, stand on your own feet. Only after that think about marriage. Taking forward the spirit of 'Beti Bachao, Beti Padhao' (Save the Daughter, Educate the Daughter), she said that making daughters educated and self-reliant is the real women empowerment.

stories.title: Brother murdered after sister plotted with lover:Caught them together in Mainpuri; husband works in IT firm in Pune
stories.summary: In Mainpuri, a sister, along with her lover, got her own brother murdered. The brother had seen her in an objectionable situation with her lover. When he protested, the lover shot him. The bullet pierced his eye and went through his head. After this, the lover, along with his brother, took the body about one and a half kilometres away from the house to a jungle near the river and dumped it. To mislead the police, the sister also filed a missing person report, but her 10-year-old son exposed his mother and her lover. This incident occurred on Tuesday night, in the Kishni police station area, about 35 kilometers away from the district headquarters. The police have arrested the accused sister and her lover. The deceased was a resident of Farrukhabad and had come to Mainpuri, his sister's in-laws' house, to drop her off. Know the full story Pooja Dubey, sister of Karan Mishra (25) from Karthia village, Farrukhabad, was married to Dilip Dubey, a resident of Kusmara village, Mainpuri, about 15 years ago. Dilip works in an IT company in Pune, Maharashtra. They have three children. The eldest son is 10-year-old Hrithik Dubey. Karan had gone to his sister's in-laws' house in Kusmara on Tuesday to drop her off. Due to it being late at night, he stayed there. Pooja's lover came to meet her at night Ritvik said - Around 12 o'clock at night, my mother's friend Jitendra alias Jitu (38) secretly came to meet her. Then my uncle woke up. When my uncle objected to Jitendra coming home, both of them clashed. There was a fierce fight. My mother was also on Jitendra's side. At my mother's insistence, he shot my uncle. After killing my uncle, Jitendra called his brother Juli. Both of them took his dead body on a bike and went somewhere. My mother threatened me not to tell anyone about this. When a call came from Grandma's house, Mom said- He had already left for home at night. In the morning, Jitendra returned again. Then Mom and Jitendra went to the police station. They left us alone at home. When they didn't return until afternoon, the neighbors asked me- Then I told them the whole story. After that, the neighbors called the police and informed them about the incident. Police arrested him at the station itself After the nephew's revelation, police reached the house based on information from neighbors. Meanwhile, Pooja had arrived at Kishni police station with her lover to file a missing person report for her husband. After the child's statement, the policemen who reached the house informed the police station. Following this, Pooja and her lover were taken into custody at the police station itself. The Kishni police station in-charge stated - On Wednesday morning at 10 AM, Pooja Dubey came to the police station with her lover Jitendra. She was talking about filing a missing person report for her brother Karan. Just then, her neighbors called. Information was received that Pooja, along with her lover, had murdered her brother Karan. Now she is trying to mislead the police. Pooja and Jitendra were taken into custody at the police station itself. Based on their confession, the body was also recovered on Wednesday evening. The body was hidden in the jungle near the river in Dharmgadpur village, about one and a half kilometers away from the house. There was a bullet wound in the head. Based on the statement of 10-year-old child Hrithik, Pooja, Jitendra, and Julie have been arrested. Brother Karan was unmarried; the lover had three children The deceased's elder brother Mohit alias Monu said, "Karan was unmarried. He was preparing for police recruitment. He had taken the Sub-Inspector recruitment exam on March 15-16. The exam went very well. He was hopeful of selection this time. Karan was the fifth among 4 sisters and two brothers." Pooja was the fourth among the siblings. She was married 15 years ago. Pooja has 3 children. She had been having an affair with Jitendra for about 5 years. Jitendra is married and also has three children. SP said - Murder happened due to illicit relations, son exposed it SP City Arun Kumar said- Karan was shot dead due to illicit relations. The youth's murderers have been arrested. Elder sister Pooja, lover Jitendra alias Jeetu, and Jitendra's brother Juli are accused of murder. All three are being interrogated.

stories.title: SP leader targeted with thallium poisoning:Wife files FIR in Varanasi, Mumbai hospital confirms toxin
stories.summary: A case has emerged in Varanasi where an attempt was made to kill an SP leader by poisoning him with thallium. A doctor from a renowned hospital in Mumbai has confirmed the presence of thallium traces in the SP leader's blood. After the investigation report came, the SP leader's wife filed an FIR against unknown persons. On Wednesday, the police registered a case at Varanasi's Kotwali police station on the complaint of Khushboo Singh. SP leader Sandeep Singh (41) has served as the national general secretary of the Samajwadi Chhatra Sabha. According to his wife, he was admitted to Medanta, Gurugram, in February 2025 after his health suddenly deteriorated. As his condition did not improve, he was admitted to Max Hospital Delhi. When there was no benefit there either, he was taken to PD Ahuja Hospital in Mumbai via air ambulance, where doctors confirmed thallium poisoning. Now, who is Sandeep Singh? Sandeep Singh, a resident of Varanasi, has been the National General Secretary of the Samajwadi Chhatra Sabha (Samajwadi Student Assembly). He also operates two transport companies named SSS Infotech Private Limited and Shiv Enterprises. The transport companies are also involved in construction work. The company also handles the transportation of asphalt, gravel, etc., for road construction. Sandeep Singh's family includes his father Ghanshyam Singh, mother Poornima Singh, wife Khushboo Singh, daughter Swapnil, and son Prahan. What are the allegations in the FIR? Wife Khushboo Singh stated in a complaint filed with the police on Wednesday that her husband stayed at Medanta Hospital Gurugram from February 4, 2025, to February 11, 2025, after an acquaintance, Shiv Prasad, fell ill. He returned on February 12 to attend her brother's wedding. After the wedding, he went back to Medanta on February 22. While there, he developed a fever and tingling in his feet on February 26. His condition worsened after body pain and vomiting. After his condition deteriorated further, he was admitted to Medanta Gurugram on March 2, 2025. On March 5, his brother-in-law, Ajit Singh, went to meet him. Doctors stated that the illness was not being identified. Upon receiving information from her brother-in-law, I myself arrived. Could not understand the illness for a month, was put on ventilator support From there, he was admitted to Max Super Speciality Hospital Delhi on March 8, 2025. He remained admitted to Max until March 22, but instead of improving, his condition started to worsen. On March 22, he was shifted to the ICU. As his condition deteriorated further, he was put on a ventilator on March 23. Airlifted to Hinduja Hospital Wife Khushboo Singh said, "We were very worried. Doctors also couldn't understand the illness. After his condition worsened significantly, my husband was brought by air ambulance to P.D. Hinduja Hospital, Mahim, Mumbai." Here, doctors examined. Dr. Medha Dhamane, after seeing the report, stated that thallium poison was found in her husband's blood. This rare poison is used to kill someone. However, he was treated at Hinduja for a few days. After this, he was discharged. Currently, Sandeep is at his home in Lucknow. He is undergoing treatment at home under the supervision of doctors. Police registered an FIR Kotwali Police Station in-charge Dayashankar Singh said- Based on the complaint filed by Khushboo Singh, a case of attempt to murder has been registered under Section 109(1) of BNS. Now know about Thallium. What is Thallium? Thallium is used as a slow poison. Thallium is a very soft substance that can be easily mixed into anything. It is grey in color, but its color fades when exposed to air. It has no taste of its own. This is why if it is mixed in food, the person eating it does not feel any change in the taste of the food, nor does the color of the food change. How does Thallium work? Thallium acts slowly. After consuming it, common symptoms like headache, vomiting, and diarrhea appear. Therefore, no one even thinks that it is the effect of a poison, but slowly, it starts damaging internal organs. First, it weakens the nervous system. It completely destroys the ability to think and comprehend. Memory starts to weaken. After this, it affects the body's muscles. After a few days of use, extreme weakness is felt throughout the body. Within three weeks, the person goes into a coma.

stories.title: Class 9 student gang-raped in Gorakhpur:10 accused committ crime in different hotels; survivor had gone missing 4 months ago
stories.summary: A Class 9 student from Gorakhpur was allegedly subjected to sexual assault by multiple men over a period of time, police said. According to officials, the minor had left home for school at around 9 am on November 1 but did not return, prompting her family to search for her. When their efforts failed, a missing person complaint was lodged at the local police station on November 7. Police registered a case and initiated an investigation. The girl was eventually traced and recovered on March 23. . During interrogation, the student revealed that she had gone away under the influence of a young man. After that, 10 people raped her on different days in various hotels. Police conducted a medical examination of the student, which confirmed the rape. Based on call details, police caught a young man accused of taking the student away. After this, 10 people including hotel operators were taken into custody. On Wednesday, police presented 4 accused in court and sent them to jail. The incident is from Chaurichaura police station area. Student went missing 4 months ago A 14-year-old student from the Chaurichaura area studies in class 9. The student's father works as a laborer in Gujarat. According to police, on November 1, 2025, she had left home to go to school. During this time, she met a young man on the way. It is alleged that the young man lured her and took her with him. When the student did not return home by evening, the family members became worried. They searched extensively in the surrounding areas, but could not find any trace of her. After this, the family members reached the police station and filed a complaint on November 7. The police registered a case against unknown persons and started investigation. After searching for a long time, on March 23, the police recovered the student. After this, when the police examined the student's call details, shocking information came to light. The investigation revealed that she had been taken to several hotels. The police took action and detained 10 accused for questioning. During interrogation, they confessed to their crime. Police are currently questioning 6 people The police arrested accused Kishan alias Bittu, Sameer alias Dilshad, Monu alias Manish Rajbhar and hotel operator Dharmraj and presented them in court, from where all were sent to jail. Meanwhile, six other accused have been detained and the police are questioning them. SP North Gyanendra Kumar informed - After recovering the minor student, her statement was recorded in court. The student has alleged that she was taken to different places and raped by 10 people. Based on this, 4 accused have been arrested and sent to jail. The role of other accused is being investigated.

stories.title: Amity student drowns in water-filled pit in Noida:Went for picnic with friends after exams, slipped into deep water
stories.summary: A 23-year-old student of Amity University in Noida, Harshit Bhatt, died after drowning in a water-filled pit on Wednesday evening. Harshit had gone for a picnic with three friends after finishing his exams. During the outing, he entered the pit, went into the deeper section and began to drown. His friends tried to rescue him but failed. They then alerted the police. Teams reached the spot with divers, pulled him out and rushed him to a hospital, where doctors declared him dead. BPEd student, father posted in Ladakh According to DCP Saad Mian Khan, Harshit was pursuing a Bachelor of Physical Education (BPEd) and was in his sixth semester. His father serves in the Indian Army and is currently posted in Ladakh. He is survived by a brother and a sister. Police said the four students had appeared for an exam earlier and later consumed alcohol before going to an empty plot. They entered the pit to bathe. During questioning, his friends said they had used the pit earlier as well, but this time Harshit moved into deeper water and drowned. Police, along with SDRF and NDRF teams, reached the spot within about 20 minutes of receiving information. He was pulled out and taken to hospital, where he was declared dead. Earlier case: engineer died after car fell into pit This is not the first such incident in Noida. On January 16, 27-year-old software engineer Yuvraj Mehta died after his car fell into a nearly 30-foot-deep, water-filled pit. Around midnight, Yuvraj was driving towards Tata Eureka Park when, due to dense fog, he could not see the road clearly. His car broke through a drain wall near Sector 150 and plunged into a pit dug for a mall basement. He managed to climb onto the roof of the sinking car and called his father, pleading for help. Despite rescue efforts by police, fire services and SDRF teams, his body was recovered after nearly two-and-a-half hours. Safety lapses flagged after earlier death Following the January incident, action was taken against officials. Then Noida Authority CEO Ritu Maheshwari was removed, citing administrative negligence. Yogi Adityanath had ordered an SIT probe into the case. Authorities had directed that water be drained from open pits, barricading be installed and drains be covered within 15 days. However, the latest incident has again raised concerns over safety compliance at such sites.

stories.title: AAP to lose by sidelining Raghav Chadha, says Avimukteshwaranand:Calls him ‘An asset to the country’; MP responds with gratitude
stories.summary: Swami Avimukteshwaranand has entered the ongoing row between the Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) and its Rajya Sabha MP Raghav Chadha, calling Chadha “an asset to the nation” and saying the party may be harming itself. Speaking in a podcast, the Shankaracharya said Chadha’s political stature has grown beyond the party and is now based on his own work. His remarks come days after AAP removed Chadha from the post of deputy leader in the Rajya Sabha. Chadha shared excerpts of the podcast on social media on Wednesday, writing a note of respect for the Shankaracharya. Shankaracharya backs Raghav Chadha, calls him ‘an asset to the country’ Swami Avimukteshwaranand said Raghav Chadha earned public appreciation for consistently raising issues of ordinary citizens in Parliament. He recalled that Chadha had once called him seeking blessings after the birth of his son. “The way he stood in Parliament and spoke for the common man was appreciated across the country,” he said. At the same time, the seer noted that a political party has the right to decide how it presents issues. “If the party feels matters should be raised in its own way, that is its internal system. No one else can interfere in that,” he added. ‘He has now become a leader beyond party lines’ The Shankaracharya said Chadha’s interventions in Parliament led to action on several public issues, raising expectations among people. “Now he is not limited to a party. He has become an individual identity. Wherever he goes, people will expect him to raise their concerns,” he said. He added that if given an opportunity, the public would continue to support him electorally. “If one platform does not allow him, people will send him from another place to raise their voice,” he said. ‘An asset to the country’ On reports of differences within the Aam Aadmi Party, the Shankaracharya refused to comment on internal decisions. “This is their matter. We are not their advisors and will not give unsolicited advice,” he said. However, he strongly backed Chadha’s leadership. “His future is bright. A person who speaks for the people cannot fail. He is polite, presents facts and is soft-spoken. Such leaders are rare. He is an asset to our country,” he said. ‘Party may be harming itself’ The seer suggested that the party’s move could be counterproductive. “The Aam Aadmi Party may be harming itself. Political calculations may be different, but the public perception about him is positive,” he said, adding that Chadha’s stature has grown significantly. Visit after wedding with Parineeti Chopra The Shankaracharya had visited Chadha’s Delhi residence in October 2024 after his wedding with Parineeti Chopra. He attended a special paduka puja and blessing ceremony, where he was given a ceremonial welcome. Chadha had shared the visit on social media, calling it a memorable moment soon after his marriage.

stories.title: Mafia Ashraf’s aide killed in broad daylight:Shot at tea shop in Prayagraj; land dispute angle emerges
stories.summary: The incident occurred around 6:30 PM near Bismillah Chowk. Irfan was sitting at a tea shop close to his house when four attackers arrived on two motorcycles. All had covered their faces with gamchas. According to eyewitness accounts, three attackers remained seated on the bikes while one got down, approached Irfan, pulled out a pistol and shot him in the chest at point-blank range. He collapsed on the spot, bleeding heavily. The attackers then brandished the weapon, mounted their bikes and fled. Taken to hospital, declared dead Locals immediately informed Irfan’s family, who live about 250 metres away in Ainuddinpur. His wife and son rushed to the spot and took him to SRN Hospital, where doctors declared him dead. The killing led to chaos and fear in the area. See 2 pictures- Family alleges role of gangster-linked accused Irfan was reportedly a close associate of Ashraf Ahmad and had worked as his driver around 12 years ago. His family has accused Asif Durrani (45), his brother Rashid, and others of carrying out the murder. Durrani, a resident of Chakiya, is known to be linked to the gang of Atiq Ahmad. An FIR has been registered at Kareli police station based on a complaint by Irfan’s son, Mohammad Aamir. Land dispute suspected as motive Police said preliminary investigation points to a property dispute as the possible motive. Both Irfan and Durrani were involved in land dealings and had ongoing conflicts over transactions. Officials said the exact reason behind the murder will be confirmed after further investigation. Accused has long criminal history Police records show that Asif Durrani has over 17 cases registered against him at Dhumanganj police station. He has been named in multiple FIRs alongside Atiq Ahmad. In 2020, he was booked in an illegal slaughterhouse case, and in 2021, authorities demolished his house under anti-mafia action. Cases related to witness intimidation have also been filed against him, and gangster charges have been invoked multiple times. Kareli SHO Ashish Singh said the case would become clearer after Durrani’s arrest. Police scan 50+ cctv cameras Following the murder, police and forensic teams reached the spot and collected evidence. Investigators examined footage from more than 50 CCTV cameras in the area. Although the suspects were spotted in some clips, their identities could not be clearly established as their faces were covered. Post-mortem today The body has been sent for post-mortem, which will be conducted on Thursday. Irfan is survived by his wife Mangrul Nisha, two sons — Mohammad Aamir and Faisal — and two daughters. Family members gathered at the hospital, demanding answers over the killing.

stories.title: 'Now I have to support my national-level player daughter':Mother alleges son-in-law tried to hang daughter in Kashi
stories.summary: “Ask a mother. The daughter who once supported me, I have been supporting her for the last 10 months. She used to bring home medals. Today, I am asking for justice for her, which we have not received so far. Her husband left her to die and is now threatening us too.” These are the words of Nisha Singh, mother of national volleyball player Priya Singh, who is now unable to speak properly. Priya had topped her MP Ed from Kashi Vidyapeeth and was known for her achievements in sports. Condition worsens after alleged attack According to the family, the incident took place in July 2025. Nisha Singh alleges that Priya’s husband tried to kill her by hanging her with a noose. She survived, but lost her ability to speak and suffered memory loss. Since then, Priya has been dependent on her family for daily care. Her mother says her condition has not improved significantly. Mother approaches commissioner On 7 April, Nisha Singh reached Commissioner Mohit Agarwal with her daughter, seeking action in the case. She said the family has not received justice so far and is also facing threats. The Commissioner assured her that the matter would be looked into and that she would get justice. Family demands strict action Nisha Singh has demanded strict action against the accused. She says the delay in justice has added to their suffering. She also warned that if justice is not delivered, she may take an extreme step along with her daughter. Case raises serious questions The case highlights concerns over delays in action in serious assault cases and the safety of victims and their families after such incidents. Bhaskar spoke to Nisha Singh to understand how Priya’s condition worsened and what the family expects from the administration. First, take a look at Priya’s wedding photographs—moments filled with happiness and celebration. Then, see what followed… National volleyball player left speech-impaired, mother alleges attempt to murder; seeks action In a small house in Parmanandpur, Varanasi, medals and trophies line the walls—reminders of a sporting career that once brought pride to the family. Today, those same medals are silently watched by Priya Singh, a national volleyball player who can no longer speak properly or recall much of her past. Her mother, Nisha Singh, says their life changed months after Priya’s marriage. Marriage followed by alleged harassment According to Nisha, Priya was married on February 25, 2025, to Amit Kumar Verma, a junior engineer posted in Gorakhpur. The family claims they spent around ₹8 lakh on the wedding. Within a month, Priya allegedly began facing harassment. Nisha says her son-in-law pressured Priya to transfer family land in his name. When the family resisted, the harassment allegedly turned violent. July incident leaves Priya critical On July 8, 2025, at around 3 am, Nisha received a call from her in-laws claiming Priya had died by suicide in Gorakhpur. “When we reached, she was alive but critical,” Nisha said. Priya was first admitted to AIIMS Gorakhpur and later shifted to Lucknow and then to KGMU for specialised care. She remained in a coma for seven days and spent over three weeks in the ICU. Doctors found severe damage to her vocal cords, which has left her with difficulty in speaking. FIR filed, family alleges weak charges The family lodged a complaint at Shivpur police station in Varanasi on July 8. However, Nisha alleges that the case was registered under minor sections despite the seriousness of the incident. She claims no arrests have been made so far and alleges that the accused’s government position influenced the handling of the case. “From supporting us to needing support” Priya, who topped her M.P.Ed from Mahatma Gandhi Kashi Vidyapith and captained its volleyball team, now struggles to speak even basic sentences. Sitting beside her medals, she tries to recall her achievements but often falls silent. Her mother says Priya cannot remember the day of the incident. “She was our support. Today, she needs support,” Nisha said. Police response SDCP Varuna Zone Neetu Kadyan said a case has been registered and the investigation is ongoing. “If any negligence is found, action will be taken. The culprits will not be spared,” she said. Family continues to seek justice Over the past months, Nisha says she has approached multiple officials, including senior police officers, but has not seen progress in the case. The family continues to demand stricter charges and immediate action, as Priya undergoes treatment and struggles to rebuild her life.

stories.title: UP farmer breaks down as hailstorm destroys crop:Hail blankets Hardoi, alert in 44 districts
stories.summary: A farmer in Hardoi broke down in tears after seeing his crop destroyed by rain and hail. Unseasonal storms, rain and hail continue to batter Uttar Pradesh. The weather department has issued a rain alert for 44 districts on Thursday, warning of strong winds reaching speeds of up to 60 kmph. While Lucknow and Varanasi saw clear skies with cool breezes, several other regions reported changing weather patterns. In Mathura, light fog was seen in rural areas on Thursday morning after days of rainfall. Cloud cover persisted across 10 western districts, including Agra, while parts of eastern Uttar Pradesh witnessed mild sunshine. In Hardoi, farmer Satiram was seen weeping inconsolably as he surveyed his damaged wheat crop. Showing his rain-soaked fields, he said, “Oh God, what do we do now?” On Wednesday evening, hailstorms hit six cities, including Bareilly and Meerut. In Saharanpur and Hardoi, heavy hail turned roads and fields white, resembling a blanket of snow. Over the past 24 hours, rainfall was recorded in 30 districts of the state. According to the weather department, the state received an average rainfall of 2.8 mm — nearly 200% above normal. The highest temperature in the state was recorded at 38.6°C in Banda. Lucknow-based meteorologist Atul Singh said the current western disturbance will weaken by Thursday, but a fresh system will become active from April 11. This could once again worsen weather conditions, bringing rain accompanied by strong winds and a drop in temperature by 6 to 8 degrees Celsius. Weather scenes from across Uttar Pradesh…

stories.title: 15 accused, multi-city kidney racket:Doctor brought surgical team from Meerut; Kanpur OT used for illicit surgeries
stories.summary: A large-scale illegal kidney transplant racket, originating from Ahuja Hospital in Kanpur, has exposed a well-organised network spanning nine hospitals across four cities in Uttar Pradesh. Investigations reveal that over 50 kidney transplants were carried out, with patients charged between ₹50 lakh and ₹2.5 crore. The racket came to light after a Bihar-based victim alleged he was underpaid for donating his kidney. Following the complaint, police cracked down on the network, arresting several individuals while others remain absconding. How the racket operated The network used agents, doctors, technicians, and hospital operators to identify donors and recipients. Poor and vulnerable individuals were lured through social media and messaging platforms, often with promises of ₹5–10 lakh. Illegal surgeries were conducted secretly, mostly between 3 am and 4 am, with hospital staff kept away and CCTV cameras switched off. The 15 key accused and their roles 1. Dr Preeti Ahuja Owner of Ahuja Hospital and one of the main accused. A qualified physician, she allegedly allowed her hospital to be used for illegal transplants. 2. Dr Surjit Singh Ahuja Her husband and co-operator of the hospital. He managed finances, coordinated doctors, and oversaw operations. 3. Shivam Agarwal alias Shivam Kada An 8th-pass agent and key middleman. He identified donors and recipients through social media and arranged deals. 4. Dr Rohit (absconding) An anaesthesiologist who allegedly handled critical medical procedures and coordinated surgeries. 5. Dr Mudassir Ali Played a central role in surgeries, including removing and transplanting kidneys. 6. Dr Afzal Handled patient coordination and brought donors and recipients to Kanpur. 7. Dr Ram Prakash Kushwaha Operator of Medi Life Hospital, where patients were admitted before and after surgeries. 8. Dr Rajesh Kumar Associated with Medi Life Hospital; managed patient care and records. 9. Dr Narendra Singh alias Nandu Operator of Preeti Hospital, where patients were shifted post-surgery. 10. Parvez Saifi Driver and logistics handler who transported doctors, patients, and money. 11. Naveen Pandey (absconding) Allegedly linked to deal negotiations and pricing within the racket. 12. Kuldeep Singh Raghav OT technician who assisted in surgeries and coordinated with doctors. 13. Rajesh Kumar (OT technician) Experienced technician who assisted during operations for payment per case. 14. Dr Vaibhav A dentist whose role in transplant procedures is under investigation. 15. Amit alias Anurag (absconding) Linked to Alpha Hospital; suspected of coordinating with key doctors in the network. Expanding network across hospitals Investigators found that the racket extended beyond Ahuja Hospital, with links to Medi Life Hospital, Preeti Hospital, and Alpha Hospital in Meerut, among others. Patients were often moved between facilities to avoid suspicion. Police action so far Key concerns raised The case has raised serious questions about: What happens next Police are continuing raids to arrest absconding accused and trace financial links. Authorities are also examining whether more hospitals and medical professionals were involved.

stories.title: Chain pulled to stop Punjab Mail for Uma Bharti:Train halted for 5 minutes in Jhansi; former CM claims it departed ahead of schedule
stories.summary: Former Chief Minister Uma Bharti had to stop the Punjab Mail by chain pulling at Jhansi on Sunday. When Uma Bharti reached the platform, the Punjab Mail going to New Delhi had already departed. The train had left half the platform. Uma's supporters immediately stopped the train. She had to board the First AC coach A-1 of the train. But by the time the train stopped, coach A-1 had reached the yard. Therefore, she boarded coach B-1. Due to the chain pulling, the train's brake air had been released. The train stood for 5 minutes, half on the platform and half in the yard. After Uma Bharti boarded the train, the train was sent forward. Uma Bharti said- The train had departed ahead of schedule. This entire incident is a result of railway mismanagement. What happened to me today is happening to passengers every day. Such difficulties frequently occur at stations like Mathura, Jhansi, and Lalitpur. Women run around on platforms with luggage and children. The elderly and differently-abled face the most trouble.Uma Bharti had to board Third AC. Now know the complete matterUma Bharti's claim - Reached the station at 2:18 PMFormer CM Uma Bharti claimed that she arrived at Jhansi Railway Station on Sunday afternoon at 2:18 PM. The train was at 2:23 PM.Uma Bharti said - I was going by escalator, but the officers asked me to go by e-cart. After walking some distance, a train passed in front of the e-cart, so we had to stand there for five minutes. Then a hand trolley came out. Due to this, the train was missed.Wrote a letter to Rail Minister on X - Lack of sensitivity at the stationUma Bharti has written a letter to Rail Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw on social media X after the incident. Uma Bharti said, I have previously written about the insensitivity towards passengers at Mathura Railway Station. Today again, an incident happened with me while boarding at Jhansi Railway Station in which there is no criminal, but the lack of practical sensitivity in the construction of modern facilities at stations has become the cause.Officers asked to go by e-cart. After this, Uma Bharti went to the platform by e-cart.CCTV should be retrievedUma Bharti wrote - CCTV footage of Jhansi Railway Station should be retrieved. I had reached Jhansi Railway Station before the train arrived and this train came before the scheduled time and departed before the scheduled time. I was being taken in a battery cart from platform number 1 towards number 4. Meanwhile, a train passed on the same track for a long time and we stood waiting.Then when we moved a little ahead, a handcart was stuck in the track. My security personnel helped in removing it. Then when I reached platform number 4 and the train Punjab Mail in which I had to board was leaving. Who pulled the chain, I have no idea, and I was made to board the train. Will tell about Mathura and Jhansi incidents togetherUma further wrote- Everything was according to time, there was no mistake by anyone. Three-four minutes of the train went bad for me. The first reason for this was the train arriving before time and leaving 2 minutes before time.Mistake of Officials Operating the TrainUma Bharti said, leave me aside, but common people, differently-abled persons, elderly, women and men carrying a lot of luggage and women with children in their laps become victims of mismanagement. I do not consider it the fault of Jhansi Railway officials at all, nor do I consider it my fault. This entire system was created by the officials operating the train inside the railway. I will tell you again to pay attention to these mismanagements.Railway's Claim - Train Departed on TimeAccording to the National Train Enquiry System, the train arrived at platform 4 at 2:09 PM, 6 minutes before its scheduled time of 2:15 PM. After that, it was supposed to depart at 2:23 PM after an 8-minute stop, and the train departed at its scheduled time. Later, when it was stopped by chain pulling, it departed again at 2:28 PM.Divisional Railway Manager Aniruddh Kumar informed-The chain pulling of the Mumbai-Firozpur Punjab Mail was not done by Uma Bharti. Some passengers who had gotten down on the Jhansi station platform to get food and water, when they saw that the train was starting to move, their fellow passengers pulled the chain. It doesn't happen in the railway system that a train leaves the platform before the scheduled time. Yes, it is true that trains do arrive at the station before the scheduled time. Still, we are investigating the matter whether the train was run before time or not.

Who ordered firing on kar sevaks in Ayodhya?:Former IAS says most decisions are political; also replies to Akhilesh Yadav
stories.summary: A senior official linked to the Ram Temple project has spoken about the Ayodhya demolition issue and the claims of firing on karsevaks. He said most such decisions are political, not taken by top officials alone. Nripendra Misra, chairman of the Ram Temple Construction Committee and a former IAS officer, spoke in Ayodhya on Saturday. He said decisions like these are not made at the chief secretary level. He added that around 90 percent of such decisions are political, while only 10 percent include inputs from officers like the Home Secretary, Chief Secretary and Director General of Police. His remarks come amid ongoing political debate on the issue. Two months ago, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav raised the matter in Parliament during a discussion on MNREGA. Akhilesh said MNREGA had been renamed “VBG Ramji”. He pointed towards BJP MP Arun Govil and asked where “Ramji” was. He said people have seen him since childhood and questioned why he was seated at the back in the Lok Sabha. He added that he should be brought forward and given seat number 2." During this, ruling party MPs said - those who fired on Karsevaks are talking. Hearing this, Akhilesh flared up. He said - those who ordered the firing are building the Ram Temple. If you don't know something, go and ask, find out. Don't come here with incomplete information. When the firing took place, I was the Secretary During the press conference, Nripendra Misra was asked about Akhilesh Yadav questioning him on the firing on Kar Sevaks in Ayodhya in 1990. At that time, you were the Principal Secretary. To this, Nripendra Misra said, yes, I was the Principal Secretary in Mulayam Singh Yadav's government. But such decisions are not made at the level of the Chief Secretary. About 90 percent of such decisions are political, and in 10 percent of decisions, suggestions received from the Home Secretary, Chief Secretary, and Director General of Police are included. He (Akhilesh) is the son of a respected leader of the country. Therefore, he must have all the information. Nripendra Misra explained the difference between Mulayam and Kalyan's tenures Nripendra Misra also mentioned his tenure under different governments, which included the tenure of former Chief Minister, the late Mulayam Singh Yadav. He also explained the difference in the distinct approaches adopted by these two leaders during times of crisis. Nripendra Misra said, "I have worked as Chief Secretary for both former Chief Ministers, Mulayam Singh Yadav and Kalyan Singh. You might also know that when a report was presented to Kalyan Singh in 1992 stating that law and order had completely deteriorated in Ayodhya, he gave a written order that there would be no firing of any kind in this holy city." Police fired bullets in Ayodhya on October 30 and November 2 During Mulayam Singh Yadav's tenure, on October 30 and November 2, 1990, police fired on Kar Sevaks, at which time a large number of devotees of Lord Ram had gathered in Ayodhya as part of the Vishwa Hindu Parishad's 'Kar Seva'. According to reports, more than 28 people died in the police firing on unarmed Kar Sevaks. Former Chief Minister Mulayam Singh Yadav later said, This action was taken on his orders, and he justified it, stating it was necessary for the security of the disputed structure and to maintain national unity. In contrast, during the demolition of the disputed structure on December 6, 1992, the then Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, Kalyan Singh, had instructed that despite the extremely tense situation, no firing should be opened on the karsevaks. It is said that Kalyan Singh had stated that karsevaks would not be fired upon for the sake of a building. Later, on the evening of December 6, 1992, after the demolition of the disputed structure, he resigned from the post of Chief Minister.

stories.title: Severe heat to hit Uttar Pradesh, mercury to cross 40°C:Strong sunshine and dusty winds expected, no rain likely for next 2 weeks
stories.summary: Summer has started to show its strong impact across Uttar Pradesh. Since Sunday morning, the sky has remained clear with bright sunshine and steady winds. The Meteorological Department has said that temperatures will cross 40°C during the day today. Dusty winds are expected to blow at a speed of 25 to 35 km/h, and in some areas, people may feel heatwave-like conditions. The department said that the effect of the Western Disturbance has now ended, leading to a rise in heat. No new weather system is expected to become active in the next 15 days. Because of this, there is no chance of rain, and the heat is likely to increase sharply. The maximum temperature may rise by up to 8°C, while the minimum temperature could go up by 6°C. In the last 24 hours, Prayagraj and Jhansi recorded the highest temperatures at 37.6°C. Varanasi and Jalaun were close behind at 37.4°C. Strong winds were seen in many districts, including Lucknow. Due to this, nights felt slightly cooler despite the rising daytime heat. Atul Kumar Singh, Senior Scientist at the Regional Meteorological Center, Lucknow, said- The weather will remain clear in the state for the next two weeks. There are no chances of rain. The wind direction will change. Humidity in the atmosphere will decrease due to winds coming from the east. The heat will further increase. The average temperature of night and day may increase by 6 to 8 degrees Celsius. Today's weather pictures- How will the weather be for the next 5 days? Farmers get relief as weather clears Agricultural experts say that farmers have got relief as the weather has cleared. This is because the harvested wheat crops had gotten wet. With strong sunlight, the crops will dry quickly. This will allow farmers to thresh as soon as possible. The chances of the crop grains turning black will be reduced. What was the reason for the sudden storm and rain? The sudden storm and rain were due to a Western Disturbance. This is normal for this season. Every year, during this season, there is rain with storms. However, this year, Western Disturbances are occurring very frequently. Because of this, the weather has been continuously stormy and rainy. Farmers suffered losses, wheat crop in crisis Untimely rains caused heavy losses to farmers. The wheat crop was destroyed. Regarding this, CM Yogi had instructed officials to go into the field. He had said that officials should survey the damage within 24 hours and compensation should be given to the affected farmers as soon as possible. No kind of negligence will be tolerated. Providing help to farmers is the government's priority.

stories.title: 4 videos show final moments before Vrindavan boat accident:Punjab youth seen singing ‘Nazar Saawre Lag Na Jaye’; death toll rises to 13
stories.summary: Four videos of devotees from Punjab, taken before the boat accident in the Yamuna River in Vrindavan, Mathura, have surfaced. In them, the scene just before the accident is clearly visible, with devotees seen singing bhajans. It can be clearly seen in the video that none of the devotees was wearing life jackets for safety. Everyone was chanting 'Radhe-Radhe' and performing bhajan-kirtan. Bhajans were being sung to the rhythm of dholak and manjira. A young man is singing a bhajan while playing the manjira - ‘Nazar Sanware Lag Na Jaye Kahin...’ Death toll rises to 13 The rescue operation continued on Sunday for the third day. A team of about 250 people, including the army, NDRF-SDRF, is involved in the operation. The search area has now been increased from 14 km to 20 km. So far, 13 devotees from Punjab have died in this accident. 22 people have been rescued. 3 are still missing. This morning, two more bodies were found. They were identified as Dinky from Dugri (Ludhiana), Punjab, and Rishabh Sharma from Jagraon. According to the administration, the bodies had bloated and floated to the surface of the river. Using ropes, the bodies were pulled into a boat and brought out. Family members identified both. Dinky was a final year BA student. Rishabh had passed 12th grade and used to assist his father in his work. What is visible in all four videos Find out how the accident happened A young man who survived the accident said- The boat was in the middle of the Yamuna river, about 50 feet from the bank. The wind was blowing at a speed of about 40 km per hour. The boat suddenly started to wobble. The boatman lost control. The tourists said that the bridge was approaching, stop the boat, but he did not listen. Twice the boat narrowly avoided hitting the bridge, but on the third time, it collided and sank.

stories.title: Punjab Banke Bihari Club linked to 13 deaths:Friends sang devotional songs, then organised Vrindavan trips; charged ₹4500 per devotee
stories.summary: 13 devotees died in the boat accident in Vrindavan. All of them were taken on a religious trip by the Banke Bihari Club of Jagraon, Ludhiana. This club was formed about 9 years ago by two real brothers and their friend. In the same accident, one of these two brothers also died. They started with 'sankirtan' (devotional singing) in temples at the age of 16-17. Then the three of them together formed this club. It was not registered. After this, people gradually joined the club. The club performs 'sankirtan' from house to house. 5 years ago, they started organizing trips to Vrindavan. This time, on April 9, they took 130 devotees to Vrindavan in 2 buses. Each devotee was charged 4,500 rupees. The accident happened on April 10, in which 13 devotees died. stories.title: Yogi says UP bulldozer will act in Bengal:Claims only BJP can tackle rioters; Mamata accused of Muslim vote bank politics
stories.summary: CM Yogi said in West Bengal on Sunday - TMC people want half the population to speak Urdu. Tell them to go where Urdu is spoken. Only Bangla will be spoken in Bengal. UP's bulldozer will treat the goons in Bengal. The bulldozer doesn't just build roads, it also treats mafias. It crushes the ribs of those who play with the honor of daughters. The CM called TMC leaders traders of Muslim vote bank. He said- In UP, namaz is no longer read on the streets. There is no sound of shouting from mosques. There is a strict law for love jihad. Cow slaughter cannot happen. Every daughter, every businessman is safe. Every hand has work, every field has water. Even Congress and SP could not stop UP's development.Yogi said - The hooliganism that exists in Bengal today was the same in UP 9 years ago. There were riots on every festival and celebration. Curfews would be imposed for months. Businesses would remain shut. Parallel to the government, goons and mafia used to rule. In 2017, a double engine government came to UP. Now in UP, there is no appeasement, there is satisfaction.Yogi said-There are no riots in UP now. No curfew, no riots, everything is fine in UP. All the mafia that were there have gone on a journey to hell. Now there is no mafia. There are no goons. Now every citizen is safe there. Only BJP can cure goons and mafia.Yogi said these things while campaigning for the assembly elections. He held a total of 3 rallies. First he reached Sonamukhi in Bankura district. After this, he held public meetings in Nandakumar and Kanthi South in Purba Medinipur.Yogi campaigned for the assembly elections in West Bengal.5 Major Points from Yogi's Speech1. BJP government will treat the riotersYogi said- Bengal has now started moving towards change. Today it is painful to see the plight of Bengal. First Congress, then the Left parties and now TMC have ruined it. Mamata Banerjee's government has made Bengal bankrupt. TMC has turned Bengal's land of nationalism into a land of appeasement. It has been turned into a land of loot, plunder and anarchy.He said - As soon as Bengal's name comes up, one remembers the two great men who gave us the National Anthem and National Song. In Ayodhya, a movement for Ram Janmabhoomi continued for several hundred years. A large number of kar sevaks had also gone from Bengal. People used to say that the temple would not be built, but when the double engine government came, the temple was built.2. Bengal's farmers are troubled, potatoes are selling at one rupee per kiloYogi said - We are surprised to see what kind of havoc has occurred in Bengal. Worker Suman Padri was shot dead. The homes of workers like Swarup and Palas Ghosh were destroyed. Someone's hand was cut off.Farmers were harassed. Bengal's farmer is feeling exploited. They are not getting proper prices. In UP, potatoes are available at 15-16 rupees per kilo, but in Bengal their price is 1 to 1.5 rupees.Yogi addressed a public meeting in Sonamukhi, Bankura district in Bengal for the assembly election campaign.3. There are many possibilities in Bengal, bring BJP to powerYogi said - Youth are getting jobs in UP. There are new possibilities for the poor. 15 crore people are getting free ration. 10 crore people are getting treatment worth 5 lakh through Ayushman Bharat. 65 lakh poor people have received PM housing.9 lakh youth have been given government jobs. Employment arrangements have been made in industries for 3 crore youth. This work can also be done in Bengal. There are many possibilities in Bengal. You just have to bring BJP to power.4. Mamata's Fear - Lest Muslim Votes Slip AwayYogi said - Recently a Dalit Hindu was murdered in Bangladesh. BJP protested, but Mamata Didi remained silent. She was afraid that if she spoke, her Muslim vote bank might slip away. These vote bank traders want to change Bengal's demography.You have time. Don't let them off the hook. These people work to create obstacles during Navratri celebrations. Now we should not accept these things. This is the best time, we must come together to restore Bengal's former glory.Yogi said - As soon as Bengal's name comes, one remembers the two great men who gave us the national anthem and national song 5. Said in Bengal - Bengal will not remain silent During the speech, Yogi also spoke in Bengali. He said - 'Banglar chup thakbe na' meaning Bengal will not remain silent now. Now khela (game) will end, development will begin. For this, BJP's double engine is necessary.

stories.title: 'Father never allowed his daughter to meet anyone':Relatives claim he avoided taking her to hospital, due to alleged black magic practice
stories.summary: A father lived in the house with his daughter's corpse for 4 months in Meerut. To prevent the smell, he would spray perfume. Finally, the decomposed skeleton of daughter Priyanka was found. Neighbours and relatives suspect that Priyanka's father, Udaybhanu, used to visit babas (godmen) for her treatment. According to neighbours, the father was never seen taking his daughter to the hospital. It is feared that due to faith healing rituals, her condition worsened, leading to her death. To hide the death, Udaybhanu kept sitting with his daughter's corpse hidden in the house. Relatives say the father did not want to get his daughter married. He would not talk to anyone. If someone approached him to discuss this matter, he would evade the conversation. From what we have learned about this case, only a psycho could do such a thing. Dainik Bhaskar team reached that house in Teli Mohalla and tried to understand the entire incident. First, know about the family and the incident- Hid daughter's death for 4 months, wife had also committed suicide In Sadar Teli Mohalla, Udaybhanu Biswas, retired from the Education Department, lived in his house with his 35-year-old daughter Priyanka. In this same house, Udaybhanu Biswas's wife had committed suicide by hanging. Udaybhanu's relatives also have houses around his house. After his wife's death, father and daughter were left alone in this house. For four months, no neighbour had seen daughter, Priyanka. Udaybhanu would often lock the house and go out. When he came once or twice in between, he told neighbors that his daughter was unwell. She is admitted to the hospital. He didn't say anything more than this. But on Friday night (10 April), his relatives living in the neighbourhood became suspicious. They caught Udaybhanu after spotting him sitting at a tea shop in Thaparnagar. They pressured him and asked where his daughter was. Later, when the police arrived and opened the gate of the house to look inside, they found the daughter's skeleton lying on the bed inside. Many empty perfume bottles were found nearby, and a pile of garbage had also accumulated inside the house. During police interrogation, Udaybhanu said that his daughter had died from jaundice. This is her corpse. He loves his daughter so much that he cannot leave her. Now read what people on the ground told... Father-daughter used to go somewhere daily by e-rickshaw Neighbor Kulbhushan Jain said that my shop is right opposite. Every day while opening the shop, I would see the father-daughter going somewhere by e-rickshaw. They would return in the evening. This was their routine. Since they didn't interact much with anyone, we never asked. Otherwise, we never saw them going to a doctor. The daughter would leave the house first and catch an e-rickshaw from the road. The father, Udaybhanu, would follow, and then both would go somewhere. They would return straight in the evening. In this same house, Udaybhanu's wife had committed suicide by hanging. Kept daughter away from phone, didn't give money for expenses There are some other shops right outside Udaybhanu's house. People from the market said that daughter Priyanka seemed somewhat mentally disturbed. Because she would often come out of the house onto the street. Coming onto the street, she would sometimes ask one person or another, through gestures, for some food items. She would say get me cheese or Kurkure, packets of chips. She never gave money. Just took the packet and went back inside the house. We also thought he was mentally weak, so we never asked him or his father for money, even for ₹5-10. We just thought that Udaybhanu had such a strange nature that he neither gave his daughter money for expenses nor gave her a phone. Even though he himself was retired from government service and was receiving a pension. People also said that apart from this house, Udaybhanu had also bought a flat ahead. Which even relatives don't know about. Relatives said- Talked to Priyanka one year ago Upon learning about the incident, Priyanka's cousin, Alpana, also reached the spot. Alpana said that whenever she came here, she would often meet Priyanka and Udaybhanu. I saw Priyanka for the last time about a year ago. She was very sweet-natured. She was quite educated. She had done MCA and MA. She used to study a lot. She didn't work anywhere; she stayed at home. We don't even know why Uncle wasn't getting her married. We told him once or twice to get his daughter married, but he avoided the topic. We also didn't say much more. She had also met at a wedding recently, and we had talked then. We don't think it's suicide, but she had jaundice. We don't know where her treatment was going on. Uncle used to meet at the temple during Durga Puja, and we would talk there. To me, it seems like a case of mental disturbance. Had limited interaction, even with neighbours and relatives Relative Rupa Biswas says, 'Udaybhanu is my uncle's father-in-law. We come and go in front of his house, but we never felt that a corpse was rotting inside the house. Uncle kept saying that Priyanka has jaundice'. She has been admitted to a hospital in Dehradun. We didn't know what was inside the house. Uncle didn't let anyone enter the house. After aunty's suicide, he had reduced talking to everyone. Neither Priyanka nor her father, Udaybhanu, used to talk much with anyone. When Priyanka's mother was alive, she used to meet neighbors and relatives. There used to be visits to their place on birthdays, weddings, or festivals. But Priyanka and Udaybhanu did not talk much with anyone. Both kept to themselves. They had reduced mixing with relatives. Mother also committed suicide due to depression Relatives said that Udaybhanu's wife, Sharmishtha, was also in depression. She never openly told relatives about her problems. But in conversations, she would say that Udaybhanu was involved in tantra-mantra (occult practices). He wouldn't go to a doctor for treatment. He wasn't letting their daughter get married either. Perhaps due to this depression, the wife also committed suicide inside the house. Behaviour changed after wife's suicide Relatives said that the behavior of both Priyanka and her father, Udaybhanu, completely changed after the wife's death. Both father and daughter would remain locked alone inside the house. Even when they went out, they wouldn't talk much to anyone. They had also reduced communication with us. After Aunty's death, relatives never went inside their house. Neither father nor daughter would talk to anyone on their own. Both would leave the house daily. They would go somewhere, but we don't know where they used to go. Then they would return in the evening. Father did this out of sympathy Akanksha is a staff nurse at the medical college. Akanksha said that I had come to Sadar for shopping on Friday. There was a huge crowd here. It was found that a father had beaten his daughter and locked her inside the house. The corpse is rotting inside the mortuary. The police did not let us go inside. But hearing about this incident is very frightening and also feels bad. Priyanka's age was also young. The father would not have wanted his daughter to be separated from him. That's why, out of sympathy, he probably kept his daughter's corpse. His mental condition must also be bad. Kept stopping the stench of the corpse with perfume If we look at the geographical location of Udayabhanu's house, there is a gated lane adjacent to the main road. Udayabhanu's house is the first one on the right side inside the lane. After this, further inside the lane are the houses of Udayabhanu's other brothers and relatives. This is the main route for coming and going. People had to pass by Udaybhanu's house. But in the last 4 months, no one smelled any foul odour from the house. Nor did anyone suspect there was a corpse. Employees come to use the washroom next door. They also did not suspect a corpse. Children come to the neighboring house for tuition. They never smelled any foul odour either, which would indicate that a corpse was decomposing in the house. Udaybhanu kept suppressing all the foul smell by applying perfume. Now read what the police say CO Cantt Navina Shukla says- A skeleton of a young woman has been found in a house that has been closed for many days. During interrogation, her father stated that his daughter died due to illness. In panic, he kept this truth hidden from everyone. The body has been sent for post-mortem. The entire matter is being investigated.

stories.title: Death toll rises to 13 in Vrindavan boat tragedy:BA student and youth bodies recovered, 4 pre-accident videos surface
stories.summary: In Vrindavan, Mathura, the death toll in the boat accident has risen to 13 devotees, while 22 people have been rescued and 3 others are still missing. On Sunday, the rescue operation entered its third day, with around 250 personnel from the Army, NDRF, and SDRF engaged in the search. The search area has now been expanded from 14 km to 20 km. Two more bodies recovered Earlier today, two more bodies were recovered. They were identified as Dinky from Dugri in Ludhiana, Punjab, and Rishabh Sharma from Jagraon. According to officials, the bodies had swollen and floated to the surface of the river. They were pulled out using ropes into a boat. The victims were later identified by their families. Dinky was a final-year BA student, while Rishabh had completed Class 12 and helped his father in work. Four videos recorded before the accident have also surfaced. In these, devotees are seen playing dholak and manjira, immersed in devotion, chanting “Radhe-Radhe” and singing bhajans such as “Nazar Sanwre Lag Na Jaye Kahin”. Earlier recovery and victim details On the second day of the search operation (Saturday), the body of Manik Tandon from Punjab was recovered near Devaraha Baba Ghat. He was engaged and was scheduled to be married in September. His father broke down after seeing his body. How the accident happened The boat carrying 38 devotees overturned on Friday around 3 pm near Kesi Ghat, about 2 km from Shri Banke Bihari Temple. Police have arrested boat operator Pappu Nishad and pontoon bridge contractor Narayan Sharma. Pappu had boarded passengers from Juggal Ghat. A survivor said the boat was about 50 feet from the bank in the Yamuna river when strong winds of around 40 kmph caused it to wobble. Despite warnings from passengers, the boatman did not stop. The boat narrowly escaped hitting the bridge twice, but collided on the third attempt and capsized. Massive search operation continues On Sunday, search operations continued with Army, NDRF, SDRF, and local teams working in coordination. The affected area has been divided into seven sectors, and the search radius has been increased to 20 km. Officials confirmed that 13 deaths have been reported so far, while 3 people remain missing. Bodies surfaced in the river due to swelling and were retrieved using ropes. Officials said the river current and depth (around 25 feet at the accident site) have made the rescue difficult. A large number of personnel and equipment have been deployed to locate the missing devotees. Background of victims and travel group Most devotees were part of a group from Ludhiana’s Jagraon area, who had travelled to Vrindavan on a four-day religious trip. The group had arrived on Friday after travelling in two buses. Authorities have also arrested the boat operator and pontoon contractor, while investigation continues into safety lapses, including overloading and lack of life jackets.
