stories.title: Preparations for UP BJP reshuffle intensify, Vinod Tawde reaches Lucknow:Meets Brajesh Pathak; plans to interact with Keshav Maurya in evening
stories.summary: Political activity in Uttar Pradesh has intensified over the formation of the BJP’s new organisational team. The party’s National General Secretary Vinod Tawde reached Lucknow on Sunday and began a series of one-on-one meetings with senior leaders at the party office. He has already met Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak. Tawde is likely to meet former state president Bhupendra Chaudhary in the afternoon and Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya later in the evening. He is also holding separate discussions with the party’s state general secretaries. He will remain in Lucknow on Monday as well. Sources say Tawde is gathering feedback from workers and MLAs on ground realities and will submit a report to the party high command. Based on this, the new UP BJP team and key political appointments are expected to be finalised. Earlier, BJP state president Pankaj Chaudhary had met Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath after returning from Delhi on Saturday. Brajesh Pathak said that organizational processes keep running in BJP; this is nothing new Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak, who reached the State BJP office, said that Organizational processes keep running continuously in the BJP. This is nothing new. We all work on the instructions of the leadership. He said- We are working to take PM Modi's welfare schemes for the poor to every person. Under CM Yogi's leadership, UP's law and order is being praised in every household. In 2027, we will form the government with a massive majority. 'Why is Akhilesh playing hide and seek on the women's reservation?' The Deputy CM also attacked Akhilesh Yadav. He said that he feels that just as property is transferred on the basis of a will, power is also transferred in the same way. But, this is not the case. Whoever the public blesses, runs the state. If you dare to speak on a woman's reservation, then speak openly. Why are you playing hide and seek? Brajesh Pathak said - Under CM Yogi's leadership, UP's law and order is being praised in every household. Preparation for organizational changes after 3 years According to party sources, after the appointment of BJP's National President Nitin Nabin, the party is now moving forward to prepare new leadership teams in the states as well. As part of this strategy, changes are being prepared in the UP BJP organization after about 3 years. Sources say that in the new team, some office bearers who have been holding positions for a long time may be removed, while several new faces are likely to get a place in the organization. Pankaj Chaudhary and Dharampal Singh have already held discussions with the party's national leaders in Delhi regarding the formation of the state organization. After consensus has been reached on several names, the focus is now on maintaining caste and regional balance in the organization. It is being reported that due to the greater influence of Purvanchal in the government and organization, Western UP, Awadh, Bundelkhand, and Kashi regions may now be given more representation in the organization. Decision may also be taken on appointments to commissions Meanwhile, the process of appointing chairpersons to various commissions, boards, and corporations, including the Minority Commission and Kinnar Development Board in the state, may begin from next week. Actually, last year, the matter of discontent regarding appointments to the Women's Commission had reached Delhi. Keeping this in view, the party leadership has sent Vinod Tawde as an observer this time, so that a final decision can be taken only after discussions with all parties. New members are elected every 3 years The current organizational team of UP BJP was formed by Bhupendra Chaudhary on March 25, 2023. At that time, he was the state president. The rule is that members should be elected every 3 years afresh. Therefore, state president Pankaj Chaudhary has to form his team anew.

stories.title: 'SP- Congress have no chance to form govt in UP':Deputy CM claims BJP is present and future; predicts wins in Bengal and Assam elections
stories.summary: UP's Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya has once again taken a swipe at the opposition. He says, ‘SP has no chance in UP, and Congress has no chance in the country till 2047’. He also launched a scathing attack on SP chief and former CM Akhilesh Yadav. He said that Akhilesh Yadav is restless due to separation from power. The people of UP are preparing for his farewell to Saifai. Deputy CM says, ‘BJP is the present, BJP is the future. The lotus is going to bloom for the third time in Assam and for the first time in Bengal. May 4, Didi is gone’. Deputy CM Keshav Prasad Maurya is in Agra on Sunday. He will participate in more than 6 programs. He first reached the program of the National Federation of Insurance Field Workers of India, organized at Hotel Mercure located on Fatehabad Road. Here, he told LIC development officers who came from across the country that those who are not yet under insurance coverage should benefit from insurance. Along with big policies, small policies should also be brought so that common people can also avail their benefits. Says, ‘Akhilesh Yadav is restless’ During the press conference after the program, he launched a scathing attack on SP President Akhilesh Yadav. On the question of continuously targeting the government, the Deputy CM said that Akhilesh Yadav is restless due to separation from power. The people of UP are preparing for his farewell to Saifai. Not in 2027, his turn is not coming till 2047. He is frustrated, that's why he makes baseless allegations against the government. He further added, ‘BJP is the present, BJP is the future. There is no possibility of SP coming to UP and Congress coming to the country till 2047’. Lotus blooming in Bengal The Deputy CM said that Lotus is going to bloom in Bengal. The promises that the BJP has made to the people of West Bengal will be fulfilled after the government is formed. May 4...Didi is gone. Meanwhile, Keshav Prasad Maurya said about the Assam elections - In Assam, Hemant Biswa Sarma is going to form the government for the third time. Deputy CM will participate in these programs . Will participate in the program of the teachers' organization UTA at Rajdevam Auditorium located on Fatehabad Road. . Inauguration of Samrat Ashok Plot organized at the ground located at Firozabad Mod in Fatehabad. Will also address the public meeting. . Will participate in the program organized on the birth anniversary of Maharaj Nishadraj at the ground located at Etmadduddaula. . Will visit the residence of Rajya Sabha member Naveen Jain located at Kamla Nagar.

stories.title: Cancer super specialty hospital to be built in Varanasi:Preparations have accelerated to set up 100-bed health centre in the city
stories.summary: Varanasi draws patients not only from nearby districts but also from other states, leading to long waiting times at major institutions like BHU. In a significant relief for cancer patients, preparations have accelerated to set up a 100-bed cancer care hospital in the city. The proposed facility will be equipped with state-of-the-art infrastructure. The Arajline development block has been identified for the project, and the search for suitable land is underway. The Kalyan Singh Cancer Institute in Lucknow has been designated as the nodal agency for its development. The move follows a recent decision by the Yogi government to establish modern cancer super-specialty hospitals in every division of the state. Chemotherapy and radiotherapy facilities will also be available Currently, a large number of cancer patients are coming to BHU and Pt. Madan Mohan Malaviya Cancer Institute, located in Sundarpur face long waiting times. The construction of the new hospital will provide significant relief to cancer patients. Here, along with consultation, all tests will also be conducted. Patients will not need to go elsewhere for chemotherapy and radiotherapy. After the hospital is built, a complete team of cancer specialists will also be appointed here. In conversation with Dainik Bhaskar, Additional Director (Health) of Varanasi Division, Dr. N.D. Sharma, said that the work of identifying the land has been almost completed. The construction of this hospital will provide considerable relief to cancer patients coming from several districts and neighboring states. More than 35 thousand patients annually The Cancer Institute, located in Varanasi, receives an average of more than 35 thousand new cancer patients every year. Patients from Varanasi district, along with Jaunpur, Mirzapur, Azamgarh, Ghazipur, Chandauli, as well as Bihar and Jharkhand, reach here. Almost the same number of patients come to the Oncology Department of BHU as well. In such a situation, there is a long waiting period for cancer patients here.

stories.title: Heat intensifies in Gorakhpur as day progresses:Dusty winds increase trouble, signs of heatwave in coming days
stories.summary: The effect of the heat started showing as soon as the strong sun came out on Sunday morning in Gorakhpur. Upon going outside, a burning sensation is felt on the face and in the eyes. Over the past few days, as the day progressed, the sun became more intense, and by afternoon, the condition became distressing. The dusty winds blowing along with the strong sun are becoming a major problem for people. Wind is blowing in the city at a speed of 35 to 40 kilometers per hour, due to which dust is flying everywhere. People walking on the road, especially two-wheeler riders, appeared more troubled. Complaints of difficulty in breathing and burning sensations in the eyes are also increasing due to dust. See 3 pictures... Today's temperature and weather conditions According to the Meteorological Department, today the maximum temperature is expected to be around 36 degrees Celsius and the minimum 22 degrees Celsius. The weather will remain dry and hot throughout the day. There is no possibility of rain in the coming days, so there is no hope of relief from the heat either. Light clouds may be visible here and there, but there will be no effect. The Meteorological Department has not issued any warning for now, but has mentioned that temperatures will rise rapidly in the coming days. It is estimated that the temperature may reach 40 to 42 degrees. Along with this, the possibility of hot winds has also been indicated. In such a situation, going out during the afternoon may become even more difficult. Air quality has also deteriorated Due to dusty winds, the Air Quality Index (AQI) has reached between 100 to 120, which is not considered good. Because of this, children, elderly people, and respiratory patients may face more problems. Issues like eye irritation, sore throat, and breathing difficulties are being reported. Weather will remain the same for the next 5 to 7 days There will not be much change in the weather for the next 5 to 7 days. The maximum temperature will remain between 36 to 39 degrees, and the minimum between 21 to 24 degrees. Strong sunshine and dusty winds will continue. The possibility of rain is very low. Temperature will cross 40 by the end of April As the month progresses, the heat will intensify further. After Wednesday, the temperature may cross 40 degrees, and conditions similar to heat waves may develop. In such circumstances, people are being advised to avoid sunlight during the day, cover their heads when going out, and drink plenty of water.

stories.title: Mirzapur advocate murder case accused shot in encounter:Shot in both legs; lawyer was murdered during morning walk
stories.summary: In Mirzapur, police arrested the ₹50,000-rewarded accused Rajendra Sonkar in an encounter on Saturday night for the murder of senior lawyer Rajiv Singh. Sonkar was shot in both legs during the exchange of fire and was later carried by police personnel to a vehicle before being admitted to the divisional hospital. SP Aparna Rajak Kaushik said the police team was checking vehicles at Baraudha intersection when the accused, arriving on a bike, tried to flee on spotting them. During the chase, he opened fire at the police, prompting retaliatory action in which he was injured. Earlier that morning, at around 7:15 am, 45-year-old lawyer Rajiv Singh was shot dead near his house while out for a morning walk. The accused fired at him from point-blank range, hitting him in the chest. He died on the spot. The attacker fled with an accomplice after the incident. The entire incident was captured on CCTV. Police had formed five teams and announced a ₹50,000 reward for Sonkar’s arrest. He was caught within 15 hours, while the search for his accomplice is still underway. See pictures of the encounter spot- Incident recorded on CCTV; attacker's bike didn't start for quite some time Lawyer's wife is village head, family lives in the city Originally a resident of Devri village in the Vindhyachal police station area, Rajeev Singh alias Rinku was living in Katra Kotwali. He had purchased land here in 2011 and built a house. He was living here because of his children's education. He used to commute to court from here. In the village, his wife, Pratibha Singh (40), is the Pradhan (village head). He himself had been Pradhan twice. Due to this, he had to frequently visit the village as well. He has 2 sons: Om (18) and Sarthak (12). Accused has also contested Pradhan elections The SP had informed that the main accused, Rajendra Sonkar, was a resident of the lawyer's village, Devri. He had contested the Pradhan elections. He had an ongoing electoral rivalry with Rajeev's wife, Pratibha Singh. Rajendra lives on rent in Katwaru's Pura, that is, near the lawyer's house. He already knew at what time Rajeev left home for his morning walk every day. He committed the crime after plotting the entire conspiracy. The investigation revealed that the accused had a case under the Arms Act registered against him in 2020. In that case, Rajiv Singh was representing Rajendra Sonkar. Family members stated that, being from the same village, Rajiv often helped Rajendra financially as well. The police informed that Rajendra Sonkar has been to jail three times before. He is also addicted to drugs. Accused considered Rajendra like a brother The deceased lawyer's father, Jata Shankar Singh, said that he considered Rajendra like a brother. He also used to plead his cases. Whenever there was any dispute, he would settle the matter through reconciliation. The reason for the murder is old enmity. He said that Rajiv Singh was the village head of Devri twice. When it became a women's seat, his wife, Pratibha Singh, is the village head. Gun was pointed at the lawyer 7 months ago, too Neighbors had informed that Rajendra Sonkar had attacked Rajiv Singh about 7 months ago by stopping him on the road. He had taken out a pistol from his bike's carrier, pointed it at Rajiv Singh, and assaulted him. Rajiv Singh had also filed a complaint in this matter at Katra Kotwali, but no action was taken by the police in time. Neighbour Manish Dubey had said that Rajendra Sonkar used to come home often. After a dispute for a few months, his visits stopped. After that, he was often seen loitering near the house in the morning. He has already been accused of murdering a lawyer earlier. He has murdered his grandmother and occupied the residence located in Danghar Mohalla of the city.

stories.title: Kidney transplants carried out in filmy style in Kanpur:Teams flew in, hospital staff sent on leave; inside the racket
stories.summary: Police have busted an illegal kidney transplant racket in Kanpur, exposing a disturbing network exploiting both the poor and the wealthy. The syndicate allegedly lured financially vulnerable people into selling their kidneys, convincing them that one can survive with a single organ. At the same time, deals worth crores were struck with affluent patients, who were provided illegal transplants. The transplant team reportedly flew in from Delhi, conducted surgeries under the cover of darkness, and left immediately after. Shockingly, the procedures were not carried out by qualified surgeons but by OT technicians. No eurologist has been identified in the case so far, even though such transplants are not possible without one, raising serious questions about how the operations were conducted. This entire case is like a movie. It has greed, fraud, and deception. What it doesn't have is a hero. Everyone is a villain. Today in Sunday Big Story, we learn about the complete Kanpur kidney case... Ahuja Hospital: The center point of the story About 2 years ago, Ahuja Hospital was started in the Kalyanpur area of Kanpur. Dr. Preeti Ahuja and Dr. Surjit Singh Ahuja started it. Both are husband and wife and are MBBS, MD. Earlier, they used to see patients in different hospitals in Kanpur, but then they set up their own hospital. They contacted big and renowned doctors of the city and convinced them to sit in their hospital. A total of 27 doctors used to sit in Ahuja Hospital. The hospital had arrangements for 35 beds. There were high-tech ICUs, NICUs, and operation theaters. Overall, a perfect hospital. Dr. Preeti is the Vice President of Kanpur in the Indian Medical Association (IMA). She is a Medical Officer at the State Bank of India. She is the Secretary of the Diabetes Association and a member of the Physician Forum of Specialist Doctors. Preeti holds positions in so many organisations that if any complaint reaches the higher authorities, they will think ten times before taking action. Preeti always maintained good relations with senior officers in the medical field. Broker Shivam built a network, lured everyone with the temptation of earning money Everything was going fine, but a few days later, Shivam Agarwal alias Shivam Kada entered the story. Shivam from Jalaun had run away to Kanpur at the age of 15. He didn't go to school after 8th grade. He did odd jobs in Kanpur, then became an ambulance driver. He built connections with hospitals and doctors. When he met Dr. Preeti, he became exclusively associated with Ahuja Hospital. Shivam Kada's connections kept growing not just in Kanpur, but in different parts of UP. He met Dr. Rohit from Noida. Rohit was an old player in the kidney transplant game. A deal was struck between the two. After this, Shivam got busy finding clients. For this, he made social media his medium. He created channels on Telegram. He became active on gaming apps. These were gaming apps where money was involved. Many people had already lost. During gameplay, through conversations, one could gauge how far the person on the other end would go for money. The work that Shivam was doing in Kanpur, the same work Dr. Afzal was doing in Meerut and Naveen Pandey was doing in Prayagraj-Noida. All of them would search for people who desperately needed money for kidneys and who would be ready to sell their kidneys. Deal made for ₹6 lakhs, sold for ₹90 lakh There are 2 victims in the kidney case. One is Ayush from Bihar, the second is Parul from Muzaffarnagar. Ayush needed money, and Parul needed a kidney. Between these two was an entire illegal system that would go to any extent for profiteering. Ayush and Shivam came in contact through Telegram. Both had discussions. When money was discussed, the deal was finalised at ₹6 lakh. Ayush was to receive ₹3 lakh before the operation and ₹3 lakh after the operation. On the other hand, Dr. Afzal from Meerut had prepared Parul from Muzaffarnagar for a kidney transplant. This deal was finalised for around ₹90 lakh. Ayush's conversation with Afzal started on Telegram. Afzal assured Ayush that the operation would be done before his MBA exam in May. In between, Ayush changed his mind, but Afzal and others convinced him again to sell his kidney. Preeti and Surjeet took charge of the management The date of March 29th was chosen for the kidney transplant. The location, as always, was Ahuja Hospital in Kanpur. It was also decided that after removing the kidney, Ayush would be admitted to Medi Life Hospital and Parul to Preeti Hospital. This had always been the practice. Dr. Narendra Singh alias Nandu, owner of Preeti Hospital, and Dr. Ram Prakash Kushwaha and Dr. Rajesh Kumar, owners of Medi Life, were already set up. They received more than ₹1-1 lakh each for admitting these patients. Ahuja Hospital kept ₹2 lakh 75 thousand for itself for one operation. The operations management was handled by Dr. Rohit from Noida. He is currently absconding. Dr. Rohit had formed an entire team. As soon as things were finalised, he would prepare the team. In his team, the kidney transplant work was done by Mudassar Ali from Dwarka, Delhi. Mudassar is not a urologist who specialises in this work. He is an OT technician. To assist Mudassar, two other OT technicians, Rajesh Kumar and Kuldeep Singh Raghav, also came from Ghaziabad. According to the plan, on March 28, Dr. Afzal reached Kanpur from Meerut with Parul. On the other side, Ayush was also admitted to the hospital. For March 29, Dr. Rohit booked flight tickets for Mudassar Ali, Rajesh, and Kuldeep. The entire team always left Delhi at night. The responsibility of picking up and dropping off at the airport was Saifi Parvez's. He used to stay with Afzal from Meerut. When the team arrived, he would receive everyone along with some other drivers. On the day of operation, the staff had a holiday The operation was scheduled for March 29 at Ahuja Hospital. Three days before that, the number of patients started decreasing. Dr. Preeti and Dr. Surjit would decide that on the day of the kidney transplant, no serious patient should remain in the hospital. More than half of the hospital staff would be given leave. The kidney transplant work would take place between 3 to 4 AM. At that time, only a few patients and their relatives in the hospital would be sleeping. There was no fear of investigation either. The operation took place on the night of March 29. The team that had come from Noida-Delhi returned by flight. Parul was shifted to Preeti Hospital on the morning of March 30, and Ayush was shifted to Medi Life Hospital. Their treatment began here. On this same day, the police received some information about the illegal kidney transplant case. It was also confirmed by intelligence inputs. After this, DCP West, Crime Branch, and SOG, all three together, raided Ahuja Hospital, Preeti Hospital, and Medi Life Hospital. The entire story unfolded from here. Kidney syndicate extends to South Africa Initially it seemed like just one case, but as the investigation progressed, a large syndicate came to light. Police arrested Dr. Preeti Ahuja, Dr. Surjit Ahuja, Preeti Hospital owner Narendra Singh, Medi Life Hospital's Ram Prakash Maurya and Rajesh Kumar, and ambulance driver Shivam Agarwal. After the arrest, during interrogation, many secrets were revealed. Several videos were found on Shivam Agarwal alias Shivam Kada's phone. In one video, Meerut's Dr. Afzal was lying with bundles of 500-rupee notes. This was ₹15 lakh. In another video, Shivam Agarwal, who has only studied up to 8th grade, is seen examining an African girl named Arabica. This shows that this syndicate has spread not just within the country, but to South Africa as well. It was found that approximately ₹2 crore were taken from Arabica in the name of a kidney transplant. No surgeon has been caught yet The biggest point in the entire case is that among the arrests made so far, there is no urologist, that is, kidney doctor. The police had recovered CCTV footage from Ahuja Hospital on the night of March 29-30. After the operation, 3 people were seen returning by car. One of these cars went towards Ghaziabad, which had Mudassar Ali, Kuldeep Raghav, and Rajesh Kumar. The second car went towards Meerut. It had Dr. Rohit, Afzal, Vaibhav, and Amit Sawar. The third car has become a puzzle in this case, as it went towards Lucknow. It is being reported that this car had one surgeon and two doctors from a private hospital. All three were also visible in the operating theatre's CCTV camera. But who they are, which hospital in Lucknow they were connected with, no information about this has reached the police so far. The police have also conducted raids at some places in Lucknow in search of them. More than 50 brokers and doctors involved in the racket A recording found on Shivam's phone revealed that he had facilitated 40 to 50 kidney transplants. In one video, standing outside Punjab's Maninder Ahuja Hospital, he was saying that these people took ₹43 lakh from me, but haven't done the kidney transplant yet. Now all of them have been caught. All our money has sunk. We have no option left except to commit suicide. In the initial 4 days, 9 accused were caught. After interrogation, many more names came to light. Kanpur Police has formed 10 teams to investigate the case. These teams are conducting raids in Lucknow, Noida, Delhi, Ghaziabad and Kanpur. Police have not been able to catch Dr. Rohit, Dr. Afzal, Dr. Mudassar Ali, Dr. Amit, Dr. Vaibhav, and Naveen Pandey yet. After they are caught, more layers of the case will come to light.

stories.title: Man loses 9 family members in Vrindavan accident:Boat overturned during kirtan, no life jackets provided, survivors blame crane work
stories.summary: "I watched my own family drowning and could do nothing. I lost 9 members of my family in the accident, including my son and wife. In just a few minutes, a journey filled with happiness turned into mourning. Our world was destroyed." Saying this, Vijay Kumar, who lost his loved ones in the boat accident in Vrindavan and was himself on that boat, breaks down crying. This accident occurred on April 10. 13 people died in it, and the search for 3 continues. Vijay described the scene of the last 7 minutes of the accident. Vijay said that many people had gathered on the boat because of the kirtan (devotional singing). Vijay said that when our boat reached near the newly constructed bridge, the crane pulled the iron dam installed there. Just then, a strong wind came, and the boat went towards the pillar. During this, the rope got entangled, and the boat capsized after hitting the pillar. Vijay said that as soon as all the people fell into the water, they started screaming. I, my son, and some other people who knew how to swim, kept struggling in the water. Son Madhur kept fighting to save his mother, but while trying to save her, he drowned. We brought him out, but could not save him. Read the full report The story of the last 7 minutes in Vijay's words Trip organizer Yashu said that they don't even provide life jackets there...

stories.title: Minister Khanna, BSP’s single seat in danger:SIR disrupts 114 seats; BJP-SP's calculations disrupted
stories.summary: 2.04 crore voters' names were cut from the final SIR list released on April 10 in UP. In the 2022 assembly elections, there were 114 seats where the victory-defeat margin was less than 10 thousand. After SIR, these seats have seen a reduction of 16 thousand to 1.18 lakh voters. In such a situation, these seats have come into the danger zone. The reason is that if the reduced voters were core voters of the party that won by a narrow margin last time, then the result there in 2027 could completely reverse. Out of these 114 seats, the BJP had won 63, SP 41, and other parties had won 10 seats. How much will the electoral game of 2027 change after SIR? Will the equations change on seats with low margins? Which party will suffer more loss? Read the special report In 2022, 15 seats had a margin of less than a thousand Looking at the 2022 assembly elections, there were 15 seats where the winning margin was less than a thousand. Of these, 10 seats had a margin of less than 500 votes. Out of these 15 seats, the BJP and its allied parties won 9. Meanwhile, 6 seats went to the SP alliance. Now, on these seats, votes have decreased by 21 to 72 thousand. Senior journalist Hemant Tiwari says, ‘Looking at the current situation, these seats have come into the danger zone for the BJP. Comparing the results of the last two elections shows that the win-loss margin in 2022 was much less compared to 2017’. This is why the BJP's winning margin on more than 60 seats was less than 10 thousand. BJP's held seats saw the biggest vote decline In 2022, there were 99 seats where the margin of victory was less than 10 thousand. Of these, the BJP got 55, SP got 35, RLD got 3, Nishad and Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party got 2-2 each, and the BSP and Congress got 1-1 seat each. Political observers believe that these seats have also come into the danger zone. During the SIR itself, CM Yogi had warned about these seats in coordination meetings with the party, government and Sangh. In western UP and Bundelkhand, 22 seats had witnessed victory-defeat margins of less than 10 thousand votes. Out of these, BJP had won 13 seats. Meanwhile, SP, along with RLD, had registered victory on 9 seats. The West has a larger Muslim and Jat population, but the equations are not the same as in 2022. RLD has broken its alliance with SP and joined the BJP. In such a situation, SP may suffer losses on seats with narrow margins. Votes decreased by 10 times more than the winning margin in Minister Suresh Khanna's seat In the 2022 Assembly elections in Central UP, there were 50 seats with a margin of less than 10 thousand. There was a direct contest between SP and BJP here. Out of these, BJP captured 30 seats while the SP won 20. OBC voters like Lodhi, Maurya, and Kurmi-Yadav dominate this belt. After SIR, the equations of both parties have been disrupted here. Votes have decreased by up to 10 times compared to the winning-losing margin here. This includes Finance Minister Suresh Khanna's Shahjahanpur seat as well. In 2022, he won by 9313 votes, while more than 1 lakh votes were reduced in the seat. The special thing is that this seat has more than 30% Muslim voters. In such a situation, BJP's equation in the seat appears to be deteriorating. Challenge for Congress and BSP in Purvanchal In Purvanchal, the victory-defeat margin was less than 10 thousand on 27 seats. In 2022, SP had contested elections in alliance with Suheldev Bharatiya Samaj Party (SBSP). This alliance proved stronger than the BJP in this region. BJP won 12 seats, while SP won 9. SBSP and Nishad Party won 2-2 seats each, while BSP and Congress won 1-1 seat each. Now Subaspa is with the BJP. This belt has a larger population of the backward classes. BJP has an alliance with SBSP and Nishad Party, which represent these backward classes. After SIR, the seats of Congress MLA Virendra Chaudhary from Farenda and BSP's sole MLA Umashankar Singh from Rasra appear to be in jeopardy. The reason is that Congress's Virendra won by 1246 votes while BSP's Umashankar Singh won by 6583 votes. Whereas in SIR, Farenda saw a decrease of about 29 thousand votes, and the Rasra seat saw a decrease of 37 thousand votes. Meanwhile, BJP had won the Duddhi seat, but MLA Ram Dular Gond was convicted in a rape case. In the by-election, this seat was won by SP's Vijay Singh Gond, but he too has passed away due to illness. Currently, this seat is vacant. Senior journalist Anand Rai says, ‘Duplicates, transfers and names of deceased have been removed from the final list issued after SIR. It could not be ascertained which caste group has migrated the most’. There is a common perception that Yadavs and Muslims are SP voters. Similarly, Dalits are considered BSP voters while upper castes and extremely backward castes are considered BJP voters.

stories.title: Thief's neck stuck between shutter and wall:Hung for 6 hours, rescued by cutting shutter in Ghaziabad
stories.summary: A thief got stuck between the wall and shutter of a clinic in Ghaziabad. The thief was entering through the roof to steal from the clinic. While climbing down, he got trapped between the shutter and concrete wall. His neck got stuck between the shutter and wall. He remained stuck in that condition for about 6 hours. When the doctor arrived at the clinic on Saturday afternoon, he came to know about the situation. He immediately informed the police. The police who reached the spot informed the fire brigade. The fire brigade team arrived and conducted the rescue. The thief was safely brought out by cutting the shutter. The case is from Indirapuram police station area. First see 2 pictures.... Now know the complete matter Body came out, neck got stuck The name of the caught thief is Abhishek. He is originally a resident of Bihar. According to police, on Saturday morning around 7 o'clock he was entering a clinic located in Abhay Khand to commit theft. There was a little space at the upper part of the shutter. Abhishek climbed onto the roof. He started entering through this space. His torso somehow got inside the clinic, but his neck got stuck between the shutter and the wall. He tried hard to get out. He kept struggling, but couldn't get free. He remained trapped in that condition. Around 12 noon, the doctor reached the clinic. He saw that a thief was stuck near the shutter. He immediately informed the police. Police reached the spot. A fire brigade team was also called along. Thief was rescued by cutting the shutter Seeing the seriousness of the incident, the fire service team immediately started the rescue operation. The team carefully cut the shutter with the help of special equipment. After this, the youth's neck was safely extracted. During the entire rescue, the team exercised complete caution so that he would not suffer any additional injury. After the rescue, the thief was safely brought out. CFO Rahul Pal said On Saturday around 1 pm, Vaishali Fire Station received information that a youth was trapped between the shutter and wall of a clinic. On receiving the information, the fire brigade team reached the spot. Half of the youth's body was stuck inside and half outside. The team broke the shutter and safely brought the youth out and handed him over to the police.

stories.title: 11 dead in Vrindavan boat mishap:Who are the 4 people responsible? No lifejackets, allegations of overcrowding boat
stories.summary: A boat carrying devotees capsized in Vrindavan after colliding with a pontoon bridge on the Yamuna river. So far, 11 people have died, while five are still missing. Just 15 minutes before the accident, passengers were seen laughing and enjoying the ride. Within minutes, the situation turned tragic. No life jackets, overcrowding alleged The boat was carrying 37 passengers in water nearly 25–30 feet deep. None of them were given life jackets. Strong winds of around 30–40 kmph were blowing, but the operator did not slow down or stop despite repeated warnings from passengers. Experts say many lives could have been saved if life jackets were provided. How the accident unfolded The boat was around 50 feet from the shore when it started shaking due to strong winds. Passengers warned the boatman as the pontoon bridge approached, but he did not stop. After avoiding collision twice, the boat hit the bridge on the third attempt. The impact caused passengers to fall to one side, and the boat capsized. Boat operator’s role under question The boat operator, Pappu Nishad, allegedly ignored basic safety rules: After the accident, he fled the spot. Contractor’s lapse flagged The pontoon bridge was being dismantled under a riverfront project. Contractor Narayan Sharma allegedly: This allowed boats to enter a risky area. Civic body under scrutiny The Municipal Corporation is responsible for issuing licences and ensuring safety. However: The boat involved in the accident was also unlicensed. Administration’s failure The local administration is responsible for safety at ghats and monitoring boating. But: Officials are now facing serious questions. Legal action and investigation Police have registered a case of culpable homicide not amounting to murder against the boat owner and contractor. However, there is debate over whether stricter charges should be applied due to serious negligence. Safety rules in place Guidelines in Uttar Pradesh require: Family tragedy: 7 relatives among dead Seven members of one family died in the accident. The victims include Madhur Bahal, his mother Kavita Bahal, Charanjit, Pinky Bahal, Asha Rani, Anju Gulati and Rakesh Gulati.

JD Vance meets Pak PM ahead of US-Iran ceasefire talks US Vice President J D Vance is holding talks with Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif ahead of the ceasefire talks between Iran and the United States. 2. Vrindavan boat tragedy: toll rises to 11, massive Yamuna search underway Death toll in the Vrindavan boat tragedy has risen to 11, with 4 still missing. stories.title: Chaos erupts during Akshay Kumar's film promotion:Fans climb escalators in the mall, put lives at risk, security lapses exposed
stories.summary: A dangerous fan frenzy erupted during Akshay Kumar’s event at Gaur City Mall on Friday, raising serious concerns about crowd management and fan safety. The actor was at the venue to promote his film Bhoot Bangla, accompanied by co-stars Rajpal Yadav and Wamiqa Gabbi. Within minutes of their arrival, the crowd swelled beyond control, creating a chaotic, stampede-like situation. Fans were seen climbing escalators and pushing through packed areas, putting their lives at risk and exposing serious lapses in security arrangements. The situation worsened, leading to a stampede-like situation. People were seen putting their lives at risk. The viral video showed some fans climbing onto the escalator railings for a better view. Barricades on the ground floor broke, and people pushed each other forward. This situation could have turned into a major accident. The biggest question is whether there were proper security arrangements for such public events? Thousands of people gathering in a closed space and the loss of control raises questions about the preparations of the mall management and event organisers. After the video went viral on social media, users appeared angry. Many called it irresponsible and said that stars and their teams should prioritise the safety of fans at such events. However, during this time, Akshay Kumar appeared calm on stage and continued to interact with fans. But the crowd getting out of control is a big warning. The film 'Bhoot Bangla' is scheduled to release on April 17. But the pictures that emerged during the promotion raise questions: Is it right to put people's lives at risk in the name of stardom?

stories.title: Gorakhpur to turn waste into fuel:New plan targets pollution, cleaner city
stories.summary: Gorakhpur Municipal Corporation has launched a new ‘RDF Roadmap’ to strengthen scientific waste disposal and curb pollution in the city. The plan focuses on converting waste into fuel, helping make Gorakhpur cleaner and more environment-friendly. The roadmap was unveiled at a round-table conference organised by the Municipal Corporation along with Environmental Management Center Private Limited at a hotel in the Gorakhnath area. The initiative aims to improve solid waste management while reducing pollution levels. Waste to be used as alternative fuel Mayor Dr Shrivastava said waste should no longer be seen as something to discard, but as a resource. Under the plan, Refuse-Derived Fuel (RDF) and torrefied charcoal made from waste will be used as an alternative to coal in cement industries. This is expected to reduce pollution and ease the burden on landfill sites. The scheme is linked to the National Clean Air Programme and the Swachh Bharat Mission. The civic body is working to develop Gorakhpur into a ‘zero waste’ and sustainable city, setting an example for others. Focus on waste segregation at source The Municipal Corporation is putting strong emphasis on segregating waste at the household level. Door-to-door collection of separated waste is being promoted, along with plans to expand the capacity of waste processing plants to convert more waste into fuel. Additional Municipal Commissioner Pramod Kumar said the roadmap will also strengthen transportation, quality testing, and supply systems. This will ensure industries receive a steady supply of high-quality RDF and make the process more organised. Steps to curb open waste burning Officials said the initiative will help reduce open burning and dumping of waste, which are major contributors to air pollution. By promoting scientific waste management and reuse, the plan also supports a circular economy. Experts at the conference shared suggestions to improve waste management and stressed the need for effective implementation of the new system.

stories.title: Badaun Health officer’s wife dies in car fire:Woman screamed amid the flames; husband severely injured
stories.summary: A 25-year-old woman died after a moving car caught fire in Uttar Pradesh’s Badaun district in the early hours of Friday. Her husband, a Community Health Officer, managed to escape but sustained serious burn injuries. The incident took place around 1 am near Rauta village in the Usait police station area. The car was being driven by Arpit Bhardwaj (28), while his wife Priya was lying on the back seat. First see 3 pictures... Wife unable to exit car According to police, Priya had undergone a kidney stone operation three days ago at a private hospital in Palia in Lakhimpur Kheri. The couple was returning home after her discharge when the car caught fire. Arpit managed to get out of the vehicle after it caught fire. Priya, who was on the back seat, could not exit the car. Police said the rear doors appeared to be locked, and she was unable to open them despite repeated attempts. Locals alerted, rescue unsuccessful Locals reached the spot after noticing the flames but could not rescue her. Police and fire brigade teams were informed and reached the site. By the time the fire was brought under control, Priya had died. Arpit, who suffered burn injuries, has been admitted to a hospital. Family travelled in separate vehicles Family members said Priya’s condition after surgery had led them to travel in separate vehicles. Arpit’s parents and their one-and-a-half-year-old daughter had reached home earlier in another car. Cause of fire under investigation Station House Officer Devendra Singh said the exact cause of the fire is yet to be determined. “Prima facie, a short circuit or technical fault is suspected. A detailed technical examination of the vehicle will be conducted,” he said.

stories.title: ‘Not a single Miyan, but named Miyanpur’:CM Yogi renames village in Lakhimpur as 'Rabindranagar'; Bangladeshi Hindus receive land rights
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Saturday announced that Miyanpur village in the Mohammadi assembly constituency will be renamed Rabindranagar. Addressing a gathering, Adityanath criticised the Congress, alleging that the village was named Miyanpur to “hide identity”. “There is not a single ‘Miyan’ here, yet it was named Miyanpur. This will now change,” he said. He added that the village would be renamed after Rabindranath Tagore, “who gave India its national anthem”, to reflect a new identity. The Chief Minister was in Lakhimpur to attend two programmes. In Miyanpur, he distributed land ownership certificates to 331 Bangladeshi Hindu families, granting them legal rights over their land. Earlier, in Palia, he handed over land ownership certificates to 4,356 families from the Tharu tribe and 2,350 families of freedom fighters’ dependents. During the visit, Adityanath also inaugurated and laid the foundation stones for 538 development projects worth Rs 1,311 crore. This included the inauguration of 345 projects valued at Rs 356 crore and the foundation laying for 193 projects worth Rs 955 crore. Read the key points of CM Yogi's speech: CM Yogi distributed ownership certificates to Tharu people for their land rights. Tharu women also gifted handmade items. 1- Hindus and Sikhs suffered due to the deeds of Pakistan CM Yogi said, “Pakistan, through its actions, caused the partition of India. That same Pakistan has itself been divided, and more divisions may follow. But who suffered the consequences? Hindus, Sikhs, Jains, Parsis and Christians living there suffered, because no other community has a presence there.” 2- Miyanpur will now be Rabindranagar Yogi said, “Look at how wrongdoing speaks for itself. These people were rejected by Bangladesh and persecuted due to Pakistan’s actions. They came as displaced persons, and their ancestral properties were seized. Congress committed injustice — they took your votes but never gave you ownership rights. To hide your identity, the village was named Miyanpur. Think about it — not a single ‘Miyan’, yet the name was Miyanpur. Now it will be renamed Rabindranagar. You will be identified with Gurudev Rabindranath Tagore, who gave India its national anthem. Bengal is the land of India’s spiritual and cultural heritage. The national anthem was written by Rabindranath Tagore, and the national song by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay.” 3- MLAs will start drooling Addressing the Tharu community in Palia, CM Yogi spoke about connecting them with industries and businesses. Praising local MLA Romi Sahni, he also made a light remark: “You will see, as soon as Romi ji’s bakery opens, public representatives sitting on stage will start drooling. He makes excellent sweets. When the issue of giving you land titles was being discussed, he even came to me with a box of sweets. Now those same sweets will be made here.” The CM added that the day is special as it precedes Maharana Sanga’s birth anniversary, making the distribution of land rights even more significant. 4- No one will be able to grab your land now The Chief Minister said that neither the Forest Department, Police, nor Revenue officials will interfere in people’s rights anymore. Illegal land grabbing and manipulation will be stopped. He added, “According to scriptures, the best governance is where people are happy. The success of governance lies in public welfare.” 5- Generations struggled for this land The CM said that several generations have struggled for land rights. Families of freedom fighters and the Tharu community were deprived for decades, but now this long struggle is being fulfilled. 6- Identity of Chandan Chowki, tribute to Maharana Sanga The CM said Chandan Chowki represents Palia’s identity, where tribal culture, self-respect and the fertility of the Terai region come together. Earlier, the Tharu community faced harassment from officials and struggled for identity. He again noted that receiving land rights on the eve of Maharana Sanga’s birth anniversary is a matter of pride. 7- Settled earlier, but rights were denied Yogi said that people who sacrificed everything during the freedom struggle were later denied their rights. During British rule, their lands were seized, they were tortured, sent to Cellular Jail (Kala Pani), executed, or exiled without trial. After Independence, they were resettled but not given ownership rights. The Tharu community was promised land in 1976 but did not receive ownership. Similarly, freedom fighters settled in eastern Uttar Pradesh in 1955 were also denied rights. “Those who sacrificed for the nation were deprived even in independent India,” he said. 8- Previous governments focused only on family interests Yogi said previous governments lacked sensitivity and prioritised family interests over public welfare. “They divided society, took away your rights and resources, and created an identity crisis. But today, the double-engine government is giving shape to your dreams by granting land rights.” He added that: 9- Development was earlier limited to one village CM Yogi said earlier development was concentrated in one place. “Today, 25 crore people are our family. Earlier, development and planning were centred only in Saifai, where one family benefited at the cost of the poor.” 10- Tharu community to be linked with bakery industry The CM said this initiative is not just about rights but also about development. He praised Romi Sahni for setting an example and said, “I want you to establish a model around Chandan Chowki that brings self-reliance to the Tharu community. By connecting with your bakery, we can expand business across the Terai region and Uttarakhand.” 11- Announcement to withdraw cases CM Yogi said that cases filed against members of the Tharu community during the Samajwadi Party government will be withdrawn. He alleged that the previous government protected criminals and filed false cases against innocent people. “I assure you, no one will be able to oppress you now,” he said.

stories.title: 'I received threats for raising cow protection issue':Shankaracharya says governments now want to act as religious leaders
stories.summary: In Rajasthan, Shankaracharya Swami Avimukteshwaranand Saraswati has said that he is receiving death threats if he visits Uttar Pradesh (UP). He said that he is being warned that he would be killed for speaking in favour of cow protection. He also commented on Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, saying that he is becoming a “meat seller wearing saffron clothes”. ‘Hinduism is being followed according to govt circulars’ He further said that today Hinduism is being followed according to government circulars instead of scriptures. He added that governments now want to act as religious authorities themselves. According to him, in Hindu tradition, the king and the religious teacher were always separate, and this system is now being changed, which he said cannot be accepted. The Shankaracharya is currently in Kota, where he spoke openly about Sanatan Dharma, Hinduism, the role of government, conflicts with saints, and the threats he claims to be receiving. Read- Conversation with Shankaracharya Q: What is the current situation of Sanatan Dharma? Is religion getting stronger in the country or facing challenges? A: The teachings of Sanatan Dharma come from the Vedas, and from Veda-based Puranas, Smritis and other literature. Today’s so-called Hindutva is not following scriptures properly. Instead, it is being followed according to government circulars. If Hindus follow circulars, they will have no protection. Only those who follow scriptures are true Hindus. Q: You have mentioned a “Dharma Yudh Board”. Is this becoming a major movement? A: It has already started. Now it depends on how deeply the people involved work for it. Results will follow accordingly. Q: Are attempts being made to suppress your voice? Have you also received threats recently? A: Attacks are being made one after another. Sometimes cases are filed, sometimes allegations are made, and sometimes death threats are given. We cannot remain silent out of fear. We are only saying what is written in the scriptures. If scriptures call the cow a mother, why is it being treated as an animal? How is cow slaughter and trade being justified in the name of tradition? Q: Are religious places being run by governments? A: Yes, governments are trying to control religious institutions. They want to become religious authorities themselves. In Hindu tradition, the king and the religious teacher were separate, but now this is being changed. Religious authority should remain with saints, while governance should remain with leaders. Q: How do you see the Prayagraj bathing incident? Was it an administrative failure or political pressure? A: If it was only an administrative mistake, the administration would have justified and investigated it, but that did not happen. No inquiry or action was taken. The Chief Minister publicly stated in the Assembly that everything happened according to his direction. Q: Even after this controversy, there have been multiple cases and disputes? A: Multiple cases have been filed, allegations have been made, and now there are death threats saying I will be killed if I visit Uttar Pradesh. All this is happening for speaking about Sanatan Dharma. Q: Yogi Adityanath is also a saint, isn’t he? A: A true saint cannot support animal slaughter or meat trade. Even a temple priest does not do such work. A true Hindu hesitates even before killing a mosquito. If someone is involved in large-scale animal slaughter and trade, calling them a saint is not appropriate. The definition of Hinduism is being changed, and this cannot be accepted.

stories.title: Man lives with daughter’s corpse for 4 months in Meerut:Uses perfume to hide stench; body turns to skeleton
stories.summary: In Meerut, a father lived in the house with his daughter's corpse for 4 months. The corpse was badly decomposed. The daughter was a teacher. In his stubbornness to stay with her, father did not want to be separated from her and therefore he did not disclosed the news of daughter's demise. He kept spraying perfume on the corpse to hide the smell. The girl's entire body had turned into a skeleton, only her feet remained. The incident came to light when relatives arrived at the house. Upon smelling the odor, they called and informed the police. Police, who arrived at the scene, recovered the corpse from a room in the house. The condition of the body was so bad that relatives, police officers, and neighbors could not bear to look at it. The case is from Teli Mohalla of Sadar Bazaar. See 3 pictures Complete case in detail Priyanka had died 5 months ago Relatives told the police that Priyanka's father, Uday Bhanu, did not let anyone know about her death. He kept his daughter's body inside the house. When relatives entered, they saw that the girl's body had turned into a skeleton. Only her legs were visible. Wife committed suicide in 2013 During interrogation, the death of Uday Bhanu's wife, Sharmishtha, also came to light. Uday Bhanu often stayed out for work and couldn't come home, which made his wife, Sharmishtha, upset. During that time, Sharmishtha hanged herself in their Meerut home. After this, Priyanka went into shock. She became completely silent. Last seen on December 5 Sunilmal Biswas, cousin of Priyanka Biswas, said he last saw his uncle Uday Bhanu Biswas on December 5. After that, neither Priyanka nor Uday Bhanu was seen. When Sunil tried calling, he couldn’t connect. Later, Uday Bhanu called from a new number, saying he was in Dehradun and that Priyanka was ill and admitted to a hospital there for treatment. Sunil said he had been searching for them for a long time. On Friday evening, someone informed him that Uday Bhanu was seen at a tea shop in Begumbagh. Sunil then reached the spot with relatives and caught his uncle there. Pile of garbage inside the house Sunil said that he called some of his relatives there. After this, everyone caught Uday Bhanu and brought him to his house. After being strict, he confessed the truth. As soon as he revealed that his daughter's body was inside the house, everyone was shocked. Upon receiving information from relatives, the police arrived and entered the house with Uday Bhanu, and were astonished. Inside the house, there was a pile of garbage. Priyanka's body was lying on the bed, but it had turned into a skeleton. As soon as this news was received, the entire neighborhood gathered. The police completed the inquest (panchnama) of the body and sent it to the mortuary for post-mortem. Priyanka's death due to jaundice In the initial police investigation, it was revealed that Bhanu Biswas was living inside the house. He used perfume to hide the foul smell. Many perfume bottles were also found from his house. After questioning Uday Bhanu, the police took him into custody and sent him to Sadar Bazar police station. Uday Bhanu told the police that Priyanka had black jaundice. He used to perform exorcisms on her, but her health did not improve and she died. He stayed with her for 2 months. After that, he went to Dehradun. He had returned from Dehradun a short while ago. Even then, Priyanka's body was more than half decomposed. Police said the death occurred 4 months ago CO Cantt Navina Shukla said- The body of a 35-year-old woman has been found inside a house in Teli Mohalla. The body is largely decomposed. The matter is being investigated.

stories.title: 5 men harass woman, thrash in Gorakhpur:Shocking video emerges, no help from crowd, accused flee from spot after threats
stories.summary: In Gorakhpur, five youths molested and assaulted a young woman. A video of about one and a half minutes of this incident has surfaced, in which 5 youths are seen beating up a young man. Meanwhile, the young woman is trying to rescue him. According to information, on Friday the young woman had come to GDA Tower with an acquaintance to have coffee. During this time, five youths standing there passed indecent comments on the young woman. When the young woman protested, the accused started abusing her. After this, the accused beat up the young man who had come with the young woman. Then they left him in a bloodied condition and all fled from the spot. This incident is from Cantt police station area. The video has surfaced today. Now read the complete matter in detail Made obscene comments on the young woman There are several shops including a cafe in GDA Tower located at Golghar. Crowds gather here every evening. On Friday afternoon around 3 pm, a young woman had come to have coffee with an acquaintance. During this time, five young men standing there made indecent comments on the young woman. When the young woman protested, they started abusing her. At this, the young man who came with her tried to explain to them, but the accused started misbehaving and an argument ensued. Girl kept screaming for help After this, the accused started beating the young man and woman. The men chased and beat the young man, causing him to fall to the ground covered in blood. During this time, the young woman kept screamin for help, but no one in the GDA Tower came to her assistance. People kept making videos on their mobiles. Even the guard deployed there for security silently watched the incident. The accused threatened the young woman that if she complained anywhere, they would kill her next time. After this, all the accused fled from the spot. Drunkards gather at the tower Shopkeepers at GDA Tower said - Every day, unruly youths gather here. Because of them, even families are afraid to come. As soon as evening falls, GDA Tower turns into a bar. On every floor of the tower, youths can be seen sitting comfortably and drinking alcohol. After drinking, there is chaos here every other day. Due to this reason, many shopkeepers have vacated their shops and left from here. Beer and liquor bottles can be seen thrown everywhere. Because of this too, people hesitate to come here. Regarding this, Cant CEO IPS Arun Kumar S said - No such complaint has been received yet. The incident is being investigated. Whoever is guilty will be acted upon.

stories.title: Short circuit triggers fire at BHU IMS campus:Students rush out as flames spread, fire brigade controls blaze before any casualties
stories.summary: Panic broke out on Saturday when a fire erupted in a warehouse at the IMS campus of Banaras Hindu University. It is being reported that the fire, caused by a short circuit in the wiring, quickly escalated. Students' classes were being conducted near the location where the fire started. Seeing the situation, all students were immediately evacuated. According to people present at the scene, the warehouse where the fire broke out had paint and related materials stored in it. Additionally, two to three cylinders were also kept there, which increased the danger. Upon receiving information, fire brigade vehicles reached the spot within approximately 10 minutes. See 3 pictures.... Rescue operation started after cutting off electricity The university administration immediately cut off electricity to the entire area and began firefighting operations. The Director of IMS also reached the spot and helped evacuate materials along with the staff. The Director informed that the fire had broken out in the warehouse behind the Department of Siddhanta Darshan. He said that only materials were damaged in the incident, and no person was injured. Fire brigade and BHU security personnel remained present at the spot to extinguish the fire. The fire was brought under control in time, which averted a major disaster.

stories.summary: An emergency landing was carried out on Saturday morning at Chaudhary Charan Singh International Airport in Lucknow for a Flydubai flight travelling from Dubai to Kathmandu after it could not get landing permission there due to bad weather. The pilot contacted Lucknow Air Traffic Control (ATC) and sought permission to land. After clearance, the aircraft safely landed at 8:22 am with 154 passengers onboard. A technical team inspected the plane and refuelled it, after which the flight departed for Kathmandu again around 10 am, nearly 90 minutes later. Fly Dubai's airline services also in the Middle East, Europe Fly Dubai tickets are considered more affordable than other companies. This company was started in 2008 with the support of the Dubai government. Its headquarters are at Dubai International Airport. Fly Dubai operates flights to several cities in the Middle East, Asia, Europe, and Africa. Direct flights are also available from many cities in India. Emergency landing also made on March 31

stories.title: Mirzapur lawyer shot dead during morning walk:2 attackers open fire on chest; threaten locals with gun when chased
stories.summary: A senior lawyer was shot dead during a morning walk in Mirzapur around 7:15 am on Saturday. Two bike-borne assailants intercepted him on the road and shot him in the chest at close range with a country-made pistol before fleeing. The entire incident was captured on CCTV. According to police, Rajiv Singh (45) had stepped out for his routine walk when the attackers stopped him midway and opened fire. While escaping, their bike briefly stalled. Locals ran to catch them, but the attackers threatened them at gunpoint, forcing them to step back. The incident occurred in Katwaru Ka Pura locality under Katra Kotwali area, about 2 km from the district headquarters. Motive linked to election rivalry Superintendent of Police Aparna Rajat Kaushik said, Election rivalry appears to be the motive. The victim’s wife, Pratibha Singh (40), is the village pradhan, and the main accused, Rajendra Sonkar, had earlier contested the same election against her. He had also assaulted Rajiv Singh about seven months ago. Police teams have been formed to arrest the accused. Pictures related to the incident What CCTV footage shows Victim’s background Police said Rajiv left home around 6 am for his walk and was attacked shortly after. Locals rushed him to the hospital, where doctors declared him dead. The body has been sent for post-mortem, and an investigation is underway. Accused identified through CCTV Police confirmed that the main accused, Rajendra Sonkar, also a resident of Deori village, has been identified through CCTV footage. He had earlier contested the pradhan election against Pratibha Singh. The second accused is yet to be identified. Months-long surveillance before attack Police said Rajendra Sonkar had been living in a rented house in Katwaru Ka Pura and had been conducting surveillance on Rajiv Singh’s routine for several months, knowing the exact time he left for his morning walk. Previous threat reported earlier Neighbours said Sonkar had earlier stopped Rajiv Singh on the road about seven months ago, threatened him with a pistol, and assaulted him. A complaint was filed at Katra Kotwali police station, but no timely action was taken, they alleged.

stories.title: Eyewitness account of Vrindavan boat mishap:Says, 'Warned boatman to slow down, he didn’t listen'
stories.summary: The scene was horrific. Everyone standing on the banks of Yamuna ran to save them. My colleague and I threw ropes and pulled people out of the river. We pulled them onto the boat. This way, 7-8 lives were saved. This is according to Mohar Singh, an eyewitness to the Vrindavan boat accident in Mathura. 10 devotees died in this accident. Among those who lost their lives, 7 people were relatives. All of them were residents of Punjab. Bhaskar spoke to those who survived the accident and those who saved the lives of the devotees. Tanish, who was on the boat, said - I told the boatman to drive the boat slowly, but he didn't listen. Meanwhile, the boat swayed 3 times and capsized. Read the report Know how the accident happened The boat was in the middle of the Yamuna river, about 50 feet from the bank at KC Ghat. At that time, the wind was blowing at a speed of about 40kmph. Due to the strong wind, the boat suddenly started to sway. The boatman lost control. The tourists told the boatman, ‘The bridge is near, stop it.’ But he did not stop. The boat narrowly avoided a collision twice. On the third attempt, it collided, and the boat sank. Photos related to the accident Eyewitness accounts and conversations with people Mohar Singh is a boatman. When the boat capsized in Yamuna, he was at some distance. Mohar Singh said, On the other side, where the boat (steamer) was going, there was sand. The water was also low. Suddenly the steamer turned back. It slightly hit the pillar of the pontoon bridge, and the public sitting in it got scared. Due to fear, they moved to one side.' Mohar Singh further said, We were on the other side on our steamer. There were two of us, Bhop Singh and I. When we heard the noise, we left our steamer. I know how to swim a little, but Bhop Singh knows how to swim better. We helped people by throwing ropes. We pulled the devotees onto the steamer. There was an elderly woman, we slowly pulled her too. We saved about 7-8 lives this way. The scene was bad, but everyone standing on the shore ran to help save people. The diver said - the water was 25 feet deep Diver Radhe said, Devotees were in two boats. One of the boats had completely capsized. The water is about 25 feet deep at the accident site. The water current there is very strong. Youth on the boat told how the accident happened Tanish, who was on the boat, said, We, about 25-27 people, were cruising on the Yamuna river in a boat. Everyone was doing kirtan (devotional singing). We asked the boatman 2-3 times to drive the boat slowly, but he didn't listen. Suddenly, strong winds started blowing, and after swaying 2-3 times, the boat collided with the temporary iron pontoon bridge built in the middle of the river. 7 relatives died in the accident 7 members of the same family have died in the accident. Among the deceased are Madhur Behl, his mother Kavita Behl, uncle Charanjit, Charanjit's wife Pinky Behl, Madhur's aunt Asha Rani, another aunt Anju Gulati, and uncle Rakesh Gulati. Helpline number issued The district administration has issued a helpline number 0565-2403200. The DM said, For any problem or information, you can contact me on my mobile number 9454417512, Additional District Magistrate Finance and Revenue Dr. Pankaj Kumar Verma on his mobile number 9012881919/ 9454417583, and SP Rural Suresh Chandra Rawat on his mobile number 9454401103.

stories.title: Final voter list rings alarm for 40 ministers:Up to 10 times more votes cut than their victory margins in UP
stories.summary: The final list of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) released by the Election Commission of India in Uttar Pradesh on Friday has raised concerns for the state government and the Bharatiya Janata Party. Data shows that on the seats of 40 ministers, the number of deleted voters is 2 to 10 times higher than their 2022 Assembly victory margins, across both urban and rural constituencies. Around 1.25 lakh names were removed from Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak’s Lucknow Cantonment seat, where he had won by about 39,000 votes. Similarly, nearly 1 lakh names were deleted from Finance Minister Suresh Khanna’s Shahjahanpur seat, where his victory margin was only 9,313 votes. These figures appear to be a warning signal for several ministers in the Yogi Adityanath government. However, they are relatively reassuring for the Chief Minister, as about 33,000 names were deleted from his Gorakhpur Urban seat, where he had won by a margin of over 1 lakh votes. Read this special report Large voter cuts hit ministers’ seats CM Yogi repeatedly expressed concern CM Yogi Adityanath had repeatedly expressed concern regarding SIR. Last year, on December 14, from the platform of the BJP state president election, he had expressed apprehension about nearly three crore voters being reduced in SIR. He had clarified that most of the seats where votes were decreasing belonged to the BJP. CM Yogi had also given this information to the then BJP president JP Nadda during his Lucknow visit. In the coordination meeting of the RSS, BJP, and the government, the CM had also stated that 80,000 to 3 lakh votes could be reduced in the constituencies of 70 BJP MLAs. Urban-rural myth broken During the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) by the Election Commission of India in Uttar Pradesh, it was initially expected that more voter deletions would occur in urban areas, as many rural-origin voters living in cities were believed to be shifting their names back to village voter lists. However, the final data shows significant deletions from rural Assembly seats as well. District-wise figures indicate that Bundelkhand recorded comparatively lower reductions, with 8.86% deletions in Banda, 8.55% in Mahoba, 6.88% in Hamirpur, and 6.66% in Lalitpur. What do political experts say? BJP faces strategy shift after SIR Senior journalist Ratan Mani Lal says the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) data is worrying for the Bharatiya Janata Party, as maximum voter deletions occurred in Assembly seats held by BJP MLAs and also in Lok Sabha constituencies represented by BJP MPs. Meanwhile, SP-influenced and Muslim-majority seats saw fewer deletions than expected, which is why the opposition in Uttar Pradesh did not strongly react after the final list was released. Drop in Hindu voters noted Senior journalist Virendranath Bhatt said the number of Hindu voters has declined significantly, including in constituencies of ministers and BJP MLAs. However, voters whose names were removed can still reapply through Form 6 to restore them in the electoral roll. Lucknow leads in gender ratio In terms of gender ratio, all five Assembly seats of Lucknow lead the state. Across UP, there are 834 female voters per 1,000 male voters. The ratios are 975 in Lucknow East, 952 in Lucknow Cantonment, 950 in Lucknow Central, 934 in Lucknow North, and 923 in Lucknow West.

stories.title: Chandrashekhar Azad’s ex-girlfriend joins Akhilesh Yadav:Plans 200 meetings in UP; agreement reached with SP on 6 issues
stories.summary: Dr. Rohini Ghawari, former girlfriend of Chandrashekhar Azad, chief of the Bhim Army and Nagina MP, is set to become active in Uttar Pradesh politics. In a conversation with Dainik Bhaskar, she said she has already spoken with Akhilesh Yadav. She will return from Switzerland in June and plans to mobilise non-Jatav Dalits, especially the Valmiki and Pasi communities, in support of the Samajwadi Party. She will hold around 200 meetings across the state, followed by a major rally in Agra or Lucknow with Akhilesh Yadav as the chief guest. Will Rohini's political entry be a setback for Chandrashekhar's politics, or will Akhilesh Yadav get a new Dalit face? Read this report How did speculations about Rohini's entry into politics begin? Post on social media X, 'Big Brother' has called Dr. Rohini Ghawari works in Switzerland. On April 8, she wrote on social media X- ‘Come, the call has come, Big Brother has called from Uttar Pradesh. 200 meetings will start from next month. All of you get ready, your sister will be with you with new energy.’ Bhaskar spoke to Rohini about this post. She said, On April 7, I spoke with Akhilesh ji. My first question to him was whether he would form an alliance with Chandrashekhar? He clearly said, never. That's why I am supporting SP. Dr. Rohini Ghawari said she is travelling to Italy for three days to meet her supporters and form a team, followed by meetings with contacts in Paris. She will return to India in June and remain active in Uttar Pradesh for a year, making Lucknow her base. She plans to hold around 200 small meetings across the state, reach out to Dalit communities, and publicly present what she calls the “truth” about Chandrashekhar Azad and his so-called Dalit movement. Rohini pushes non-Jatav Dalit unity 1. Representation demand under PDA formula 2. Outreach to leaders, support claims Rohini-Akhilesh discussed these 6 issues 6. Proper implementation of the SC/ST Act. Answers to the 2 most important questions 1. Rohini campaign may hit Chandrashekhar’s base Senior journalist Syed Qasim says Dr Rohini Ghawari has publicly exposed Chandrashekhar Azad, and if she campaigns against him through rallies in Uttar Pradesh before the Assembly elections, she could gain sympathy support and directly affect his politics. Among UP’s 21% Dalit population, about 12% are Jatav and 10% non-Jatav, with non-Jatav voters already divided between the Bharatiya Janata Party and Samajwadi Party. Rohini is expected to further split this base to weaken Chandrashekhar. 2. Rohini may help Akhilesh woo non-Jatav Dalits Senior journalist Ratan Mani Lal says Akhilesh Yadav’s PDA strategy (with D for Dalits) already promotes non-Jatav Dalit leaders, including Dr Ragini Sonkar (Machhlishahr), Awadhesh Pasi (Ayodhya), and Priya Saroj (Jaunpur). However, it remains uncertain whether Jatav voters will shift from the Bahujan Samaj Party and Chandrashekhar to SP in 2027. In 2022, SP gave tickets to Jatav, Pasi, Kori, Dhobi, and Khatik candidates but none to the Valmiki community, pushing many non-Jatav votes toward the BJP after BSP. By promoting Rohini, Akhilesh may attract non-Jatav Dalits and influence 50–70 seats where these communities play a decisive role. Know who Rohini Ghavari is, and the dispute with Chandrashekhar? Dr. Rohini Ghavari is a resident of Indore. Under the Madhya Pradesh government's fellowship scheme, she got an opportunity to study in Switzerland. From there, she completed her PhD and founded an NGO named 'Janpower'. During her studies in Switzerland, Rohini met Chandrashekhar, the founder of Bhim Army. According to Rohini, Chandrashekhar also hid the fact that he was married and physically exploited her by promising marriage. When he became an MP from Nagina, he started to distance himself. Rohini had also filed a complaint against Chandrashekhar with the Women's Commission, but no action was taken. On the other hand, an FIR has been registered against Rohini by Chandrashekhar and his supporters. Rohini has been running a campaign against Chandrashekhar on social media for some time.

stories.title: UP's Vrindavan boat tragedy:Death toll rises to 11, 4 still missing; search continues in Yamuna
stories.summary: At least 11 devotees have died in a boat capsizing incident in Vrindavan, Mathura, while 22 people have been rescued so far. Four persons remain missing. The search operation continued for the second day on Saturday, with around 250 personnel — including Army teams — combing a 14-km stretch of the Yamuna river. One body was recovered near Devaraha Baba Ghat, triggering emotional scenes as a father broke down on seeing his son’s remains. Rescue officials said the river’s strong current could have swept victims far away. They added that bodies may be trapped in silt and sand, and could surface after 24 hours. The incident took place around 3 pm on Friday at Kesi Ghat, about 2 km from the Banke Bihari temple. The boat, carrying 37 devotees, overturned mid-river. Among the dead are seven members of a single family, including a mother-son pair and close relatives. Pictures related to the rescue Boatman detained after 6 hours Police detained the accused boatman, Pappu Nishad, around 9 pm, six hours after the accident. The boat belonged to him. He had boarded the devotees from Jugal Ghat and fled after the incident, but was later taken into custody. Two videos of the incident surface Two videos related to the tragedy have surfaced: Survivor recounts how the accident happened A survivor said the boat was about 50 feet away from the riverbank when the incident occurred. At that time, strong winds of nearly 40 km/h were blowing, causing the boat to lose balance. The boatman reportedly lost control. Passengers warned the boatman that a bridge was approaching and asked him to stop the boat, but he ignored their warnings. The boat narrowly avoided collision twice, but on the third attempt, it hit and overturned. Devotees had arrived for a 4-day pilgrimage The devotees had reached Vrindavan on Friday morning as part of a four-day pilgrimage organised by the Shri Banke Bihari Club of Jagraon in Ludhiana. Around 130 devotees travelled in two buses, including 90 from Jagraon and others from nearby cities. The deceased include Madhur Bahl, his mother Kavita Bahl, uncle Charanjit, aunt Pinky Bahl, aunt Asha Rani, another aunt Anju Gulati, and uncle Rakesh Gulati.

stories.title: 10-foot iron rod pierces youth’s chest in Aligarh:Cut mid-way to fit in ambulance, screamed in pain
stories.summary: A 19-year-old worker was seriously injured in Aligarh after a 10-foot iron rod fell from an under-construction building and pierced through his chest. The incident took place on Monday afternoon in the Mahuakheda police station area. Rod fell from fourth floor during construction work The injured youth, identified as Zakir, is a resident of Jharkhand and was working at a construction site in Ozone City. Around 3 pm, he was standing below the building while cutting iron rods for pillars and lintels. During this time, a long iron rod fell from the fourth floor and pierced through the left side of his chest. Zakir collapsed on the ground, bleeding heavily and screaming in pain. Other workers at the site immediately rushed to help him. Ambulance team cuts rod to shift him Co-workers informed the police and called an ambulance from Pandit Deendayal Upadhyay Joint District Hospital. However, due to the length of the rod stuck in his body, Zakir could not lie down inside the ambulance. To save his life, the ambulance staff used a cutter to shorten the rod at the spot. Around 4 feet of the rod was cut off, but nearly 6 feet still remained lodged inside his chest. He was then placed on a stretcher and taken to hospital. Admitted to JN Medical College, surgery planned Zakir was admitted to Jawaharlal Nehru Medical College in critical condition. Doctors are preparing to perform surgery to remove the remaining portion of the rod. Similar incident in Bulandshahr last month A similar accident was reported on March 22 in Bulandshahr, where a 10-year-old boy was severely injured after an iron rod pierced through his throat while playing at a construction site. Doctors performed a 3.5-hour surgery and successfully saved his life.
