stories.title: Why Noida factory workers turned violent?:Haryana’s 35% wage hike sparks unrest; what UP workers are demanding
stories.summary: The industrial areas of Noida and Greater Noida saw massive unrest on Monday after a workers’ protest turned violent. The protest, which began on April 9, escalated as thousands of factory workers came out on the streets. Workers carried out vandalism and arson in at least 13 locations. Several vehicles, including police vehicles, were set on fire and stones were pelted. The violence also led to a long traffic jam on National Highway-9, leaving commuters stranded for hours. Haryana salary hike sparks anger among UP workers The main reason behind the protest is a recent decision by the Haryana government. On April 9, Haryana increased the minimum wages of factory workers by around 35%, with a notification issued the next day. After this announcement, workers in Noida also began demanding a similar hike, leading to widespread discontent. Big gap in wages between Haryana and Noida There is a significant difference in wages between Haryana and Uttar Pradesh: Haryana: Noida (UP): Daily wages: This gap has become a major trigger for the protest. Five key demands raised by workers Workers say rising inflation and expenses such as LPG cylinders have made survival difficult. They have put forward five main demands: What labour laws say As per labour laws, workers are entitled to: No agreement between administration and industry The administration claimed that a consensus had been reached on workers’ demands. However, industry owners were not ready to accept key issues such as wage hikes, overtime pay, and allowances. Workers had raised these concerns with labour officials months ago, but no concrete action was taken. Timeline: how the situation escalated Heavy security deployed, appeal for peace Security forces, including the Rapid Action Force, have been deployed in several areas to control the situation. stories.title: UP Evening Wrap:Workers’ wage protest turns violent in Noida, police fire tear gas; Asha Bhosle cremated with full state honours more
stories.summary: Bhaskar English brings you the biggest news from Uttar Pradesh and around the world. Here are the top news headlines of the day: 1. Asha Bhosle's funeral held with state honours Singer Asha Bhosle's funeral was held at Shivaji Park in Mumbai on Monday evening. She passed away on Sunday at Breach Candy Hospital in Mumbai at 92. Maharashtra Police gave her a guard of honour and Bollywood singers paid musical tribute with the song 'Abhi Na Jao Chhodkar....'. 2. Noida Police thrash journalist during protest: Bhaskar reporter assaulted; workers dragged, detained Police allegedly lathi-charged journalists during a violent workers’ protest in Noida, injuring Bhaskar reporter Saket Anand. Labourers demanding a pay hike were beaten, dragged into buses and detained. Journalists sought action against the accused officer as unrest spread across multiple factory units. 3. Delhi–Dehradun expressway opens: Asia’s largest wildlife corridor; travel time halves to 3 hours Prime Minister Narendra Modi will inaugurate the Delhi–Dehradun Expressway on April 14. The 212-km project cuts travel time to 3 hours, with 135 km in Uttar Pradesh. Built at ₹12,000 crore, it features Asia’s largest wildlife corridor and an 18-km toll-free stretch. 4. US says, ‘Any vessel in Hormuz blockade ⁠area subject to ⁠interception, ⁠capture’ Trump is reportedly considering resuming limited military strikes in Iran after talks over the weekend in Pakistan failed to bring a lasting end to the war. The Wall Street Journal reports, citing unnamed US officials, that the president is considering strikes in addition to other measures including the blockade on the Strait of Hormuz. 5. Kanpur’s ‘Mini Jamtara’ busted: Jungle offices exposed; cyber fraud run during job leave Police cracked a cyber fraud network across seven Kanpur villages dubbed ‘Mini Jamtara’, arresting 20 accused. Fraudsters used fake SIMs, forged bank accounts and operated from hidden jungle setups, targeting victims nationwide while returning home on leave from regular jobs, officials said. 6. Wedding bus crashes into truck in Hapur: 6 dead, 7 critical; guests trapped after midnight collision Six people died and seven were critically injured after a wedding bus collided head-on with a truck in Hapur. The returning procession from Ghaziabad overturned, trapping passengers inside. Police and locals rescued victims by breaking windows; injured were rushed to hospital. 7. Owaisi says, ‘PM Modi, Mamata are two sides of same coin’ The Union Home Minister Amit Shah on Monday addressed a public gathering at Mayureswar, West Bengal. During the public gathering, Shah warned that “TMC goons should stay home on poll day, else they will be sent to jail after May 4". 8. Reel stunt ends in death: Bike slams divider at 70 kmph; 19-year-old killed, friend critical A reel shoot turned fatal in Ghaziabad as 19-year-old Ikra died after her speeding bike hit a divider near IMS flyover. Her friend, filming from behind, is critical. Both were helmetless and thrown off impact. Police confirmed video evidence has surfaced. 9. Woman falls from hospital’s fourth floor: Dies on spot; family alleges murder, creates chaos A 32-year-old woman died after falling from the fourth floor of a private hospital in Lucknow. Family members created chaos, alleging murder, while hospital authorities claimed suicide. Police have launched a probe into the incident at Prasad Hospital. 10. PM Modi calls women’s reservation 21st century's most important decision, says decades-long wait to end The government will convene a special session of Parliament from April 16 to 18 to move forward on the implementation of the women’s reservation framework. The proposed legislation aims to increase women’s representation in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies.

stories.title: UP’s first heart transplant at SGPGI:40-year-old woman gets new life, 5-hour surgery succeeds, leaders hail milestone
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh marked a major milestone in advanced healthcare as Sanjay Gandhi Postgraduate Institute of Medical Sciences (SGPGI), Lucknow, successfully carried out the state’s first heart transplant. A 40-year-old woman received a new lease of life after the complex procedure. The donor heart was sourced from Dr. Ram Manohar Lohia Institute of Medical Sciences in Delhi and transported to Lucknow within the critical time window. 22-hour effort, 5-hour complex surgery A team of over 20 doctors, led by senior heart surgeon Dr. S.K. Agarwal, worked non-stop for 22 hours to make the transplant possible. The actual surgery lasted nearly five hours and was described as highly complex. Dr. Agarwal, Head of the CVTS Department, said the team received confirmation about the availability of a cadaver heart around 7 pm on Saturday. From that moment, preparations began immediately, culminating in a successful transplant after continuous effort. He added that the institute had been waiting for such a breakthrough for nearly 15 years. Patient stable, shifted off ventilator Post-surgery, the patient’s condition is stable. She has been taken off ventilator support and is currently under close observation in the ICU. Doctors said the coming days will be critical, but initial signs indicate a positive recovery. Top leaders congratulate medical team Uttar Pradesh Governor Anandiben Patel, Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath, and Deputy Chief Minister and Health Minister Brajesh Pathak congratulated the SGPGI team for achieving the historic feat. They termed it a landmark moment for the state’s healthcare system and praised the doctors for their dedication and expertise.

stories.title: CM Yogi warns against unrest in Muzaffarnagar:Announces civic upgrade and jobs push; unveils projects worth ₹951 crore; calls for unity beyond caste
stories.summary: Uttar Pradesh Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath on Monday cautioned against attempts to spread unrest and stressed that development and security should not be politicised. Addressing a public meeting in Muzaffarnagar, he announced that the district will soon get a municipal corporation and highlighted ongoing welfare and employment initiatives. Programme and announcements The Chief Minister arrived at the Police Lines around 1:30 pm, travelled to Ahilyabai Chowk to unveil a statue, and later reached Numaish Ground. He inaugurated and laid foundation stones for 423 projects worth ₹951 crore. A book titled Kaushal Darshan was released, and an employment fair was launched, where around 10,000 youths are expected to receive job opportunities. Key points from the speech Petroleum prices and inflation Yogi Adityanath said global inflation remains high, but India has maintained relative stability in petroleum prices due to central policies. He compared the situation with other countries, stating that India has been able to manage costs more effectively. Warning against unrest He said that attempts to create industrial or social unrest should be avoided, adding that the state government is ensuring security for traders, workers, and women, while also supporting farmers. Workers’ welfare The Chief Minister said the government is committed to ensuring minimum wages for all workers, including sanitation and outsourced staff. He added that efforts are underway to extend health benefits through coordination with insurance companies. Appeal against caste divisions He urged people not to view historical figures through caste identities, stating that national heroes fought for the country, not for caste interests. Development and investment He highlighted infrastructure growth, including the Jewar airport and upcoming film city, and said these projects are creating employment opportunities. He also said Muzaffarnagar is being prepared for Smart City development. Women’s safety and recruitment Yogi Adityanath said women’s participation in policing has increased significantly, from around 10,000 personnel before 2017 to about 44,000 now. He added that increased recruitment has strengthened safety measures. Political presence and remarks RLD chief Jayant Chaudhary shared the stage and spoke about expanding opportunities in jobs and startups. He reiterated confidence in future electoral performance. A demand was also raised by Minister Kapil Dev Agarwal to rename Muzaffarnagar as Laxminagar. Security and arrangements Tight security arrangements were in place, with heavy police deployment, drone surveillance, and monitoring of high-rise buildings. Around 30,000 people attended the event. Incident during entry An awkward situation occurred when RLD MLA Ghulam Mohammad was denied entry at the venue as his name was not on the authorised list. Ahead of the Chief Minister’s arrival, non-vegetarian hotels in select market areas were closed, and the entire route was secured.

stories.title: Gurugram protest turns into arson conspiracy:WhatsApp chats expose petrol bomb plan, 6 held; wage row at centre
stories.summary: A major development has emerged in the April 9 protest over salary hikes at companies in Manesar IMT, Gurugram. Police have arrested six people and said the protest was part of a planned conspiracy to trigger arson and violence. Investigators found evidence that petrol bombs were to be used to set fire to company premises. Screenshots of WhatsApp chats indicating coordination have also been recovered. Accused identified from multiple states The arrested accused have been identified as Akash (Rohtak), Ajit Singh (Jind), Harish Chand (Pauri Garhwal, Uttarakhand), Pintu Kumar Yadav (Madhubani, Bihar), Raju Singh (Udham Singh Nagar, Uttarakhand) and Shyambir (Badaun, Uttar Pradesh). Screenshots of WhatsApp chat… Protest began after wage dispute The protest followed a strike at a Honda plant in Manesar IMT over salary issues. Workers from companies including Kotyam, Munjal Showa and Rico joined the agitation on April 9. Honda workers resumed duty after reaching an agreement, but employees of other companies continued their protest. Over 20 injured in lathi-charge As the protest escalated, workers gathered on roads and refused to disperse despite police appeals. Police used lathi-charge to control the situation, in which more than 20 workers were injured. During the unrest, some protesters set a police motorcycle on fire and pelted stones at vehicles. A case was registered at Manesar police station against unidentified persons for vandalism and damage to government property. Police: outsiders incited workers Gurugram Police spokesperson Sandeep Kumar said the investigation found that outsiders played a key role in inciting workers. Police said the accused were involved in planning vandalism, arson, stone-pelting and assaults on company staff and police personnel. Most accused not linked to companies Police said most of the arrested individuals have no connection with any company in Gurugram. Authorities have urged workers not to be misled by outsiders and to report any attempts to incite unrest.

stories.summary: Lucknow Super Giants (LSG) went down to Gujarat Titans (GT) in an IPL match at Ekana Stadium on Sunday, marking their second consecutive home defeat and drawing a muted response from disappointed fans in Lucknow. Nehra animated on sidelines; fans take swipe with banners Gujarat Titans head coach Ashish Nehra appeared animated during the match, repeatedly stepping out to pass instructions as his bowlers executed their plans. His on-field intensity drew attention from spectators in the stands. In the crowd, some fans held up banners with satirical messages. One read, “No gas at home, sold the cylinder to come watch the match,” drawing reactions from nearby spectators. Sara Tendulkar’s appearance draws attention in stands Among those present in the stands was Sara Tendulkar, whose Lucknowi chikankari outfit caught the eye of many. She was seen interacting with family members, including the wife of LSG all-rounder Arjun Tendulkar, who was dressed in the team’s jersey to show support. Sara was also seen clicking photographs and suggesting poses, while several fans gathered nearby for selfies. Goenka meets players after match After the match, LSG owner Sanjiv Goenka was seen on the field interacting with players. He checked on Princ Yadav’s hand injury and greeted several members of the squad, including brief embraces with some players. See 5 pictures-

stories.title: Showroom, supermart looted in Lucknow:Roof-top entry in sanitary shop, shutter cut in second theft; cash, valuables stolen
stories.summary: Two showrooms were targeted by thieves in separate incidents in Lucknow’s Gudamba and Madiyaon areas late Sunday night. Police have registered cases in both matters and begun a search for the accused. Sanitary store looted through roof in Gudamba Aditya, a resident of Gudamba, runs Awadh Sanitary Store on Kalyanpur Ring Road. He said he closed the shop around 8:30 pm on Sunday. When staff opened it on Monday morning, they found the store ransacked. Cash worth ₹8.54 lakh kept in the office was missing. A bundle of ₹50,000 was found lying on the floor. Costly sanitary items worth around ₹13–14 lakh were also stolen, taking the total loss to nearly ₹22 lakh. The thieves also took away the CCTV DVR and Wi-Fi router. Police said the accused likely entered by placing a ladder from a vacant house at the back and breaking in through the roof. A police team and dog squad inspected the spot. Gudamba SHO Anjani Mishra said a case has been registered and efforts are on to identify the accused. Supermarket targeted in Madiyaon In a separate incident, thieves cut open the shutter of Anmol Supermart in Madiyaon and stole goods around 2 am on the intervening night of Sunday and Monday. Shop owner Dilip Rajput said he learned about the theft when he reached the shop on Monday morning. A case has been filed at Madiyaon police station. Madiyaon SHO Shivanand Mishra said CCTV footage is being scanned to trace the accused.

stories.title: Noida crackdown exposes anti-worker policies:Tear gas fired after 3-day wage protest at factory; Ajay Rai says ₹250–300 hike ‘cheats’ workers
stories.summary: Tension escalated at a factory in Noida after police used batons and fired tear gas to disperse workers protesting for a wage increase. The workers had been holding a peaceful protest for three days. Several workers were reportedly injured in the action. Congress targets state government Ajay Rai, president of the Uttar Pradesh Congress Committee, criticised the incident and blamed the government. He said, “Chief Minister, heavy s do not fill stomachs. Tear gas cannot answer empty stomachs.” Rai alleged that workers were offered only ₹250–300 as a wage increase despite years of work. He said the use of force against workers raising their demands reflects the functioning of the government led by Yogi Adityanath. Workers’ demands According to Rai, the workers were demanding minimum wages, timely salary revisions, and better working conditions and safety. He said these demands were not addressed. Demand for action and compensation Rai said the state government is responsible for the situation. He demanded free treatment for injured workers and action against officials and company management. He also called for fixing a minimum wage of ₹25,000 per month for workers in the state. Congress expresses support Rai said the Congress party stands with the workers and will continue to raise the issue. He added that the incident has led to anger among workers, with many families dependent on the factory affected.

stories.title: Woman falls to death from hospital’s fourth floor in Lucknow:Family storms hospital, creates chaos after incident; kin allege murder
stories.summary: A woman patient died after falling from the fourth floor of a private hospital in Lucknow. Following the incident, her family created a ruckus at the hospital, alleging that she was murdered. The hospital administration, however, stated that the woman died by suicide. The incident occurred on Monday morning at Prasad Hospital in Junabganj under Banthra police station limits. The deceased has been identified as Sita Dixit (32), a resident of Kishunpur Kaudiya in Banthra. Her husband, Abhay Dixit, works as a contractual bus driver with the Roadways department and drives an auto on his days off. Under treatment for mental health issues According to reports, Sita Dixit had been undergoing treatment at the hospital for some time due to mental health issues. She was admitted again on Sunday. She had reached the hospital on her own after her condition worsened. Her husband later joined her, and she was admitted to the general ward on the fourth floor. He stayed with her overnight. Found unconscious on the ground in the morning Around 3 am, her husband reportedly dozed off. During this time, Sita left the room. At about 6 am, she was found lying unconscious on the ground below the ward. She was rushed to the ICU, but doctors declared her condition critical and she later died. After receiving the news, family members reached the hospital and protested. Family questions absence of blood at scene The family alleged foul play and questioned the hospital’s version of suicide. They said CCTV footage showed Sita leaving the ward at around 4 am, and her slippers falling, but her fall was not captured. They also raised doubts over the absence of blood at the spot. “If she fell from the fourth floor, there should have been visible blood marks,” family members said, alleging involvement of hospital staff. Police intervene; complaint filed Police reached the hospital after being informed about the protest and pacified the family. A written complaint was taken against the hospital administration and the principal of Prasad Institute of Medical Sciences. Banthra SHO Rana Rajesh Singh said the woman had been under treatment for mental instability for several days. Action will be taken based on the complaint. ACP Krishnanagar Rajneesh Verma confirmed that a case would be registered and investigated. DCP South Amit Kumar Anand stated that the death occurred due to a fall from the hospital building. Husband recounts last moments The husband said he brought Sita to the hospital on Sunday afternoon. After treatment and shifting to the fourth floor, they had dinner together and went to sleep. She woke up around 2 am, went to the washroom, and returned. “I told her to rest and that we would consult the doctor in the morning and go home after getting medicines,” he said. He added that he fell asleep again around 4 am and was unaware when she left. He also claimed that no security staff alerted him, unlike previous instances. Brother alleges evidence tampering The deceased’s brother, Dheeraj Tiwari, accused the hospital administration of hiding evidence and misleading the family. He claimed the hospital did not inform the police and falsely stated that the husband had refused to do so. He has filed a written complaint seeking an FIR for murder against the hospital chairman Bhagwan Prasad Yadav and the principal. Demand for murder case In his complaint, the brother stated that Sita had recovered and had spoken to him on the phone the previous night. He alleged that she was murdered in collusion with hospital staff and doctors. Police said the case will be investigated based on the written complaint.

stories.title: Reel shoot turns fatal in Ghaziabad:Bike hits divider at 70 kmph; 19-year-old girl dies, friend critical
stories.summary: A 19-year-old woman died after the motorcycle she was riding crashed into a road divider while a video was being filmed in Ghaziabad on Sunday evening, police said. According to officials, the woman was riding at high speed near the IMS College flyover in the Wave City area, while a 20-year-old man seated behind her was recording a video on his mobile phone. The bike reportedly lost balance and hit the divider. The impact threw both riders several feet away. Neither of them was wearing a helmet, police said. Local residents alerted the police, following which both were taken to a nearby hospital. Doctors declared the woman dead on arrival. The deceased has been identified as Ikra (19), and the injured man as Hashim (20). Both were residents of the Pasaunda locality in Ghaziabad. A video showing the woman riding the motorcycle has also surfaced, police added. See 3 pictures... Now read the full details of the case Iqra (19), a resident of Iqbal Colony in Pasaunda, Sahibabad, left her house around 11 am on Saturday, telling her family she was going to the market. When she did not return till late evening, her family began searching for her but could not trace her. Hashim (20), who lives in the same locality, was also missing from home. He had left on his sports bike. Despite concern in both families, no complaint was filed with the police. According to neighbours, the police informed Iqra’s family about the accident on Sunday morning. Police received information at 4 am ACP Wave City Priyashree Pal said the police received information around 4 am on Sunday about a motorcycle crashing into a divider near the IMS College flyover on NH-9. A police team reached the spot and found a young man and woman lying injured. Iqra had suffered severe head and facial injuries, while Hashim had injuries to his leg, waist and shoulder. Both were taken to a private hospital, where Iqra died during treatment. Hashim remains in critical condition and is undergoing treatment. Both were neighbours, man works as a welder Police said both were neighbours, and Hashim works as a welder. Preliminary investigation suggests that Iqra was riding the motorcycle, while Hashim was recording a video from the pillion seat. Neither of them was wearing a helmet, and the bike reportedly went out of control due to high speed. No complaint has been filed so far. Police said further legal action will be taken once a complaint is received. Video of stunt surfaces A video has also surfaced showing Iqra riding a sports bike (R15) at a speed of around 70 kmph, while Hashim records the clip from behind. Both were without helmets and were filming a reel at the time.

stories.title: Vrindavan boat tragedy toll rises to 15:SDM Ritu Sirohi goes on long leave; newlywed Monica, first-time visitor Yash among dead
stories.summary: The death toll in the boat tragedy in Vrindavan has risen to 15 after two more bodies were recovered on the fourth day of the search. The victims have been identified as Monica Tandon and Yash Bhalla, both from Ludhiana. One person, Pankaj Malhotra, is still missing as rescue teams continue an intensive search operation. At the same time, Mant SDM Ritu Sirohi has gone on long leave, and Deepika Mehra has been given charge. Questions were raised over alleged administrative lapses, but the District Magistrate said Sirohi is on leave for personal reasons and her decision is not linked to the accident. Search operation intensified, 200+ personnel deployed The search operation is underway along the Yamuna River with around 200–250 personnel from the Army, NDRF and SDRF involved. The search radius has been expanded from 14 km to 20 km. On Monday morning, two bodies were found—one near Bengali Ghat, about 12 km from the accident site, and another near Devara Baba Ashram. Officials said the bodies surfaced due to swelling in the river. Families have identified both victims. First-time visitor Yash Bhalla among victims Yash Bhalla (22), a resident of Ludhiana, had come to Vrindavan for the first time. He was associated with a Banke Bihari group and played the dholak during religious gatherings. In a video recorded before the accident, Yash is seen playing the dholak and singing bhajans. His family said he had been excited about the trip for nearly a month. His father sells clothes on a roadside stall, his mother is a homemaker, and his elder brother works as an accountant. Monica planned to go abroad, married six months ago Monica Tandon, a resident of Dugri in Ludhiana, had been married just six months ago. She had travelled to Vrindavan with her mother-in-law Savita. Her husband lives abroad, and she was preparing to join him soon. She was seated in the boat with her neighbour Dinky, whose body was recovered earlier. Her family had reached Vrindavan after the accident and identified her body. Pankaj Malhotra still missing Pankaj Malhotra, a resident of Jalalabad in Fazilka, remains missing. He worked in a private steel company and was the sole earning member of his family. He is survived by his wife and two children—an eight-year-old son and a three-year-old daughter. Family members said they are continuing to search for him and are hoping for his safe return. How the boat capsised The accident occurred on April 10 at around 3 pm when a boat carrying 38 devotees capsised near KC Ghat, about 2 km from the Banke Bihari Temple. A survivor said the boat was about 50 feet from the riverbank when strong winds of around 40 kmph began. The boat started to sway, and the boatman lost control. Passengers warned him that a bridge was approaching and asked him to stop, but he did not listen. The boat narrowly avoided hitting the bridge twice but collided on the third attempt and capsised. Police action and safety measures Police have arrested boatman Pappu Nishad and pontoon bridge contractor Narayan Sharma. After the incident, the administration announced stricter safety rules: Tragedy that unfolded over four days The accident involved a group of devotees from Ludhiana who had travelled to Vrindavan. Initial reports confirmed 10 deaths. Over the next three days, more bodies were recovered as they surfaced in the river, taking the toll to 15. Videos recorded before the incident show devotees singing bhajans and chanting “Radhe-Radhe”, moments before the tragedy struck. Authorities continue the search for the last missing devotee as families wait for closure after one of the deadliest recent river accidents in the region.

stories.title: Inside Kanpur’s ‘Mini Jamtara’ network:Cyber fraudsters set up jungle office; carried out crimes during leave from jobs
stories.summary: Seven villages in Kanpur are currently being referred to as ‘Mini Jamtara’ due to cyber fraud activities. After about three months of field operations, police surrounded the villages and arrested 20 cyber fraudsters who allegedly used SIM cards in others’ names and opened bank accounts with fake documents to target victims across different states. A Dainik Bhaskar team visited Rathigaon, Laxmanpur, Samaj Nagar, Liladas Ka Purwa, Badhail, Pulandar, and Kailashpur, located about 70 km from Kanpur city via Ghatampur, to assess the ground situation. Since the arrests, silence has gripped these villages. In settlements with 1,700–2,000 residents, roads were deserted, and around 80% of the youth were missing. Locals were seen closing doors on spotting strangers, while women and children watched from windows. Read this report What are the 'Mini Jamtara' villages? Jamtara is infamous for cyber fraud, and on similar lines, a cluster of villages in Kanpur has now gained notoriety. Rathigaon, Laxmanpur, Samaj Nagar, Liladas Ka Purwa, Badhail, Pulandar, and Kailashpur are involved in cyber fraud. All these villages lie within a 4–5 km radius, with a combined population of 1,700–2,200. The team first reached Rathigaon in the Reuna area, where police had arrested four accused, Shailendra, Romi, Neeraj, and Gyan Prakash. When their houses were located with the help of children, the doors were found closed. Nearby, a group of mostly elderly people and women was seen sitting, but they dispersed on noticing outsiders, and no youth were visible. Although some houses had open doors and windows, no one was willing to speak. Eventually, the team met the family members of Romi, Shailendra, and Shivkant (a resident of Makhauli). After initially expressing anger, all three agreed to speak on camera. Family members' accounts and those who were arrested? ‘Son is not a fraudster, he works in a mill’ Romi’s mother Siadevi, said her 15-year-old son works in a textile mill in Ahmedabad and had returned to the village a month ago for the wheat harvest. She claimed that on April 6, he had gone out to defecate when police detained him and sent him to jail, insisting that her son is not involved in cyber fraud. Shailendra from the same village has also been apprehended by the police. Shailendra's grandmother, Shanti, says, Our grandson Shailendra works in farming. He had gone to relieve himself. That's when the police caught him. There is nothing in my house. We kept asking the police where they were taking our grandson, but no one told us anything. Seven kilometers away from Rathigaon, we met Indrajeet, a resident of Makhauli. Indrajeet says, My brother Shivkant works as a laborer in Allahabad. Seven days ago, he had come on leave. Our cousin Kaushalya lives in Rathigaon. He had gone with his friend Gyan Prakash to find a harvester to cut wheat at her place. The police took Shivkant along with Gyan Prakash. Know where the fraud den was set up Hidden worksite found in dense trees near village Near Rathigaon, police identified the location where cyber fraudsters operated. Anuj Kumar, SHO of Reuna police station, inspected the site with his team. The area had dense trees, three huts, a stove inside one hut, and hundreds of disposable plates and glasses scattered around. The spot is considered the center of seven villages under police radar and is located about 1 km from the border of Kanpur Dehat district near Musa Nagar. Over 50 boys used to gather here daily A farmer said that for years, more than 50 boys gathered there daily, staying from morning till evening, cooking food and constantly talking on phones while holding papers with phone numbers. After the police raid, it became clear they were involved in cyber fraud. Hidden spot close to road, easy escape route to district border Despite being just a few steps from the road, people passing by had no idea about the activities due to dense tree cover. The group could monitor movement outside and escape through village paths or cross into Kanpur Dehat district within minutes if alerted. 20 arrested, 100+ fraud numbers still active Police have arrested 20 cyber fraudsters, but during a cyber check on April 10, more than 100 fraud-linked numbers were still active. Police are currently searching for 17 absconding accused. Gang active for 5 years, targeted victims via government scheme calls Investigation revealed the gang had been active for about five years, operating in teams of 4–5 members. They called around 100 people daily, luring them with benefits from housing and other government schemes, then transferred calls to senior members posing as officials. The defrauded money was distributed among team members by evening. Members worked outside to avoid suspicion Most gang members worked in mills or outside the state as cover and carried out fraud during leave periods. When complaints were filed, they returned to their jobs outside, telling locals they worked elsewhere to avoid suspicion. Most accused studied only till class 10 Police found that most accused were educated only up to Class 10, while some had studied only till Class 5 or 8. The lure of quick money drew them into cyber fraud.

stories.title: Corpse carrying boats ignore safety norms in Ganga:Mourners travel without life jackets inviting risk; 3,000 boats in Varanasi, but only 1,270 registered
stories.summary: After the boat accident in Vrindavan, strict measures are being enforced across the state regarding boating in the Ganga and other rivers. In this sequence, in Varanasi too, boatmen are being continuously alerted by the water police, municipal corporation, and district administration through advisories. Recently, after a boat accident in Varanasi, life jackets have been made mandatory on all boats. These life jackets must be ISI-marked. Along with this, boatmen are now also carrying divers on board. In this situation, Dainik Bhaskar conducted a ground check of boats passing through Rajghat and those stationed there. The condition of corpse-carrying motorboats operating from Rajghat in Varanasi was also examined, including whether passengers accompanying the bodies were wearing life jackets or not. Read the report… First, understand the condition of boating in the Ganga and the status of boats… According to boatmen in Varanasi, there are around 2,500 to 3,000 boats in the Ganga. Out of these, only a little over a dozen have licenses issued by the municipal corporation. Boatmen, on condition of anonymity, said that the licenses of all boats have expired. None have been renewed in 2026. More than 100 boats operate from Rajghat People start arriving at the Ganga घाट in Kashi for boating even before sunrise. After that, boating begins. At Rajghat, both large and small boats are present. In the afternoon, fewer passengers were seen on boats passing through here. On some boats, people were seen wearing life jackets, while on others, people were travelling without them. Around 100 boats were found anchored along the ghats. Now understand the negligence on boats carrying corpses… NDRF does booking, service is free At Rajghat, the NDRF arranges bookings for boats to carry bodies to Manikarnika and Harishchandra cremation grounds. This service is completely free. However, passengers accompanying the bodies are risking their lives while travelling in these boats. No safety arrangements were visible on these boats. Not a single person was seen wearing a life jacket. There was also no safety tube or tyre on the boat that could help in case of any accident. Boat of Sudhanshu Mehta Foundation Boatmen at the ghat said that these boats are being operated on contract and belong to the Sudhanshu Mehta Foundation. During Dainik Bhaskar’s inspection, a boat carrying a body left in front of the team, where none of the 20 passengers on board were given life jackets. When an attempt was made to speak to the boatmen and those handling bookings, they refused to comment. Know what boatmen said on safety and the Vrindavan incident… According to boatmen operating in Varanasi, all boat operators here are running boats in the Ganga with life jackets and divers. Boats are not being operated without these safety measures. Boatmen said they are ensuring all safety standards while providing boating services to tourists. However, despite this, the municipal corporation is not listening to them. They prioritise tourists’ safety over their own Durga Majhi, president of the Rajghat Majhi community, said that they prioritise tourists’ safety over their own. They keep life jackets, tyre rings, and divers on boats so that any incident can be handled immediately. He said the Vrindavan incident was very unfortunate. In Varanasi, life jackets are strictly followed, unlike there. He alleged that since it was a contract boat, such negligence happened. He demanded that contract-based boats should be stopped not just in Vrindavan but across the state and Varanasi, as such incidents are caused by them but the entire boatmen community faces the consequences. Even the Titanic couldn’t survive, what about a small boat Govind Sahani Neeraj said that they belong to the Majhi community, and when the 882-foot Titanic ship could not survive after collision, then a small boat cannot be expected to withstand such situations. He said the accident happened due to strong winds and collision with a pontoon bridge, but after that, the boatmen community is being criticised. He added that accidents involving large ships and boats happen often, but no one speaks about them. Two types of ISI-mark life jackets are used Govind said that after directions from the municipal corporation and district administration, life jackets are being used on all boats in Varanasi. They were instructed to use ISI-marked life jackets. Two types of life jackets are available—one that supports up to 90 kg and another up to 120 kg. Most boats are equipped with the 120 kg capacity life jackets.

stories.title: Wildlife corridor under Delhi–Dehradun Expressway:135 km stretch in UP; journey time cut from 6 hours to 3 hours
stories.summary: Narendra Modi will inaugurate the Delhi-Dehradun Expressway on April 14. Its key feature is that there will be no toll for the first 18 km. Of the 212-km expressway, about 135 km (64%) passes through Uttar Pradesh, making it equally beneficial for Uttarakhand. Built at a cost of around ₹12,000 crore in about four years, the expressway includes interchanges at key points. Sections passing through forests are fully elevated to allow wildlife movement below and vehicles above. This report explains all major features of the expressway and how it will make travel between Delhi and Dehradun faster and easier. Asia's largest wildlife corridor People use National Highway-58 to travel from Delhi to Dehradun. This route goes from Delhi to Ghaziabad, Meerut, Muzaffarnagar, Roorkee, Haridwar, and then reaches Dehradun. There are about 10 such points on the highway where traffic jams are common. This journey takes 6 to 7 hours. Considering all these difficulties, it was decided in February 2020 to build the Delhi-Dehradun Expressway. However, the project faced opposition due to the forests falling on the route. Later, a solution was also found for that. On December 4, 2021, Narendra Modi laid the foundation stone for the Delhi-Dehradun Expressway. At the time, he said the project would be a model of development with environmental protection, featuring an industrial corridor on one side and Asia’s largest wildlife corridor on the other, ensuring safer movement for wild animals while improving connectivity for people. The expressway’s estimated cost was ₹11,868 crore, and it was initially scheduled for completion by December 2024. No toll for the first 18 kilometers Extra road built where there's a taffic problem On the 212-km Delhi-Dehradun Expressway, 13 underpasses, 5 railway overbridges, and 62 bus shelters with passenger facilities have been built. Emergency lanes are provided at intervals, and there are 16 entry-exit points along the route. For security, cameras are being installed at multiple locations, enabling help to reach accident sites within about 10 minutes. The speed limit is 100 km/h, and high-tech sensors will issue challans for overspeeding. After crossing Saharanpur, the expressway enters Uttarakhand, with Roorkee and Haridwar ahead. Keeping the Haridwar Mahakumbh in mind, a separate 6-lane road of about 50 km has been built from near Halgoa village to Haridwar–Roorkee, so travelers to Haridwar do not depend solely on the expressway and traffic remains jam-free during Kumbh. TOpposition to building road in the forest The distance between Haridwar and Dehradun is about 50 kilometers. To go from here to Dehradun, people take NH-58 or NH-307. This is a hilly route, which used to slow down the speed. It takes about 2 hours to cover the 50-kilometer journey. However, now there is a new option in the form of an expressway. This route passes through Rajaji Tiger Reserve and the Shivalik region. This is why the construction of this expressway was opposed. Environmentalists said that if the road passes through the forest, animals will face problems. Conflict between humans and animals will increase. Also, thousands of trees will have to be cut. This will harm the environment. With these arguments, several petitions were filed in the Supreme Court. In November 2021, the court temporarily halted tree felling and directed the NGT to re-investigate. An expert panel was formed for the investigation. The panel was headed by the DG Forest of the Ministry of Environment. The government and NHAI presented their case before the panel. NHAI said that efforts would be made to minimize tree felling in the construction of the expressway. The corridor would be made completely wildlife-friendly. After hearing the panel's report and the government's side, the Supreme Court had permitted to build the expressway. Entire road in the forest was elevated Animals like tigers, lions, elephants, and deer are found in the Rajaji Tiger Reserve and the Shivalik Hills region. To avoid disturbing wildlife, a 12-km elevated stretch of the Delhi-Dehradun Expressway has been built through the forest, the longest elevated road in a forest anywhere in Asia, allowing vehicles to pass without affecting animal movement. The elevated section includes yellow lighting (instead of white) to guide animals at night and special noise-blocking walls. It is India’s first expressway with such extensive wildlife-protection features during construction. What's special about the Wildlife Corridor? 1. 12 km Elevated Section- An approximately 12-kilometer-long elevated corridor has been built between Ganeshpur (Haridwar) and Asharodi (Dehradun). Vehicles will move above it and animals below it without interruption. 2. Free Movement for Elephants- The entire corridor has been kept at a height of 6 to 7 meters, so that tall animals like elephants can also pass comfortably. Its design has been prepared keeping in mind the traditional migration route of elephants. 3. Noise Barrier and Light Control- Noise barriers and light control systems have been installed in the corridor to prevent vehicle noise and bright lights. About the toll

stories.title: Woman kills mother-in-law by feeding poisoned 'roti':Planned husband’s murder too; had affair with nephew who returned from Iraq
stories.summary: A shocking revelation has emerged in the murder case of 65-year-old Shanti Devi in Lucknow. Police said her daughter-in-law, Shalini (26), mixed poison in her roti, after which Shanti Devi’s condition worsened, and she died within 24 hours. Suspicion raised by the son led to strict questioning, during which Shalini confessed to the crime. During interrogation, Shalini admitted she had an affair with her nephew Karan (24). Her mother-in-law opposed the relationship and prevented them from meeting, which led Shalini to attempt to kill her 10 days earlier by mixing pesticide in tea. However, Shanti Devi did not drink the entire tea and survived. Later, on April 5, Shalini mixed pesticide in flour and made roti, which proved fatal. She said she procured pesticide from her minor cousin-nephew, a friend of Karan, who lives opposite her house. Since Shanti Devi’s death, Karan has been absconding, and police are searching for him. The body was exhumed from the grave, and the viscera were collected from the intestines for investigation. The case is from Ibrahimganj village under the Kakori police station area. The report also examines whether the husband knew about the meetings between Shalini and Karan and what steps he took, if any, to stop them. And how did the aunt-nephew love story begin? Full case details Shanti Devi’s son Manoj Rawat (28) had married Shalini four years ago, and the couple had a son within a year of marriage. Everything was normal until Manoj’s nephew Karan, who works in Iraq, returned home in January this year. During his stay at his maternal uncle’s house, he developed an attraction toward his aunt Shalini. They began meeting frequently and talking on the phone, and Karan started visiting the house repeatedly. Since they were relatives, no one initially suspected an affair. Later, Manoj caught Shalini talking on the phone and broke her phone. During this time, a cousin-nephew supported Karan, allowing him to call Shalini from his own phone when Manoj was away. This continued interaction began troubling Shanti Devi, who started objecting and creating obstacles, after which Shalini killed her mother-in-law. Ordeal of the accused's husband Mother's health deteriorated immediately after eating chapati Manoj said, On April 5, mother Shanti Devi said that the roti tasted a bit bitter. After eating one and a half rotis, she started feeling nauseous. She started vomiting. I rushed and brought medicine for vomiting. Even after giving the medicine, the vomiting did not stop. At my sister's insistence, we took her to a doctor in Junabganj. There, the doctor admitted her. He further said, Mother was given an injection. When the pain subsided a little, mother fell asleep. After some time, her condition suddenly worsened again. The doctor immediately called for a car and sent mother to Prasad Hospital, where she passed away on April 6. After this, her body was brought and buried near the house. Wife narrates a different story every time Manoj Rawat said that after his mother was buried, a discussion took place at home on the night of April 6 about the roti given to her. Shalini claimed the leftover roti had been kept outside, but when Manoj checked, he could not find it, which raised suspicion. On April 7, the roti was found wrapped in plastic and hidden inside sand (morang) in the house. When questioned, Shalini tried to mislead him. Manoj then warned her he would get the grave exhumed and a post-mortem conducted unless she told the truth, but she denied knowing anything and told him to proceed with the post-mortem. After this, a village panchayat was called. During the discussion there, a cousin-nephew revealed that Shalini had ordered pesticide twice by paying money. When Shalini was asked about this, she said that the pesticide was ordered to be sent to her grandmother's house. I said that your grandmother's house is only 2 kilometres away from here. I will call her, and everything will be clear. Shalini got nervous. Manoj said, Shalini confessed in front of everyone that she conspired to murder with Karan. People made a video of her confession. A complaint was filed with the police. On April 10, a report was filed against Shalini and her nephew Karan. The police took Shalini into custody. After necessary paperwork, the police exhumed the body from the grave on April 11.

stories.title: Safety norms being violated at UP ghats:Speakers installed on boats, but no life jackets in Vrindavan; overcharging in Prayagraj Ayodhya
stories.summary: After 13 people lost their lives in the Vrindavan boat accident, it became clear that many lives could have been saved if passengers had worn life jackets. The incident also exposed how the boat operations at major religious centers continue to swing between strictness, lax enforcement, and disorder. Dainik Bhaskar team reviewed safety standards in four holy cities, Mathura, Prayagraj, Ayodhya, and Varanasi, to assess what changed after the accident. The team examined whether life jackets are being provided and worn by passengers, how well prescribed safety norms are followed, and how alert the administration is. Situation in Vrindavan Silence on Yamuna river ghats after the accident When our team reached Vrindavan, the impact of the accident was clearly visible on the Yamuna ghats. The river stretch that earlier saw daily tourist movement and heavy boat traffic is now silent, with hundreds of boats docked. Most boatmen have stopped operating voluntarily, though there is no official confirmation of any administrative ban. Boatman said that no one ever asked for life jackets We spoke to boatman Babulal, who said his family has been operating boats for generations, and this is the first such major accident he has witnessed. When asked why life jackets were not kept, he said no one had ever asked earlier, but now they will keep them as the administration is insisting. On why boats remain shut, Babulal said many boatmen were engaged in rescue operations for two days after the accident, and they were emotionally affected, so operations were paused voluntarily. He clarified that the administration has not officially stopped boat operations. Tourists seen sitting in boats At Keshi Ghat, located about 100 meters from the accident site, we saw hundreds of boats docked. Here, some tourists were seen sitting in the docked boats and taking photos. When we took pictures, those people got off the boats. Most of the boats docked here had large speakers installed, but none of them had life jackets. Double-decker made with makeshift arrangements The boat standing at Keshi Ghat had a seating capacity of 25 to 30 passengers. Some boatmen here have made it a double-decker by attaching a ladder with makeshift arrangements. : Corpse carrying boats ignore safety norms in Ganga:Mourners travel without life jackets inviting risk; 3,000 boats in Varanasi, but only 1,270 registered Situation in Prayagraj No life jackets in boats, arbitrary fare collection continues After the Vrindavan accident, safety standards are being followed to some extent in Prayagraj, but overcharging from devotees continues unchecked. The official fare from Qila Ghat to Triveni Sangam is ₹60, yet passengers were seen being charged ₹500–₹1,000 per person, while ₹4,000–₹5,000 was demanded for booking an entire boat. Notably, life jackets were not available on boats. At Qila Ghat, we met Rajendra Singh Gohil from Gujarat. Rajendra Singh said, We are four people who have come from Jamnagar. The boatman asked for 1500 rupees per person to go to Sangam. When I talked to another boatman, he also said he wouldn't take less than 5000. We don't know who to complain to here. There is no board or number written around the ghat to contact the water police. Claim - Life jackets are being strictly enforced In Prayagraj, wearing life jackets on boats was made mandatory since the Mahakumbh. This system was followed in the Magh Mela and is continuously ongoing even now. At the Sangam bank, we observed that all passengers sitting on large boats were being made to wear life jackets. The prescribed number of passengers allowed is also being adhered to. Prayagraj Water Police In-charge Ravindra Nath Gaur says- Life jackets are checked periodically. For this, a diver is made to wear a life jacket and lowered into the river. It is observed whether they are swimming safely or not. Currently, no specific brand has been designated. Monitoring is also done to prevent overloading. Situation in Ayodhya After the Vrindavan boat accident, security has been tightened at the Saryu River ghats in Ayodhya. The Water Police and administration are on high alert to ensure devotees’ safety during boating. Life jackets have been made mandatory, monitoring has increased to prevent overloading, and safety equipment checks are being carried out at every level. The Water Police are also making regular announcements about safety norms and life jackets, with instructions not to carry passengers beyond permitted capacity. Water Police In-charge Rube Pratap Maurya says The safety of devotees is the highest priority. All boat operators have been strictly instructed not to allow any passenger on the boat without a life jacket. Do not take more passengers than the prescribed capacity. Strict action will be taken for violation of rules. Situation in Varanasi Some passengers are traveling without life jackets At the Ganga River ghats, our team boarded a boat where all tourists were given life jackets, but some refused to wear them. Boatmen insisted they were mandatory due to police checking. Some passengers complained that the jackets were not up to standard and had broken buttons, after which they were given replacements. The boat had a capacity of 80 passengers, but left for Namo Ghat with 50 passengers. During the trip, several small motorboats carrying foreign tourists were seen without life jackets, and on some boats, around 50% of passengers were not using them. Life jackets mandatory for everyone Atul Anjan said security arrangements have been tightened for devotees’ safety. Authorities observed that some passengers remove life jackets for photographs, and strict monitoring is underway. Wearing life jackets is mandatory for everyone, and warning boards have been installed at deep-water points. Three monitoring teams are continuously patrolling the river, action will be taken against rule-violating boatmen, and 3 km barricading will be installed for traffic control.

stories.title: Violent protest in Noida, vandalism in 350 factories:Cars torched outside showroom, 150 vehicles damaged; Yogi forms high-level committee
stories.summary: Factory workers protesting for a pay rise in Noida turned violent on Monday morning. Workers vandalised more than 50 factories across different areas. Over 150 vehicles were damaged and around 50 were set on fire. Hundreds of workers, carrying sticks, marched in groups and said they would not stop until their demands were met. The protest has no single leader or face. Workers are demonstrating in small groups. Meanwhile, the Yogi government has formed a high-level committee to investigate the incident. The situation first worsened in the Phase-2 area. Workers became aggressive after their grievances were not heard. They began stone pelting and set several vehicles and buses on fire. When police tried to stop them, their vehicle was overturned. As tensions rose, forces from multiple police stations reached the spot. Workers pelted stones at them as well. Police then used tear gas shells and barricaded all routes. After Phase-2, the protest gradually spread to around 10 industrial areas in Noida and nearby districts. Workers vandalised over 30 factories and offices in Sector 57. Companies were surrounded in Sectors 40 and 60. In Sector 85, the gate of the Dixon company was broken. Roads were blocked in Sectors 1, 15, 62 and near the DND flyover. To control the situation, RAF and PAC have been deployed in some areas. DGP Rajeev Krishna and ADG (Law and Order) Amitabh Yash are monitoring the situation from the control room. The DGP said strict action will be taken against those spreading rumours. Chief Minister Yogi, during an event in Muzaffarnagar, appealed to workers to stay cautious of those trying to create unrest. See pictures of the violent protest- Noida DM Medha Rupam urged people not to pay attention to rumours. She stated that key decisions were taken in meetings with companies, including forming workplace sexual harassment prevention committees headed by women, installing complaint boxes, ensuring respectful treatment of workers, and mandating full salary payments by the 10th of each month along with salary slips.

stories.title: Higher voter reduction on BJP-held constituencies:33,000 names deleted from Yogi’s seat, and 41,000 from the LoP's constituency
stories.summary: The final voter list released after the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) has validated the apprehensions expressed by Yogi Adityanath. In Uttar Pradesh, voter reduction has been higher on seats held by BJP and its allies compared to SP, and this trend is visible across both urban and rural assembly seats. Yogi had raised this concern during coordination meetings of the state BJP organisation, government, and RSS, urging workers to overcome their indifference toward SIR. He warned that if this booth-level challenge is not addressed now, preparations for the assembly elections will remain incomplete. The key question now is whether BJP will need to rework its electoral strategy, especially on high-profile seats like those of Yogi, Raghuraj Pratap Singh, and Brajesh Pathak. Impact of SIR on UP’s 403 seats Out of 403 assembly seats, BJP currently holds 257, SP 102, Apna Dal 13, RLD 9, SBSP 6, Nishad Party 5, Jansatta Dal Loktantrik and Congress 2 each, and BSP 1 seat. After SIR, 2.04 crore voters were removed statewide, averaging 13.24% reduction per seat. However, cuts were higher on BJP-held seats than SP-held seats. Among 102 urban seats, SP had won 19 in 2022, where 26,000–1.07 lakh voters were reduced. On NDA’s 83 seats, reductions ranged between 26,000 and 3.16 lakh voters. Among 301 rural seats, SP had won 92 seats with reductions of 16,000–79,000 voters, while BJP’s 176 seats saw cuts of 15,000–1.42 lakh voters. Vote reductions on allied party seats included: Senior journalist Hemant Tiwari said, Victory margins in 2022 were much lower than in 2017, and BJP won over 60 seats by margins below 10,000 votes, making voter reduction significant. Changes in high-profile seats after SIR Fewest votes removed from CM Yogi’s seat Among the 102 urban seats in the state, Amroha recorded the lowest numerical reduction (26,223 voters / 8.32%). In 2022, the seat was won by SP’s Mehboob Ali with a margin of 71,000 votes. In percentage terms, the lowest reduction was on Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath’s Gorakhpur City seat, where only 6.88% (33,094 voters) were removed. He had won this seat by 1.03 lakh votes. 8,000 more votes cut on Mahana’s seat than his victory margin Similar situation on Raja Bhaiya and Mata Prasad’s seats Impact on the top urban and rural seats Most votes cut in Sahibabad (urban) Among urban seats, BJP holds the top-10 seats with the highest voter reductions. Sahibabad recorded the highest cut (about 3.16 lakh voters). BJP’s Sunil Sharma had won this seat by 2.12 lakh votes. On Lucknow North, Neeraj Bora had won by over 33,000 votes, but 1.54 lakh voters were removed. On Lucknow Cantt, Deputy CM Brajesh Pathak’s seat saw 1.24 lakh voters reduced, against a 39,000-vote margin. On seven other seats too, voter cuts exceeded earlier victory margins, which could affect win-loss equations in 2027. Lowest vote reduction in Barkheda (rural) Among rural seats, Barkheda recorded the lowest reduction (15,000 voters). BJP MLA Jayadrath had won here by 81,000 votes. On Tindwari, BJP’s Ramkesh Nishad saw around 16,000 voters reduced, against his 28,000-vote victory margin. On Kundarki, 19,000 voters were removed. In 2022, SP’s Ziaur Rahman had won the seat by 43,000 votes, but in the subsequent by-election after he became an MP, BJP’s Ramveer Singh won by 1.74 lakh votes. Around 60% of the constituency’s population is Muslim.

stories.summary: In Hapur, UP, a bus full of wedding guests and a truck collided head-on at 1:30 AM on Sunday. Six people died on the spot in the accident, while 7 were seriously injured. The wedding procession had gone from Dasna, Ghaziabad, to Gulawathi, Bulandshahr. The collision was so severe that the bus overturned. The wedding guests were trapped inside. There was a lot of screaming and shouting. Police, who had been informed, carried out a rescue operation with the help of passersby. People were pulled out by breaking the bus windows. The injured were taken to the hospital. The accident occurred on the Dhaulana-Gulawathi road while the wedding procession was returning. Upon receiving information about the incident, the administrative team also reached the spot. District Magistrate Abhishek Pandey, Superintendent of Police Kunwar Gyananjay Singh, and Chief Medical Officer Dr. Ved Kumar inspected the accident site. They also visited the hospital to inquire about the condition of the injured. SP Gyananjay Singh said- A bus full of passengers returning from a wedding ceremony and a truck collided head-on. The accident occurred due to high speed and darkness. Police teams immediately reached the spot. Relief and rescue operations were started. The injured have been sent to the hospital. Traffic was disrupted for some time after the accident. Pictures of the accident

stories.title: VIDEO before boat capsized in Vrindavan:Devotees chanting ‘Radhe-Radhe’ and clapping; none were wearing life jackets
stories.summary: A video has emerged from Vrindavan, Mathura, taken 15 minutes before the boat capsized. This video was posted by the devotees in their Banke Bihari member WhatsApp group. All the tourists were clapping and chanting 'Radhe-Radhe'. Everyone looked very happy. There was a higher number of women on the boat. No one was wearing a life jacket. Actually, a private boat carrying 27 tourists from Punjab capsized in the Yamuna River on Friday, around 3 PM. 10 tourists have died by drowning. Among them are 7 women and 3 men. Currently, 5 people are missing and are being searched for. The young man who survived said - he had warned the boatman to slow down, but he didn't listen The young man who survived the accident said - About 25-27 people were cruising in a boat on the Yamuna river. Everyone was chanting. The boatman was driving the boat at high speed. We warned the boatman 2 to 3 times. We told him to drive the boat slowly. At that time, the wind was blowing strong, and our boat in the middle of the river collided with the pontoon bridge. The collision was so severe that the boat lost its balance and capsized in no time. We all fell into the water. There was a lot of screaming. We were asking for divers to be called. But no help came. The ambulance was also not arriving. After this, other boats present and local people came and started rescuing us. Our whole family and relatives were together. So far, many people have been safely rescued, but some people are still missing or in the hospital. The administration is responsible for the accident. We demand that the boatmen should be apprehended. The situation was very terrifying; we couldn't understand what happened in the blink of an eye. What other devotees said A group of 120 people came from Punjab: A woman said - A group of more than 120 people had come from Punjab. The boat capsized. Many people have drowned. Some people have been rescued. The boatman was asked to stop the boat: Tanish Jain of Jagraon, Ludhiana district, was also on board the boat that met with the accident. He said that about 130 people had come to visit Vrindavan by two buses. All are staying near Fogla Ashram in Vrindavan. Collision on the third attempt, diver rescued: He said that when our boat reached near the pontoon bridge, we told the boatman that the bridge was coming, stop it. But he did not stop. The boat narrowly avoided collision twice. On the third attempt, it collided. There were some divers nearby who rescued us. Now know how the accident happened On Friday afternoon at 2:30 PM, devotees set out on a boat to tour the Yamuna. The Pipa bridge is only 400 meters away from KC Ghat. At that time, the wind was also quite strong. At 2:45 PM, the boat started swaying due to the wind. Suddenly, it collided with the Pipa bridge. Then the boat completely submerged in the Yamuna. All the people on board the boat drowned. Divers present at the scene launched a rescue operation. After this, the police arrived at the scene. 10 people have died. 5 people are still missing. The boat has also not been found. The Army, NDRF, DM, SP, DIG are present at the scene. Locals said - boatmen seat people arbitrarily, Local Lala Pehalwan said - there have been many arguments with the administration and boatmen. We people say that they seat 25-25, 30-30 people in the boat. There is no rule, no life jacket. Anyway, whatever it is, the accident has become very big. Whatever work the administration is doing, we want to tell the administration that in the future, they will have to make a plan by consulting local people and the Teerth Purohit Brajwasi Panda Sabha. Outside boatmen have also come here. Aunts, nieces, uncles, paternal aunts... all of them are coming and operating boats, which is wrong. Overloading is the cause of the accident Overloading is the cause of the accident. And they say some rope got stuck in this bridge. Operating a boat means Yamuna Vihar, our Thakur ji had done Yamuna Vihar. So, operating a boat doesn't just mean roaming around, it doesn't mean playing songs. We request the administration to set a rule that there should not be more than 8 people, life jackets should be available, and a fixed fare should be charged. What happens is that they set a fare of 100-200 rupees, they feel like quickly taking them around and dropping them off to pick up new people. Small children and novice people are operating boats - Councilor Ghanshyam Chaudhary, a Congress councilor from Vrindavan, said - Overloading has been a major reason for the boat capsizing in the Yamuna Ji. We had warned the administration and the boatmen many times not to seat more people than the capacity in the boats, but no one paid attention. Absolutely not. Neither did anyone have a life jacket, nor any other means of rescue. Boat operators also do not follow the rules. Even small children and novice people are operating boats, who have no idea about the depth and current of the water. Our demand from the administration is that strict rules should be made for the operation of boats. Life jackets should be made mandatory, heavy fines should be imposed for overloading, and only experienced sailors should be licensed to prevent such accidents in the future.

stories.title: ‘Yaksh’ app sharpens smart policing:Reveals shocking truth in robbery and kidnapping, saves elderly man from false case
stories.summary: The 'Yaksha' app is providing significant help in police action against criminals in Uttar Pradesh. In just 90 days, more than a dozen serious cases have been solved. This app provided quick assistance to the police in cases like kidnapping, murder, robbery, and theft. It brought out surprising truths in robbery-kidnapping cases. It saved an elderly person from a false case. Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath had launched this app during the 'Police Manthan' program. Robbery solved in a few hours, a surprising truth in the kidnapping case According to DGP Rajiv Krishna, the Yaksha app includes a complete digital database of criminals, CCTV camera locations, and advanced analytical tools. Where earlier police had to search old registers, now the complete history comes up in minutes. The app made a big revelation in a kidnapping case in Hardoi. The investigation revealed that the person whose kidnapping was reported had been in jail for two and a half years. The robbery of a Jan Seva Kendra operator in Jaunpur on March 11, 2026, was solved within a few hours. Police scanned more than 40 CCTV footages, which helped identify and track the location of the accused. Subsequently, three criminals were arrested in an encounter, and about 1.30 lakh rupees were recovered. Two robbery incidents that occurred within an hour in Kakori, Lucknow, were solved within 48 hours. Police apprehended the accused by analysing their mobile locations and activities. With the help of the same app, an 8-member interstate vehicle theft gang was also busted in Raebareli. Elderly man saved from false accusation The Yaksh app has proven effective not only in catching criminals but also in saving innocent people. In Agra, an elderly man was falsely accused of molestation. Police identified the real culprits through CCTV footage and face recognition and arrested them. The app also played a crucial role in apprehending the murder accused in Bareilly. Similarly, in Meerut, Hathras, Farrukhabad, Kanpur, and Gonda, theft and pickpocketing gangs were exposed with their help. What are the features of the 'Yaksha' app?

stories.title: Woman climbs UP High Court roof with child:Says i will jump, claims no justice; wants divorce from husband
stories.summary: A woman climbed onto the roof of the Lucknow High Court with her child in her arms and threatened to jump. Shouting, she said - I did not get justice. This high-voltage drama continued for about an hour. However, some security personnel showed presence of mind and kept the woman engaged in conversation. As soon as her attention was diverted, a female constable pulled her down from the railing and secured her. This incident occurred on Friday evening around 4 PM at the five-story building located in C-Block of the High Court campus. The woman has been identified as Rupali Sharma, a resident of Gonda. Actually, her divorce case with her husband is ongoing. She had come for mediation for the third time. She had an argument with her husband in court over something, which made her angry. See the first 4 pictures Had a love marriage with a Muslim youth Roopali had a love marriage with Mohammad Sabir about two years ago. The marriage took place without the consent of both their families. After a few days of marriage, fights started between them. During this time, the woman became pregnant. Roopali filed an application for divorce in court. Initially, dates were given for settlement in the lower court. When no solution was found, the matter reached the High Court, where mediation was ongoing. The husband did not attend this. Every time a new date was given. Distressed by this, the woman took this step. CRPF security officer said - The woman was safely brought down with her child CRPF security officer R.K. Tiwari said- The team, acting with prudence, first engaged the woman in conversation and, seeing the right opportunity, safely brought her down. After a rescue operation that lasted about an hour, the woman and her child were safely rescued.

Clearance drive near Sambhal Jama Masjid:8 bigha encroachment to go; 18 houses and shops in graveyard to be demolished
stories.summary: The illegal construction built on the graveyard land adjacent to the Jama Masjid in Sambhal will be demolished. The Civil Court has dismissed its own stay on the administration's action. Now, after the final decision from the Tehsil Court, the administration will take action to remove the illegal construction. This entire dispute is regarding about 8 bighas of graveyard land in the Kotwali area. A complaint was received by the DM regarding this. It stated that stones were pelted at the survey team and police during the Sambhal violence from the roofs of the houses and shops built on this very graveyard land. The administration had measured the land on December 30, 2023. Against this, some people approached the Allahabad High Court, but did not get relief there. The matter was then sent back to the Tehsil Court. After the administration's notice, the encroachers filed a petition in the Civil Court, on which the court had issued a stay. 18 houses-shops are built on 8 bighas of graveyard land Now read the full story in detail Claim of being a graveyard before 1990 On December 12, 2025, Subhash Tyagi (Shri Kalki Sena), while filing a complaint with the District Magistrate, claimed that this entire land was a graveyard before 1990. Later, illegal construction took place on it. He claimed that stones were thrown at the police from the roofs of these illegal houses during the Sambhal violence. Following this, a team comprising the Tehsildar, Naib Tehsildar, and 26 Kanungo-Lekhpals was formed on the orders of the SDM. The land was measured on November 30, 2025. The administration sent notices to the illegal encroachers in this matter. Against this, the occupants filed a petition in the Allahabad High Court in January 2026. On this, the High Court dismissed the petition and advised them to go to the Tehsildar Court. 4 out of 15 encroachers withdrew their petition Out of 18, a total of 15 illegal encroachers, including Salma Rani wife of Shahabuddin, filed a petition in Sambhal Civil Court in January 2026. Three main defendants were named in this, including the Executive Officer of Nagar Palika Parishad Sambhal, the CEO of UP Sunni Central Waqf Board, and the DM and Tehsildar on behalf of the Government of Uttar Pradesh. Out of the 15, four later withdrew their petition. Civil Court Judge Lalit Kumar, on February 27, 2026, ordered to maintain the status quo by staying administrative action until the completion of the case hearing. On March 27, the government lawyers of the Nagar Palika received a copy of the court order. On March 9, DGC Prince Sharma appeared in court and received a copy of the petition. Thereafter, dates were set for March 9, March 16, March 23, March 30, and March 10. On March 16, no cross-examination could take place due to a strike. Lawyer said - Court removed the stay after the truth came out Nalin Jain, the lawyer for the Municipal Council, said - "The disputed site in Mohalla Kot Purvi, Sambhal, was a graveyard next to a religious place. Some people had occupied its land and obtained a stay from the Civil Court by misleading it. I filed a reply on behalf of the municipality and argued the case." Today, the court dismissed the stay after the truth came to light. Now, the stay imposed by the Civil Court on the land of the graveyard where illegal houses are built has been removed. Illegal encroachers had obtained a stay by misleading the court. After the facts were presented by the municipality, there is now no stay in any of the 11 cases that were taken on the cemetery.

stories.title: International cricket stadium to be built in Ghaziabad:Construction on 37 acres at cost of 400 crore; 380-acre aerocity township planned nearby
stories.summary: An International Cricket Stadium and Aerocity Township will be developed in Ghaziabad at an estimated cost of around 2200 crore rupees. This will be Western UP's first international cricket stadium, built across approximately 37 acres. An Aerocity will be established around it, spanning 380 acres. The Aerocity will feature shopping malls, high-tech business hubs, international convention centres, sports academies, and smart residential areas. Preparations are underway for Prime Minister Narendra Modi to lay the foundation stone for both projects. Development of sports, business, and tourism across 417 acres Nand Kishore Kalal, VC of Ghaziabad Development Authority, stated that the two proposed projects in Rajnagar Extension (Morti area) will create an integrated urban hub, where sports, business, tourism, and modern lifestyle will develop simultaneously. Actually, the blueprint for this project was prepared in 2014-15, but it could not progress for a long time. Due to the sluggishness of the previous government, this project remained stalled for years. Now, under the Yogi government, it is being given priority and rapidly moved forward. Stadium to have a seating capacity of 30,000 The Ghaziabad International Cricket Stadium, which will be built at an estimated cost of around 400 crore rupees, will have a capacity of more than 30,000 spectators. It will feature modern facilities such as a media centre and a high-tech lighting system. The construction of this stadium will provide Western Uttar Pradesh with its first opportunity to host major international cricket matches. To become a complete destination for work, living, and entertainment Nand Kishore Kalal, VC of Ghaziabad Development Authority, stated that the Aerocity developing around the stadium will be the biggest highlight of this entire project. It will include large hotels, luxury resorts, modern shopping malls, retail zones, high-tech business hubs, office spaces, and entertainment centres. Being close to the airport, this area will become a major attraction for tourists and investors from India and abroad. Both projects are being developed as a new urban model. It will also include a sports academy, smart residential complexes, green spaces, and outdoor sports facilities, making this area a complete destination for living, working, and entertainment. Employment from the hotel, retail, and service sectors After the proposal is passed by the Ghaziabad Development Authority (GDA) board, it will now be developed on a joint venture model with the UP Cricket Association. All facilities are being designed according to global standards, so that this project can become a major hub for investment and development in the future. Upon completion of this mega project, Ghaziabad and the entire Western Uttar Pradesh will receive significant economic benefits. Large-scale employment opportunities will be created, from construction to the hotel, retail, and service sectors.

stories.title: 10 dead after tourist boat capsizes on Yamuna river:Steamer with over 25 people onboard hits bridge in Mathura: 15 rescued, several missing
stories.summary: A steamer boat carrying around 30 people, including tourists and locals, overturned in the Yamuna River in Vrindavan, Mathura district, on Friday. Ten people have died due to drowning, officials confirmed. Mathura District Magistrate Chandra Prakash Singh confirmed that nine people lost their lives in the incident. More than 10 passengers are still reported missing, raising concerns that the death toll may increase. जनपद मथुरा में नाव पलटने से हुई दुर्घटना में जनहानि अत्यंत दुःखद एवं हृदय विदारक है।मेरी संवेदनाएं शोक संतप्त परिवारों के साथ हैं। संबंधित अधिकारियों को तत्काल मौके पर पहुंचकर बचाव व राहत कार्य संचालित करने और घायलों का समुचित उपचार कराने के निर्देश दिए हैं।प्रभु श्री राम…— Yogi Adityanath (@myogiadityanath) April 10, 2026 Rescue operations underway Police teams rushed to the spot immediately after receiving information about the accident. A rescue operation has been launched, and teams have already recovered one body from the river. The State Disaster Response Force (SDRF) has been called in to assist with the ongoing search and rescue efforts. #WATCH | Uttar Pradesh | A boat accident occured on the Yamuna River near Keshi Ghat in Mathura. According to the Police, 22 individuals have been rescued and shifted to hospitals, but investigation is underway to determine how many of them are safe. Further details awaited. pic.twitter.com/kwzlwF0Kkz— ANI (@ANI) April 10, 2026 Tourists from Punjab According to initial reports, all the passengers onboard the steamer were tourists from Punjab who had come to visit Vrindavan. Authorities are continuing efforts to locate the missing individuals as the rescue operation intensifies.
